covenants.name: Longmist
covenants.notes:
Past magi. Niall of the Younger House (927-1011), founder, who made peace with the druids. Fergus of Merinita (927-1014), founder, who forged the alliance with the Tuatha Dé. Hannewalt on Bar (937-1049), first Tytalus here, from England, with magic for perceiving and crossing boundaries. Marcus Cordo of Flambeau (967-1002), the only Flambeau, killed with his apprentice in the raid. Cearnach of Verditius (978-1064), faerie-blooded smith who wielded the blade that took the pelt, and retired to Verdi once he had trained an apprentice. Astwick of Bonisagus (1027-1070), forced out under suspicion of sharing secrets, who took his works to Durenmar; his lineage is gone. Faventinus of Verditius (1087-1164), who made the Bronze Man, and fell into Final Twilight. Calvacius of Tytalus (1125-1218), Mícheál's parens, who vanished; Conchobor showed it was Final Twilight. Tadhg an Tuir of Verditius (1128-1218), the Cailleach's parens, who died in an aging crisis no magic could lift and lies at Qui Sonant Pro Quieto.

The Offices, for all magi of any rank, rung on the bell by covenfolk since its magic failed: 02:00 rise; 02:15 a reading from the Vitae Magnae, then a nap; 05:00 breakfast with a reading, tokens given back to visitors; dawn, the Parma Magica; 07:00 study, laboratory work or the covenant's business; 15:00 dinner with a reading; dusk, the Parma Magica, tokens collected; 19:00 supper with a reading; 20:00 retirement. The times with dawn and dusk shift, and meals are also given as midmorning, two hours before dusk and three after.

Story seeds. The Dwindling Fish: few and small fish in the withies. Is it overfishing, or new magi upstream looking for a site? What of the vis? A Service for a Service: Ruadan's people demand a deed, from facing a danger underground to bringing the tears of a mother bereft; refuse, and the bargain guarding the cathach is broken. The Missing Cathach: a Lab Text in the library describes the cathach exactly, as if the true one were replaced by an enchantment, and without it the covenant's resources have no protection. The Cattle Raid: Éamonn saw a mechanical bull in a Leinster covenant's herd; do the magi go to Tribunal, or raid? The bronze man looks at one warrior woman: can the Cailleach free him and let the story play out?

Storylines. The Death of the Elders: one will go first, and the survivor's side may turn on the other's. Covenant Governance: win the vacant offices and their votes (Eochaid, Mícheál; Fractured Council, Divided Loyalty). Rebuilding the Covenant: masonry, finances, new craftsmen against the elders' word (Crumbling, Dwindling Resource). Clan Mac Tire: it accepts nothing less than the pelt, so peace needs a new trophy, or there is escalating conflict; Mícheál at the center (Contested Resource). Alliance with the Tuatha Dé: can the magi learn Ruadan's aims and get free, perhaps as he offers an apprentice of his blood or steers research to lift the curse that keeps his people from sunlight? Eochaid and Dara (Faerie Court). Rejoining Hermetic Society: trade, with naivety to exploit; the Cailleach must find a Verditius master, and Conchobor, under Ruadan's sway, opposes (Seclusion, Superiors). Expelling Foreign Magi: a beacon for like-minded magi, driven by Lugh if he publishes; Dara and Mícheál may feel threatened, Eochaid and the Cailleach see chances (Fractured Council, Seclusion).

As a background covenant: others may investigate its silence; Clan Mac Tire may seek allies against it, or Longmist hire help to hunt the Clan across Ulaid and into Connacht; its six votes can be won; Lugh's books may divide the Tribunal; he may secretly trade covenant wealth through Redcaps for new Magic Theory texts. Moved elsewhere, its split could be the Rhine's Harmonists and Wilderists, its isolation the Alps or the Holy Land, and the pelt still an insult.

Themes: isolation, tradition and conflict. The elders suit the storyguide, assigning tasks and keeping the younger magi in line; the four younger magi suit players. Own magi could fill the same roles: a Verditius to rebuild, a tie to Connacht, a Merinita link to the valley's faeries, and a keeper of tradition and future leader.

possessions.name: The Broken Shield of Cú Chulainn
possessions.description: Two halves of a wooden shield with a sharpened iron edge, made for a very large man, shown in the great hall. Once a faerie weapon that gave skill to its bearer; magically mended, it would give a Single Weapon Defense Total as if Ability 10. 10 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Observance Bell
possessions.description: A cracked and tuneless bronze bell, medium size, in the lesser tower's belfry. Its magic died nearly forty years ago, and covenfolk ring it by hand; none knows why, and the magi do not ask. It was opened with 15 pawns and need not be opened again. A shallow dent at the crack's top suggests a hammer. Its effects, whose Lab Texts are in the library: Divine the Heavens' Aspect (InVi 29, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual, The Mysteries Revised Edition p. 51), watching the sun, moon, seasons and year to trigger the rest; Toll the Offices (ReTe 12, 12 a day, Personal, Diameter, Individual); Toll the Phases of the Moon (ReTe 8, 1 a day); Toll the Equinoxes and the Solstices (ReTe 8, 1 a day).

possessions.name: Partholon's Crown
possessions.description: A silver circlet set with diamond, ruby, sapphire and topaz, said to be of the old times, held by generations of Censors, each disenchanting it for the next, and now in Mícheál's wardship. To open it takes at least 20 pawns and Magic Theory 10. Old Lab Texts give effects, which must go in before it is attuned: Aura of Rightful Authority (ReMe 20), Strings of the Unwilling Marionette (ReCo 25), Calm the Motion of the Heart (PeMe 15), Sense the Lingering Magic (InVi 30), Piercing the Faerie Veil (InVi 20), Haunt of the Living Ghost (CrIm 35). The elders would frown on another talisman.

possessions.name: The Warrior Women
possessions.description: Two bronze automata that once opened the main gates on command, now seized and broken.

possessions.name: The Clapper of Saint Patrick's Bell
possessions.description: A relic in the chapel, Faith 4 and Divine Might 40: for 5 of its Might it grants a supplicant the Strong-Willed Virtue for a day. With it Patrick's iron bell knocked the demon Caoranach from the sky. The same clapper is said to lie in the Shrine of the Bell at Armagh, and a Divine relic is there too; that two exist is surely God's work. 55 Build Points.

possessions.name: Tribute from the Underworld
possessions.description: One pawn a season. Under its pact with Longmist the Tuatha Dé lead the covenant to a human body each season, to be dug from its grave, holding a pawn; it lasts while relations are good. 20 Build Points.

possessions.name: From the Very Walls Themselves
possessions.description: One pawn a season, accreting in roof tiles, cobbles and walls of the lesser tower, which are pockmarked by stones taken away and patched in haste. A Dwindling Resource: three pawns after three years, two after five, one after eight, none after ten. 20 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Swine in the Woods
possessions.description: Mushrooms and other fungi in woodland near Longmist. Pigs brought for the purpose sniff them out, and a trained swineherd takes the morsels before they are eaten. 20 Build Points.

possessions.name: Gold Teeth from the Pike Pulled
possessions.description: A fearsome pike comes to the same water each spring to take a wife; a quick, brave fisherman can wrestle it ashore barehanded and pull three gold teeth, a pawn in each. It was once a feast and a contest, and is now a dangerous chore. 15 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Leeward Side
possessions.description: Two pawns a season: lichen on the side of certain trees away from the sun, in woods not far off. 40 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Gifted Blacksmith
possessions.description: Some seasons a piece of very pure iron in Cathal Gobha's forge gives off its own heat: glassy black shards too hot to hold, kept in water, in oil or in the ground. Shard of Iron, CrIg 14, Pen +0, constant, Personal, Sun, Individual, as Heat of the Searing Forge. The text says Creo and the summary table spell-like Ignem. 12 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Needfire
possessions.description: A ritual of the Lebor Feasa Runda: on Beltane night, on land outside the Aegis, a fire of willow, hazel, alder, birch, rowan, yew, elm, oak and ash. A living being passed three times through its smoke has an effect like Cheating the Reaper, Pen +10. Pre-Hermetic: once known it can be lit each year, only in a Magical aura, and the Aegis suppresses it. Unused, the charred staves hold the vis. Some see visions in the smoke, so it may do more. The summary table says Corpus, the text Creo. 30 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Black Root
possessions.description: Each autumn one of Úna's plants, onion or parsley or any other, grows a black root that poisons those around it if left. Lifted, it loses its power and keeps a pawn. Rarely another appears, in autumn or otherwise. A persistent presence means her herbs harm. 5 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Floating Stones of Maghera
possessions.description: Each year a grove five miles north of the Maghera Falls gives a stone little bigger than a fist, held by a long stony root. Broken free, it takes men of combined Strength +5 to move and stays where put, unsupported, holding things aloft (ReTe 14, Pen +0, constant, Personal, Sun, Individual, like The Unseen Porter). Many float lecterns, tables and lanterns about the covenant. Outside lands the Tribunal recognises, so unprotected by the peripheral code. 6 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Hunt
possessions.description: Six pawns of various Arts, Animal and Herbam most often, in the low Magical auras of the hills and valleys of western Ulaid; a magus spends a ten-day distraction across the year finding them. Rarely done now. Outside lands the Tribunal recognises, so unprotected by the peripheral code. 30 Build Points.

possessions.name: Fleas of Saint Nannan
possessions.description: Soil in linen in glass jars, from a Connacht meadow where Saint Nannan swept a village's fleas, which Giraldus Cambrensis describes; no one can stay long there. Each pawn scattered on any ground raises 1000 natural fleas, unaffected by Magic Resistance (ReAn 20, Touch, Momentary, Group). 3 Build Points for each 5 pawns.

possessions.name: Destroy the Fleas of Saint Nannan
possessions.description: Soil in linen in glass jars, from the Connacht village where no flea can live. Each pawn scattered kills animals up to a standard group, of any type, so take care (PeAn 45, Touch, Momentary, Group). 6 Build Points for each 5 pawns.

possessions.name: The Burning Hand
possessions.description: A macabre gift of the Tuatha Dé: a left hand cut from a corpse. A candle between its fingers lights and burns on with magical flame until removed (CrIg 9, constant). 2 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Balm of Tír nan Óg
possessions.description: A faerie gift, five doses left of four pawns each; splitting a dose loses its magic. Applied to a stricken target it holds off age, so that the target overcomes a terminal aging crisis (CrCo 40, Touch, Momentary, Individual). A dose failed Tadhg an Tuir. 20 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Ax of Cú Roí mac Dáire
possessions.description: A faerie weapon in the great hall, too large for an ordinary man, said to be the Ulaidh king's. It is a Pole Ax, but anyone with Brave +3 or more, which replaces its Strength +1 requirement, gains the Heroic Combat pretense and wields it one-handed as at Ability 10. Penetration +10 against the wielder's own Magic Resistance (Realms of Power: Faerie pp. 19, 62). 10 Build Points.

possessions.name: The Fish Runs
possessions.description: Looping channels cut into the banks, set with fish traps, feeding the covenant with a surplus sold at Inniskil. With the toll bridge, a Lesser Income Source of 80 Mythic Pounds.

possessions.name: The Toll Bridge
possessions.description: Held by the grogs. A larger English bridge further south is drawing the traffic, so it may stop paying in five years: from the start of play, take 8 Mythic Pounds a year off earned income. Jealous eyes weigh up its guards.

covenants.summary:
A mist-bound valley in the north of Ulaid, home to faeries of the dark underground, to giants, and to a shut-in covenant whose symbol is a wolf pelt. Two elders hold it between them, one at the top of the tower in the light and air and the other among the cellars and cisterns, and four younger magi live by their rule. No generation stands between them, lost to Twilight or death, and the seat of princeps stands empty. The younger magi might yet steer it between its extremes, or go the way of two generations of feuding.

History. Founded in 927, on land disputed by druids and a Bjornaer wolf with his followers. Unable to beat either alone, the first magi turned to the Tuatha Dé on a bargain of which no record exists, overcame the druids, and held off the Bjornaer for the year it took to found the covenant, with the shield of Cú Chulainn as cathach. For seventy years they entertained magi, faeries and nobles and grew rich. In the Schism War they withdrew to their new inner tower, and the Bjornaer raided them, killing a magus and three apprentices and taking the shield. The Tuatha Dé armed their allies, and in the swift reprisal Ualgrimm the Bjornaer elder died and the shield shattered. At their urging his pelt was taken in its place. Then trade and letters dwindled, until the gates opened only to covenfolk and the odd Redcap, though druids long brought Gifted children here first to trade. In the last century foreign invaders came, and Longmist's call to hound them out was ignored, which it resents still.

Income. The fishery and toll bridge, a Lesser Income Source, earn 80 Mythic Pounds a year against 84.5 spent: buildings 8, consumables 13 (16 less 3), laboratories 44.5, wages 16, weapons and armor 0 (1 less 1), writing materials 3 (7 less 4), tithes 0. Weapons and armor cover the turb and six sets in store. Wealth makes up the shortfall, as it has for years, and anyone looking closely can see it. Lugh's laboratory is the great drain. New income, cuts agreed by Lugh, or craftsmen such as glass-blowers, silversmiths, masons and a master brewer would help, at the price of isolation (Covenants ch. 5).

Wealth. 300 Mythic Pounds, little of it money: tapestries, fine linen, silk, velvet and fur bedding, window glass, silver plate and cutlery from the days of princely guests, all stored away as a distraction. Living Standards +1, as for a Winter covenant; a magus who spends a season putting these things to use makes it +2.

Loyalty. Prevailing Loyalty 0: base -42.5 from the magi's Gifts, offset by the covenant's age; the Turb Captain +5; Living Conditions 0; austerity -1. The total, 4, does not buy a Score of 1. A steward and chamberlain, both unfilled, would help. The covenfolk are few, aging without issue, Warping, and split in loyalty; little is done without a magus's word.

Religion and rule. The magi live an almost ascetic life of set hours, reading the Vitae Magnae, a Hibernian kind of book telling a subject through lives of famous magi, mostly on Area Lore: Hibernia, Code of Hermes or Organization Lore: Order of Hermes. Before the Parma each recites standing, eyes closed and head bowed, touching two fingers of each hand to brow, eyes, ears, nose and lips while naming notable magi of the past, 30 seconds with no effect. Those who had their Gift opened here share a light mist in their sigils.

charter_of_covenant.name: The Rule of Longmist
charter_of_covenant.preamble: Council and offices as the charter gives them, with the rule of conduct the magi keep as tradition. A magus can stall the council by not leaving his laboratory, since all must attend for a quorum and only a quorate council can censure him.

clauses.text: A council may be called at any time. It is quorate only if every magus in residence attends, on pain of censure; a proxy may be appointed, or a magus excused, as for Twilight. Only a quorate session binds.
Each magus has one vote at council on each matter brought before it.
For its help through the covenant's life, the Tuatha Dé hold a seat and vote at council, which do not count toward the quorum.

Offices: Princeps (held by Tadhg an Tuir, now vacant); Castellanus, mundane and magical security within the Aegis (vacant); Cancellarius, the covenant's financial and magical well-being, including accounting for vis and its use on Longevity Rituals (long vacant); Praefectus, security of lands and property beyond the Aegis, including the cathach (Conchobor); Aedilis, planning magical works (long vacant); Censor, leading rituals and upholding the magi's moral standards (Mícheál); Propraetor, relations with outside covenants, nobles and the Church (Lugh).
A magus in an office has one more vote on matters of its responsibility.
An office is filled by a quorate council. Candidates may not vote, and the matter counts as within every office's responsibility, so holders cast a second vote.
A magus who has trained an apprentice is treated as an elder, with more respect, though age gives no power at council.
Every magus has a sanctum; the elder magi must be added to a younger magus's sanctum marker, and refusal invites censure.
All use one code and script for their Lab Texts.
Voting sigils are made by the covenant's blacksmith, so are always metal, the apprentice having some say over which.

Magi dress respectfully: a simple belted woolen robe, the hood down at study and meals and up otherwise. Charms, rings and amulets fit for a magus are allowed; ornament is not, nor arms and armor unless a talisman. Hair is short and shaved at the back and sides; women are exempt but keep theirs covered in public.
No music or singing in the tower; that is for grogs and servants.
All magi in residence eat together at the bell, in silence but for a reading, in strict rotation among all ranks, on magic, the Order or the realms. Refusal may be punished. No food between meals.
Magi attend to their Parma Magica at the bell at dawn and dusk.
Study and laboratory work keep to strict hours; a non-standard routine (Covenants p. 107) or any experimentation needs the council's leave.

Falling short brings private admonishing, the withholding of a meal, exclusion from a gathering, suspension of all communication, or ten days of duty. Records show public certamen with a senior magus in the past, seemingly with vis appointed him; no wayward magus is recorded as winning, and either outcome seems to have bound.

Twenty-eight iron medallions engraved with a wolf's head are worked into the Aegis each year, besides any the magi present. A visitor has one from dawn's Parma to dusk's, and none by night. If visitors outnumber them they go in order: a magus of the Order, a familiar of the Order, a beast of Ireland, a mundane lord, a hedge wizard or druid, an apprentice, a mortal man of Ireland, a foreigner.

covenants.secrets:
Tribute from the Underworld is a sham, unknown to Longmist: the bodies make no vis, it is put there by the Tuatha Dé's magic, perhaps to make the magi party to something unseemly and bind them closer.

Ruadan works against any magus whose doing would take him from the valley or bring others to it; his reasons are unknown.

A tale keen-eyed apprentices may find says the music ban came after a faerie princess entranced the whole covenant by her voice.

Visitors from Normandy are said to have stolen tokens and books many years ago.

covenants.notes: Troupes may detail the Clan as far as they need. It may seek allies against Longmist with a share of the spoils; Longmist may hire others to track it through Ulaid and into Connacht, and an enemy of both could bring a truce.

covenants.summary:
A nomadic line of seven Bjornaer, an unofficial covenant that moves through Hibernia with the seasons, setting up mobile laboratories in booley villages, simple dwellings lived in for a season or two. It seeks those with Magical auras, many on lake islands, some with regiones. It robs other covenants and shelters outlaws. Its founder Ualgrimm was killed and skinned for Longmist's cathach, and its leader Cú Chonnacht Cluasach Mac Tire has vowed to put that right.

Income. Robbery, raiding and hiring out to other magi and covenants; the grogs thieve enough to pay for provisions.

Now. Cú Chonnacht is old and weak, and too many failures to win back the pelt have shaken the clan's faith. His junior Bán wants to strike the pelt's protectors, Prince Ruadan and his subjects, not the pelt. The clan lacks raw magical power, but commands a large band of robbers and mercenaries, enough to challenge the faeries guarding the cathach, and an assault will soon come.
