description.biography:
In truth an ancient man of bent bones, hollow eyes and cheeks and withered fingers; by illusion, healthy, robust and energetic, stern of gaze but pleasant enough. Casting sigil: a misty impression of the spell's target grows from his hands or device and fades within a round. Voting sigil: a silver medallion with a polished moonstone mounted through its middle.

Combat: dodge Init +2, Defense +2; fist Init +2, Attack +1, Defense +2, Damage +1; staff of Lugh Init +2, Attack +1, Defense +2, Damage +1. Soak 0. Encumbrance 0. Longevity Ritual +13.

Sihr is an Accelerated Ability. He knows 10 Names of Power, Arcane Connections to ten airy spirits. Levels of his general spells: Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit 20; Wizard's Communion 20 and 40; Demon's Eternal Oblivion 15; Circular Ward Against Demons 25; Opening the Intangible Tunnel 35. Coerce the Spirit of Anger is from Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 99.

characters.summary: Of the Younger House, atop the greater tower where he watches all that happens, and in his own eyes the rightful leader. He has opposed the coming of continental magi for fifty years, and having lost the argument he stopped going to Tribunal and dropped friends turned enemies, fearing the native Order will be pushed aside as the Fir Bolg, the Tuatha Dé and the druids were. Propraetor: he has the last word on relations outside the covenant and has closed them to all who take a lenient view. A Corrguineach (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 109), he summons spirits as his eyes, ears and agents, some holding Aegis tokens kept in his sanctum. He is the covenant's Corpus specialist and maker of its Longevity Rituals. Vain, he wears youthful illusion.
characters.secrets: He has written polemics for Hibernia to secede and set its own Code, with residency only for magi who can show three generations in Hibernia; none is in the library or yet circulated, though Dara knows of them. He has read in the Lebor Feasa Runda that drinkers of Tobar Segais, on the plain of Mag Mell, on Tir Na nÓg, ruled by the giant Fomórach, live forever. His age is outrunning his ritual, and he may soon send his filius for that water.

characters.name: Conchobor Crosach

invented_spells.name: To See as Others See
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

invented_spells.name: Sense of Faerie Power
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
Hunched and wrinkled, with short patchy white hair and hooded eyes forever watching from their corners. Small horns rise from his head. His left arm looks to be banded bronze, still youthful, and its weight drags that side down. Casting sigil: black mist swirls round his right arm and hand. Voting sigil: a large bronze brooch embossed and patterned round the edges. Twilight scar: his Parma Magica does not shield him from the effects of The Gift.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense -1; fist Init -1, Attack -1, Defense -1, Damage 0; bludgeon Init -2, Attack +1, Defense -1, Damage +2. Soak +2. Encumbrance 1. Longevity Ritual +12.

Strong Goblin Blood gives +1 to stealth totals, and Second Sight came with it. Nature Lore (Underworld) (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 103) covers the tunnels beneath Longmist and the wider valley and what lives in them. To See as Others See is from Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 139; its Art is printed In(Re)An. Opening the Intangible Tunnel at level 30.

characters.summary: He keeps sanctum and laboratory underground among the cellars and cisterns, has not left the covenant in many years, and meets princes and envoys of the Tuatha Dé there in the dark; those ties, he holds, make him Longmist's natural leader. An isolationist whose concern stops at the gates, he shares his allies' enmity for the Fir Bolg and the Fomórach. Demanding and suspicious of his fellows since a Twilight left his Parma no shield against The Gift. Praefectus: nominally the security of the lands outside the Aegis, which he has been stretching over everything that comes from outside, vis sources and stocks included.
characters.secrets: The Tuatha Dé still hold a powerful Arcane Connection to him, a coin Ruadan forged from his pain, since he tried to master them with his glove's first power.

characters.name: Cailleach Dhé Dherg

invented_spells.name: Piercing the Magical Veil
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
Small, well-formed and fair, with green eyes and striking red hair, which goes tied and demurely veiled when she is not feeling rebellious. Casting sigil: a light red mist swirls round the target during the casting or device activation. Voting sigil: a highly polished disk of copper of remarkable clarity and evenness. She carries her Casting Tools.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack +1, Defense 0, Damage 0; knife Init 0, Attack +2, Defense 0, Damage +2. Soak +1. Encumbrance 1. Verditius Magic gives her +4 Shape and Material bonus (her Philosophiae and specialty) to future enchantments. A Visible Demand for Repair is from Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 65; The Crystal Dart is printed Mu(Re)Te.

personality_traits.name: Keen to venture out of the covenant

reputations.name: An ill-omen (elders and covenfolk of Longmist)

characters.summary: Known as the Cailleach to all, and the only maga now at Longmist; her apprenticeship caused much argument, her parens Tadhg an Tuir holding firm against the council though it appealed to House Bonisagus. She is admonished for going with her hair uncovered. She means to learn to repair and wake the bronze man in the courtyard, which is close to past repair, and that will take her outside the walls. These two years she has given to her laboratory, with its great forge, and her talisman; Lugh dislikes the work. In her macgnímartha she was laboratory assistant to an itinerant Verditius called Peter, learning her House's secrets ahead of her Initiations.

links.note: She assisted an itinerant Verditius of this name

characters.name: Dara Connachtach

params.detail: killed a druid while undertaking his macgnímartha

invented_spells.name: Reveal the Lingering Spirit
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
A handsome, very slender, well-proportioned man with thick chestnut hair. The belt of his robe is strung with sticks, rabbit feet, herbs and old wooden spoons, remnants of Arcane Connections to spirits he has met. He carries a satchel of vials and flasks, always ready for samples. Casting sigil: a misty outline of the target forms between caster and target and fades. Voting sigil: an iron disk, thick and roughly beaten.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense -1; fist Init -1, Attack -1, Defense -1, Damage -1; knife Init -1, Attack 0, Defense -1, Damage +1; bludgeon Init -2, Attack +1, Defense -1, Damage +1. Soak 0. Encumbrance 1. Sihr is 8 and +2 from Puissant.

reputations.name: Inexperienced (spirits of Ulaid, druids of Connacht, the Fir Bolg)
Spent time in Connacht (magi of Hibernia)

characters.summary: Of the Younger House, the youngest and last gauntleted, treated as an inexperienced junior though only three years behind the Cailleach. Lugh's former apprentice and a Corrguineach, he summons, bargains with and controls elemental spirits, and has spent time among the druids of Connacht and the Fir Bolg. He respects and fears his parens, but does not share Lugh's view of the Order.
characters.secrets: In his beardless years he travelled with Brea, a man schooled in spirits, and against Brea's advice and out of bravado summoned one he could not control. It attacked them; Dara ran, and the druid died. He has told no one at Longmist. Something unseen meddles with his laboratory, and he fears what it may be.

characters.name: Eochaid Dubh

description.biography:
Pale skin, very black hair and dark eyes, always ready with a smile, though among magi he usually looks apologetically contrite. Casting sigil: mist seeps through the ground round the caster. Voting sigil: a disk of lead and iron with a horseshoe inscribed on the leaden side. He squirrels food scraps into a belt pouch for his magpie, and tries a different would-be talisman each time to see what feels right.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack +2, Defense 0, Damage 0. Soak +1. Encumbrance 0.

characters.summary: Conchobor's former apprentice, an accomplished illusionist who has put off the Merinita Mysteries for Imaginem and is now warming to them. Easily led, weak for music and carousing, he is often made to eat apart for joining the covenfolk's revels. He has no talisman or familiar yet but has readied his laboratory, and risks more punishment smuggling scraps to a magpie that visits him. He drank his way round Hibernia in his macgnímartha, The Gift and the drink putting him in harm's way more than once. He knows the Tuatha Dé but does not trust their motives.

characters.name: Mícheál Amhreaidh

params.detail: when not casting from a circle

description.biography:
Always frowning, in disapproval or deep thought, his hair thin and short, his robes and white tabard spotless. Under them he bears the scars of many bites and gashes. Casting sigil: the target trembles slightly through the casting and sheds a light mist, as shaken stonework sheds dust. Voting sigil: a small gold disk with the impression of a crown punched into it.

Combat: dodge Init -2, Defense 0; knife Init -2, Attack +2, Defense 0, Damage +2; fist Init -2, Attack +2, Defense +1, Damage 0. Soak +3, and a further +3 when Doublet of Impenetrable Silk is cast on his robe. Encumbrance 0.

Artes Liberales and Philosophiae are each 3 and +2 from Puissant. Mystical Choreography is in Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 56. His satchel of prepared props (candles, herbs, auspicious stones, transcripts of the Vitae Magnae) gives +3 to spells cast ceremonially as medium props; it holds props for three spells, chosen before he sets out, or all of them with a packhorse, which the covenant lacks.

His future talisman is Partholon's Crown, kept by the covenant's Censors.

characters.summary: Censor, master of rituals, who leads the communions and answers for the younger magi's conduct. The rest are nominally Christian, but he was taught to venerate the goddess Domnu; he reasons that she is a primal Kosmokrator (Realms of Power: Magic p. 109) subject to a greater power, yet keeps his faith, and his devotion is known across the Tribunal. He hopes to see the old magics of Ireland joined to Magic Theory. In his macgnímartha, among the old pagan sites, the Bjornaer of Clan Mac Tire fell on him; a Fir Bolg war band rescued him gravely wounded, and he has hated all Bjornaer since.

characters.name: Bran in Gai Móir

params.detail: must not suffer a dog in his house

description.biography:
Long-limbed, a head taller than most of the grogs he leads. He has round shield, full chain mail and a horse; the arms and armor were handed down and altered to fit, and by City & Guild's rules the armor has one Damage Level left. He wants new gear for himself and his men (prices in City & Guild p. 144).

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +6; fist Init -1, Attack +7, Defense +7, Damage +1; dagger Init -1, Attack +8, Defense +6, Damage +4; sparra and round shield Init 0, Attack +12, Defense +10, Damage +7; long spear mounted Init +1, Attack +14, Defense +10, Damage +6; long spear Init +2, Attack +9, Defense +7, Damage +8. Soak +9. Encumbrance 4.

Faeborchless, the Dancing Shield Feat (printed among his Virtues before the Minor ones), a Cles learned from Úathach of Leth Cuinn. He throws his shield or weapon to defend as many characters as his Single or Great Weapon Ability, on a Dexterity + that Ability feat check against Ease Factor 9. On success they are defended and it returns to his hands; on failure he must fetch it, and may be left defenseless.

characters.summary: Turb captain, who distrusts Conchobor's allies and so favors Lugh. Trained in the clesa by Úathach of the Tuatha Dé (The Contested Isle). He is married to Ailbhe, eight years younger; they are childless, and he blames an enchantment of the magi. His resentment is growing and he may soon confront them, and they may have to research fertility magic.
characters.secrets: He is under no Longevity Ritual, so their childlessness is not its doing.

characters.name: Éamonn Cruittire

description.biography:
A handsome young man with the Sidhe's refinement in his blood, sparkling blue eyes, bouncy blond hair and an easy smile: every father's nightmare and every husband's fear. Good quality clothes.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense +2; fist Init 0, Attack +3, Defense +3, Damage -1; knife Init 0, Attack +3, Defense +2, Damage +1; bludgeon Init -1, Attack +4, Defense +2, Damage +1. Soak 0. Encumbrance 1.

Enchanting Storytelling works as Enchanting Music with stories. His Dependent is his mother, weak since an illness and likely to lose her home without him.

characters.summary: Éamonn Cruittire mac Aindileas Uí hEódhasa, of the line of Baile Uí Eódhasa, magical bards of the Ulaidh, whose power to enchant through story goes from father to son. He carries tales of old battles and feuds through Ulaid. He values his family's tie to Longmist, finds Conchobor unsettling and distrusts Lugh far more, scorns the magi's staid life and their ban on music, is fond of the villagers, and enjoys his sway over his friend Eochaid.

characters.name: Longmist Grog

description.biography:
The block stands for each of the six grogs under Bran. Dirty, in thick wool against the cold mists, drying their oiled leather shoes by the fire; they look more like brigands than toll collectors. They carry partial leather scale armor patched down to one Damage Level, round shield, sparra, short spear, two throwing axes, eating knife, warm cloak and light camping gear.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense +4; fist Init 0, Attack +6, Defense +5, Damage +2; kick Init -1, Attack +5, Defense +3, Damage +5; knife Init 0, Attack +6, Defense +4, Damage +4; sparra and round shield Init 0, Attack +11, Defense +8, Damage +8; short spear and round shield Init +1, Attack +8, Defense +7, Damage +7; throwing ax Init 0, Attack +8, Defense +5, Damage +8. Soak +8. Encumbrance 1.

No leader among them: they have trained as a group, but fight as an untrained one without their captain. Loyal more from habit than wish, and lazy; they complain of work but are rarely pushed. Poor Living Conditions is -1 Living Conditions Modifier, from days spent living off the land.

characters.summary: The six grogs of the turb, for the most part on the toll bridge, on escort to market, or now and then on guard or seeing off giants.

characters.name: Columb Brathair
characters.summary: The penitent monk, priest and confessor, a fallen priest whose diabolic excesses Calvacius and Tadhg an Tuir found out; he threw himself on their mercy and for reasons unclear they brought him here. Appears 65. Longevity Ritual -4. Communication +1, Teaching (Infernal Lore) 6, Infernal Lore 8, Dominion Lore 8. Teacher, 15 Build Points.

characters.name: Cathal Gobha
characters.summary: The blacksmith, five years under a Longevity Ritual. Warping has made him Offensive to Animals, so he leaves farrier work to his son. His forge is rarely active. Communication +1, Teaching (Blacksmith) 6, Craft: Blacksmith 8. Teacher, 15 Build Points. His workshop, 45 Build Points, has Innovation +3 and Raw Materials +2 (City & Guild p. 65), and makes Superior goods. Blacksmith to the voting sigils, which are always metal.

characters.name: Cináed mac Cathail
characters.summary: Cathal's son and only apprentice, who would rather be a grog, has no love for the English, and hopes Longmist will one day stand against them. Dexterity +3, Craft: Blacksmith 4. 4 Build Points.

characters.name: Úna
characters.summary: The herbwife, who has refused magical help with aging, trusting her own compounds. Intelligence +1, Profession: Herbalist 7, Chirurgy 5. 7 Build Points. Married to the farmer Cormac; villagers bring her their knocks and scrapes.
characters.secrets: For some years she has been cuckolding Cormac with Fearghal.

characters.name: Íomhar
characters.summary: Librarian since old Thomas passed, frustrated to lack his predecessors' rigor, and eager for any way to improve. Intelligence 0, Profession: Librarian 7. 7 Build Points.

characters.name: Maghnus
characters.summary: The scribe, slovenly in person and workshop, but fluent in Latin, Greek, Gaelic, French and German. Dexterity +1, Profession: Scribe 7. 7 Build Points.

characters.name: Piaras
characters.summary: The percamenarius, morose and withdrawn, whose vellum other covenants have sought. Appears 50. Longevity Ritual -4. Dexterity +3, Craft: Parchment 9 (uterine vellum). 9 Build Points, with 45 for his workshop (Innovation +2, Raw Materials +3). Warping has Disfigured his skin to thin white parchment, veins and pulse showing through. His four vernacular manuals on the skins of cows, sheep, goats and magical beasts each add +3 to other parchment makers' Craft Totals (City & Guild p. 73), 12 Build Points.

characters.name: Maol Phóil
characters.summary: Piaras's assistant, as morose, and growing jealous and impatient. Craft: Parchment 5. 5 Build Points.

characters.name: Fearghal
characters.summary: The animal handler, last of the team that served Longmist's kennels and stables when kings hunted here; he tends the rare horse, advises on sick livestock and keeps the bees. Dexterity +2, Animal Handling 7. 7 Build Points.
characters.secrets: He commits adultery with Úna, a sin he forgives himself.

characters.name: Bán Mac Tire
characters.summary: Cú Chonnacht's junior, whose heartbeast is a white wolf, and who grows impatient with the old man. The book gives no stat block.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: The top of the greater tower, enlarged across two floors: work below round a great cauldron, and above a gallery for contemplation, writing, and his personal library and stores. Highly specialized for Longevity Rituals. Upkeep 36 Mythic Pounds a year. Virtues: Greater Feature (Cauldron), Highly Organized, Priceless Ingredients, Spotless, Spacious, Gallery, Elevated, Greater Expansion. Flaws: Greater Focus (Cauldron). Size +0 (0). Marker: none added. 60 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: Cold, dark and deep, a spacious chamber of rocky steps and platforms round a slowly turning orb of granite held over a still clear pool. He claims nothing for the orb, but visitors have glimpsed the world beyond Longmist in it. Within the Aegis, yet a nearby gateway to the Otherworld lets pixies, brownies and other fair folk in to watch, listen and sometimes help unasked. Upkeep 1 Mythic Pound a year. Virtues: Spacious, Faerie Ingredients, Greater Feature (Orb), Lesser Feature (Pool). Flaws: Gateway, Subterranean, Gremlins. Size +0 (0). Marker: none added. 50 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: A forge dominates, the outer walls pierced by iron hollows and chimneys, its bellows reverberating as the fire reaches magically high heats. Cathal Gobha makes and keeps up her superior tools, so they add no Upkeep. Upkeep 1 Mythic Pound a year. Virtues: Greater Feature (Forge), Highly Organized, Superior Tools. Flaws: Greater Focus (Forge). Size +0 (-2). Marker: Conchobor Crosach, Lugh-éccnaid. 20 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: Dominated by a summoning circle built into a raised circular dais, the equipment lining the walls. Upkeep 1 Mythic Pound a year. Virtues: Greater Feature (Summoning Circle). Flaws: Greater Focus (Summoning Circle), Haunted. Size +0 (0). Marker: Conchobor Crosach, Lugh-éccnaid. 20 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: Stark brilliant white, walls plastered smooth and painted the most unnatural white to be had. A near floor-to-ceiling round window in the curved outer wall is reflected in hand-sized mirrors along the inner one, each at its own angle or depth. Scores of candles light it (he has promised something cheaper), and equipment is kept from the walls, which makes it awkward. Upkeep 3 Mythic Pounds a year. Virtues: Greater Feature (Mirror), Lesser Feature (Window), Excessive Lighting, Highly Organized. Flaws: Greater Focus (Mirror), Awkward Shape. Size +0 (0). Marker: Conchobor Crosach, Lugh-éccnaid. 40 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: A year's enhancement: two seasons' refinement, then a pentagon's Auspicious Shape and a Summoning Circle engraved in the floor. He means to add an Antechamber and a Balcony. Upkeep 1 Mythic Pound a year. Virtues: Auspicious Shape, Highly Organized, Lesser Feature (Summoning Circle). Size +0 (0). Marker: Conchobor Crosach, Lugh-éccnaid. 20 Build Points.

rooms.name: The greater tower
rooms.description: Once a former member's; the valuable equipment has been reused and what remains is decaying. Upkeep half a Mythic Pound a year. Size +0 (-1). Flaws: Missing Equipment, Decaying, Missing Sanctum Marker. Impossible: Enchanting Items. The three cost 150 Build Points.

rooms.description: Once a former member's; the valuable equipment has been reused and what remains is decaying. Upkeep half a Mythic Pound a year. Size +0 (-1). Flaws: Missing Equipment, Decaying, Missing Sanctum Marker. Impossible: Enchanting Items. The three cost 150 Build Points.

rooms.name: A booley
rooms.description: Each of the seven has one like it, packed for carriage by servants and soldiers, and doubling as his living quarters, of which the younger magi often complain. Size +0 (0). Virtues: Lesser Feature (cauldron), Living Quarters, Mobile, Specimens, Servant (Intelligence +2, a learned clerk, loyal from fear). Flaws: Hovel. Marker: none added.

books.description:
By an ancient High King, translating works from before Christ: objects of virtue, rituals that yield vis, and powerful bonuses from the sixteen characters of the Boibel Loth. No magus has yet brought these into Hermetic magic. A most valued possession.

Boibel Loth. Sixteen characters whose inscribed forms give Shape and Material bonuses, in rituals to the casting total, and as distinct Charms in Charm Magic (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 96). A minor breakthrough (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 26) is needed first. Boibel (B) +5 inception, +3 sun; Loth (L) +5 fire; Forann (F) +5 spring; Salia (S) +5 moon, +3 witches; Neiagadon (N) +5 water; Daibhaith (D) +5 door, +3 travel or passage; Teilmon (T) +5 growth, +3 gain; Cailep (C) +5 women; Moiria (M) +5 autumn; Gath (G) +5 balance and even-handedness; Riuben (R) +5 winter, +3 decay; Acab (A) +5 birth, +3 new life; Ose (O) +5 youth, +3 initiation; Ura (U) +5 maturity, +3 consummation; Esu (E) +5 aging and old age; Jaichim (I) +5 death.

powers.description: Variable points, Init Qik - twice the points. Crafts faerie arms and armor of strange stuff such as moonlight, song, loss, anger or a storm's power, for 1 point of Might Score and up to 9 more to enchant up to 45 levels, one effect under the usual modifiers. Those points return only by consuming faerie Vim vis or smelting the weapon back.

powers.description: For each Might point spent, +3 to one person's totals for making weapons and armor, the points regained only when it is withdrawn. Must penetrate when given.

creatures.equipment: Armor forged from tempered night (Protection +14), a long slender sword of purest moonlight, and a dagger poisoned with loss.
creatures.appearance: A tall, handsome man seemingly in his early thirties, attractive but for bright blue skin and red eyes, with lustrous blond hair and oil-black armor that fascinates in torchlight.
creatures.notes:
A prince and druid of the Tuatha Dé, descended from Goibhniu the smith, whose craft he has, though his counsel serves the covenant more than his magic. He mediates with the faerie world, his soldiers guard the cathach, and the charter gives him a seat at council, where his chief ally is Conchobor. He always counsels keeping the valley shut.

Might +10 in his place of power, the labyrinth beneath Longmist, where his forge's exotic supplies and magical fires add +2 to make Superior arms and armor, and Excellent swords (City & Guild p. 69). His combat figures assume his faerie weapons; the abilities are pretenses, and Faerie Weapons covers all faerie-made or -touched weapons, mortal ones being no better than bludgeons in his hands. The great sword and knife need his training, and then give +5 to attack. Wounds: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Vis: 8 pawns of Rego, +2 in the Otherworld.

Great Sword of the Moon: MuCo 45, Pen +20, unlimited, Sight, Concentration, Group: those who count themselves his allies see it glow and can see in darkness as under a full moon. The Knife of Sorrows: CrMe 45, Pen +50, 1 a day, Touch, Moon, Individual: poisons the mind with loss for a Moon; each day a Personality roll against Ease Factor 9 holds it off, failure bringing -3 to all totals.
creatures.secrets: He may only now be ready to act on a plan of centuries for Longmist.

creatures.appearance: A bare-chested bearded craftsman in bronze, larger than life and classical of face, though the complex joints betray him.
creatures.notes:
An automaton of Faventinus of Verditius, the Cailleach's grand-parens, who used it at the forge until something made him send it into the courtyard for good; most now take it for a statue. Mute, it has seen and heard everything in the courtyard for 80 years. Opened with 17 pawns, 14 used, room for up to 30 levels more. Its powers are constant, and it can suspend them on command. 48 Build Points.

Its Might is damaged: effective Might 6, -5 to any Ability roll. Repair needs the Verditius Automata Inner Mystery (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 128); investigating its powers is a standard laboratory action, and reveals the command words. Working, it follows instructions of any complexity about its smithing, and any others needing neither positive Intelligence nor an Ability but Craft: Blacksmith. Soak +25 applies to Damage Checks, with 4 Damage Levels (City & Guild p. 77).

treaties.title: The Treaty of Cnoc Maol Réidh
treaties.parties: The Order of Hermes in Hibernia and the Coill Trí
treaties.witness: Negotiated by Fedelmid Ua Heirméais of Mercere
treaties.ends: Never by one party alone; a clause is added when a Tribunal votes it and every ceannaire agrees
treaties.terms:
Made after High-King Congalach Cnogba's embassy of 844, brought by the Chief Bard Cormacan, on behalf of hedge wizards harried by the Order; signed in 851 once the Diedne had withdrawn, refused by the Diedne, rejected by the Grand Tribunal of 865, and made binding at Hibernia's first meeting in 898. It is named for Connacht's highest mountain, and its terms apply 'between druids and magi', not to lesser hedge wizards. Druids can change it only through a magus who proposes it for them.

1. The Order founds no covenant in Connacht, and no magus spends more than three nights running under a Connacht sky or roof.
2. The Coill Trí give the Order seven Gifted children at each Tribunal.
3. The Coill Trí have the right to be heard at Tribunal, their grievances are considered, and the Order does not deny them justice.
4. The Coill Trí are masters of their own places; the Order is master of all others.
5. The lands of Qui Sonant Pro Quieto are a safe haven for everyone.
6. Magical places outside Connacht are in the Order's protection until the Order gives that charge back.
7. The Coill Trí may use the beasts of the coast as they wish, save those of Vigil, which are the Order's alone.
8. Members of Praesis may enter Connacht for three reasons only: to pursue Hermetic justice, when Manannán mac Lir expressly asks it, and to find bees for their hives.
9. No magus or druid alone may set aside a clause: a magus invited into Connacht by a druid must still leave after three days.

treaties.title: The Treaty of Cnoc Maol Réidh
treaties.parties: The Order of Hermes in Hibernia and the Coill Trí
treaties.witness: Negotiated by Fedelmid Ua Heirméais of Mercere
treaties.ends: Never by one party alone; a clause is added when a Tribunal votes it and every ceannaire agrees
treaties.terms:
Made after High-King Congalach Cnogba's embassy of 844, brought by the Chief Bard Cormacan, on behalf of hedge wizards harried by the Order; signed in 851 once the Diedne had withdrawn, refused by the Diedne, rejected by the Grand Tribunal of 865, and made binding at Hibernia's first meeting in 898. It is named for Connacht's highest mountain, and its terms apply 'between druids and magi', not to lesser hedge wizards. Druids can change it only through a magus who proposes it for them.

1. The Order founds no covenant in Connacht, and no magus spends more than three nights running under a Connacht sky or roof.
2. The Coill Trí give the Order seven Gifted children at each Tribunal.
3. The Coill Trí have the right to be heard at Tribunal, their grievances are considered, and the Order does not deny them justice.
4. The Coill Trí are masters of their own places; the Order is master of all others.
5. The lands of Qui Sonant Pro Quieto are a safe haven for everyone.
6. Magical places outside Connacht are in the Order's protection until the Order gives that charge back.
7. The Coill Trí may use the beasts of the coast as they wish, save those of Vigil, which are the Order's alone.
8. Members of Praesis may enter Connacht for three reasons only: to pursue Hermetic justice, when Manannán mac Lir expressly asks it, and to find bees for their hives.
9. No magus or druid alone may set aside a clause: a magus invited into Connacht by a druid must still leave after three days.

changes.name: Tír na nÓg, the Otherworld
changes.was:
The Irish faeries' Otherworld: a lovely, uncanny mirror of the land around it, close by and yet apart. It is called Tír na nÓg (Land of the Young), Tír na mBeo (Land of the Living) or Mag Mell (Delightful Plain), and Hermetic scholars cannot tell whether they name one place or many. They do know the names point to the three faerie worlds of Realms of Power: Faerie: half of Ireland's faeries live in Elysium, the land of myth that keeps a people's history; a third in Eudokia, among the turning points of single lives, where babies are taken, wives stolen and drunkards led astray; and the fewest, though more each year, in Arcadia.

It is reached from faerie homes: most often a mound (sídhe, which also names the faeries), inside either a rough dwelling of stone pillars and earth roof or a sunlit, summery mansion; also cairns, tumuli, mountaintops, lake beds, the hearts of forests and bogs. Some are only Faerie auras, but many are regiones. It is the Faerie realm itself, not a site, so it has no aura of its own here.

Story seed: faeries often move house. A child makes an abandoned faerie ráth his secret den, and after a month of play vanishes; its owner, a brutish swamp-ogre, has come home. Was the boy eaten, flayed or sold to another faerie? The magi must learn which and bring him back.
changes.value:

covenants.notes:
Story seeds. The Magical Whale: Maris of Tytalus tells of a whale that brings an aura to the surface as it breaches. The First Contract: a stowaway from Southampton to Riga, fleeing a forced marriage. The First Act of Piracy: a ship said to hold silver carries monks and relics instead. The Rusted Bars: Tibor's cage rusts through overnight. The Fall of the Mercantile Families: Waddenzee's piracy threatens those who bank the covenant's silver. The Oyster Prince: the Oyster King's heir wants Hilde's trophies back.

Storylines. Exploration: Frisland and Icaria, Rupes Nigra, Estotiland, Drogeo, the Purple Islands, the far south. Lost cities: Atlantis, Tartessos. A new Tribunal: Carles means to help found three more ocean covenants, in Stonehenge, Hibernia, and the Rhine or Loch Leglean, for the twelve magi across four covenants needed to found one. The covenant is expected at Normandy's Tourney, and may be courted in the Lotharingian debate.

Magestones (Guardians of the Forests p. 70) would give each laboratory an aura of 3, if any could be got. Its Tribunal can be moved to the Rhine, Provence, Stonehenge or Hibernia to suit a saga.

The four younger magi suit players, Carles and Hilde the storyguide.

possessions.name: La Charytee
possessions.description:
A tall rear tower with a red-painted balcony; +2 to sailing. The Long Bone of Saint Epiphanius hangs from her mast.

Master: Carles Magnus. Captain: Gilot Vallet, shaven-headed, robust and exacting (Exacting +3, Loyal to Carles +2, Reckless -1).

possessions.name: Marie de Bayonne
possessions.description:
+1 to sailing close to shore, but she leaks. A sea opening in Hilde's laboratory lets her swim out in shark form.

Master: Hilde Oddfish. Captain: Taupin le Ribaut, a grey-bearded tyrant who runs a decent God-fearing ship (Merciless +3, Pious +2, Loyal to Hilde +1).

possessions.name: The Black Bark
possessions.description:
Her hull is painted pitch black.

Master: Andrew of Jerbiton. Captain: Pierre l'Englais, vibrant and clean-shaven, who loves the adventurous life (Adventurous +3, Energetic +2, Cautious -1).

possessions.name: The Laurens
possessions.description:
Wide in the beam, slower but stable in rough seas, with 25 tons more cargo than the others that could become a council chamber.

Master: Columba. Captain: Tiessot, a Breton who walks the ship at night and is silently in love with Columba (Thoughtful +3, In love with Columba +2, Protective of his crew +1).

possessions.name: Le Genet
possessions.description:
Patched and repaired many times. Tibor's iron cage stands in her sanctum.

Master: Tibor Milos. Captain: Susane la Fèvre, strong-willed, vocal and hard, with no qualms over piracy (Garrulous +3, Showy +1, Loyal to the Covenant -2).

possessions.name: Trinite
possessions.description:
Long-bodied with towers fore and aft, once a wreck on the seabed and a gift of the Merfolk to Carles. Her lateen sails tack close to the wind, but she takes -1 to damage checks in northern oceans. Matilda keeps a reading room in the forecastle.

Master: Matilda Page. Captain: Sarrasin, a Frenchman of Moorish descent (Patient +3, Paternal to his crew +2, Respectful +1).

possessions.name: The Long Bone of Saint Epiphanius
possessions.description: A relic of Faith Score 3 in a box at La Charytee's mast, with a Divine Might of 30 that scourges demons within 30 feet. Invoked, it lets those in the same structure understand each other's speech, Christians only (Babel Rejoined, InMe 40, Pen +8, 2 a day).

possessions.name: Brooch of Lungs of the Fish
possessions.description: MuAq 24, constant: the wearer breathes as by Lungs of the Fish. One, with its Lab Text.

possessions.name: The Freshwater Barrel
possessions.description: PeAq 20, 1 a day: takes the salt from seawater poured in. Carles and Hilde each have one, and the Lab Text.

possessions.name: The Master's Chart
possessions.description: An enchanted map on which carved miniatures of each ship, each an Arcane Connection, sail to her true position (Finding the Fleet, InHe 14, and Mark the Fleet, ReHe 11, each 12 a day). Opened with eight pawns, four used. Carles's; Hilde knows of it and has the Lab Text, and Matilda suspects.

possessions.name: Bell of Summoning
possessions.description: CrIm 30, 12 uses a day, Pen +32: rung on La Charytee, it sounds on all six ships, using six uses, so it can ring twice with effect.

possessions.name: Magical Astrolabes
possessions.description: InVi 40, unlimited use: gives the direction of an active magical effect, not its distance, and so finds the Bell. One on each ship.

possessions.name: The Agile Shields
possessions.description: The two halves of the Oyster King's shell, turned by The Agile Shield (MuTe 14) into kite shields of Excellent make, +3 Defense and Load 1, each holding 3 pawns of Lesser Enchantment vis.

possessions.name: Fire From the Sky
possessions.description: Fist-sized spheres of burning granite fall in a yearly hail storm over the northern seas and lose their vis if not gathered that night. Int + Artes Liberales (astrology) finds where and when.

possessions.name: The Kraken's Egg
possessions.description: A giant kraken rises each spring two hundred miles south-west of La Rochelle to feed and lay one egg; taken from the sea the egg keeps its vis, left there it hatches.

possessions.name: The Summer Fog
possessions.description: On the last night of July a fog of nightmares rolls in on Sønder Vorupør (The Unbidden Horrors, CrMe 20, Pen +10). Gathered in leather bags, it gives vis and frees the village.

possessions.name: The Black Horse of Boulogne
possessions.description: A vast black stallion comes to a secret pool Otto-Pauels knows; leave it new iron shoes and it casts off the old, a pawn in each. Tainted by Faerie. A seisin of the covenant under Tribunal law.

possessions.name: Alfgeir's Resting Place
possessions.description: Dedicated Rego Aquam vis (RoP: Magic p. 122) in the rune-carved timbers of a sunken knarr.

possessions.name: Alfgeir's Bones
possessions.description: Lesser Enchantment vis in his self-animating corpse, chained in La Charytee's hold (The Animated Corpse, ReCo 24). A season's taming gives it Dexterity and Single Weapon from its controller's Intelligence and Finesse.

possessions.name: The magi's shares
possessions.description: Fifteen pawns each, three of each Technique.

covenants.summary:
A flotilla of six ships working the seas from the Rhine to Hibernia and from Iceland to Iberia, its symbol a black cog at full sail on white. Each magus is master of a ship, with a captain and crew, and lives, studies and works aboard. Normandy's claim on it is tenuous: it has stayed out of Tribunal politics but is still bound by the Peripheral Code, and is expected at the Hermetic Tourney. Barfleur is its nominal home port, and Otto's office at Boulogne its nominal council chamber.

Income. Trade and transport earn only 40 Mythic Pounds a year against about 133 spent, 51 of it on provisions; the stores aboard and with merchant houses (340 pounds in London, Bruges, Hamburg, Lübeck, Bergen and Riga) last four or five years. Piracy is still being debated. Loyalty is -2.

At sea. With no aura and no Aegis the magi work with their ships at anchor, or trade for a season in a friendly covenant's aura, and they are charting auras and currents at sea. Their specialists stay ashore: Clovis the chaplain near St. Malo, Stephen the sail maker at Cherbourg, Hugh the carpenter, Guerrier the rope maker at Abbeville, the tax collector Shimon Avraham at Barfleur, and merchants in Antwerp, London and Paris. Each ship carries about a dozen sailors and a captain.
