The tithes are a tenth each to Church and Cathars. The costs allow for about two visiting nobles and retinues. 300 pounds in a locked chest in the manor house
Loyalty: +4 (53: base 30 from Loyal Covenfolk, turb captain +7, autocrat +6, living conditions +10). It does not apply to disputes between the magi, and Serena's threats could erode it; a steward and a chamberlain would help (Covenants pp. 30-39)
Council: at least once a season in the library's chamber, one vote each. Precedence runs from first residence, not the Gauntlet, and orders vis, books and resources: Joia, Lexora, Xenophanes, Beatriz, Ahenobarbus (1209), Alyssa (1214)
Votes: 6 at Tribunal, unused for four meetings. Spare laboratory room for three or four more magi; Council would likely stop at nine
Allies: Stella Durus; Bellaquin, now distant; Ostal des Exiles, through Joia and Gilbert
Rivals: Miniata Sophia; the Coenobium, since Joia's jibe at Alazais

charter_of_covenant.name: The Charter of Jardin
charter_of_covenant.preamble: Under the Provençal Peripheral Code a sworn charter binds in law, and breaking it can be tried as a Low Crime at Tribunal, so outsiders may be asked to rule on it.

clauses.text: Each maga spends one season a year in the covenant's service. What counts may be widened by Council vote, and a later vote may withdraw it.

Standing services, needing only a declaration: writing Lab Texts, tractatus or summae for the library; copying these to trade with other covenants; making enchanted devices for the covenant, vineyards or gardens; maintaining the gardens or vineyards; making one's own longevity ritual; setting up a new laboratory; extracting vis, or collecting it for the stocks if that takes over ten days; training an apprentice; teaching spells, Arts or Abilities to magi or covenfolk.
By tradition a maga may skip the service for a year, and is then assigned no vis.
A maga in good standing has four pawns of vis a year, plus what her covenant enchanting needs, the Aegis and the grogs, the library, and five pounds of silver.

An apprentice of the covenant who leaves to found a new covenant has a pawn of vis for each year trained here, fifty pounds of silver, and up to two years' free copying; one who joins an existing covenant does not.
Resident magae help collect the vis sources and attend Council when present.
Magae obey the Code of Hermes; one convicted of a Low Crime by a lawful Tribunal is asked to leave. This has never happened.

Magae swear never to declare Wizard's War on a fellow member, nor to use Certamen to overturn a ruling of Council. Added in 1219 over Ahenobarbus's and Lexora's votes; it binds only those who swear the charter hereafter, and so none of the present members.

covenants.secrets:
The legends are wrong: the visitor's three nights do nothing, and the Heart's Desire is a quest made through the Door. Scholars of the Order would flock here if the aura's change were known.

Serena is the covenant's greatest danger, and Lexora its open one. Skullface and lesser faeries already get past the Aegis.

Library: guests may copy for a season or more for a summa of equal or greater value, with no guest expenses; Lab Texts are open one season a year for the usual contribution and as many spell levels given as copied. Only one maga reads a book at a time, and Council rules when two want it

tribunals.name: The Provençal Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Tribunal of the langue d'oc: by the Grand Tribunal's ruling of 1129 it reaches wherever Occitan is spoken, from the Atlantic coast of Gascony across the Toulousain and the Narbonnais to the Rhône and the Alpine edge of Arelat, and from the Massif Central south into the Pyrenees and beyond them into Catalonia. Its magi, just over a hundred of them, lived quietly apart from the world until lately, in the wild south and the mountain strongholds; the gentle, personal bonds of paratge that bind the southern nobility left them freer than their sodales of the feudal north. The Albigensian Crusade has broken that ease: Mistridge, Lariander, Bentalone and Berinor have fallen in eleven years of war, refugees fill the covenants, and the question of what the Order should do about the crusade divides every council.

Three powers dominate. In the west the pagan Mercurians of Aedes Mercurii and the Mithraic, Christian Flambeau of Castra Solis, the domus magna, each claim to be the true heirs of Val-Negra and of Flambeau himself, and despise one another. In the east the many chapters of the Coenobium, Jerbiton and Redcaps under the Chief Redcap Alazais, smother any rival covenant in its shadow and have grown steadily stronger while the crusade wrecked the rest. Old and proud covenants stand apart from both: Tolosa Paratge, now tearing itself apart over its Cathar magi, and Bellaquin, the bankers of Andorra. Mystery cults matter here more than almost anywhere: the Legion of Mithras, the Cult of Mercury, Matres & Matrones, the Knights of the Green Stone and the Gorgiastic Cathars all reach across covenant lines.

Founding a covenant is easy: magi swear a charter together and a Quaesitor notarises it, and no vote is needed. Covenant oaths can be enforced at Tribunal, and a covenant may be spread over many sites or be no more than magi who meet in council now and then. The result is a land littered with the ruins of covenants that failed. Minutes and proclamations are written in Latin and Occitan both.

The Tribunal meets every seven years. By custom the eldest magus is Praeco: now Dama of Merinita, a maga of great age and power who lives apart from her covenant, Castra Solis, in a small tower near Mimizan, favours female magi, and is heeded even by Aedes Mercurii. A Presiding Quaesitor is chosen at the close of each meeting, with two advisers. Each day of a meeting opens with the rite of the Cult of Mercury's flamen, masked and robed, who speaks for the gods and reads the omens; most magi think it a quaint relic and Castra Solis's pious magi a blasphemy, but the office carries quiet influence. Midius of Flambeau, of Aedes Mercurii, holds it now.

The meeting of 1207, at Aedes Mercurii, spent a day on the Church's war on the Cathars and decided nothing; Oxioun of Tytalus argued for keeping out of mundane affairs. Months later the legate was killed and the crusade proclaimed, and the Traditionalist Presiding Quaesitor Protantus died; Senex held the office by 1210. The meeting of 1214, moved from besieged Toulouse to Castra Solis to the Mercurians' disgust, was the most bitter since the Schism War: charges of mundane interference flew, Normandy magi were accused of meddling and Tytalus of starting the crusade, Tolomae of Jerbiton was put out of the debate for demanding open magical war on the crusaders, and Aedes Mercurii's threat to walk out, which would have left the meeting without a quorum, was headed off only by Tibaut, then acting Presiding Quaesitor, and by the Chief Redcap's threat to suspend all Redcap service. Tres Ex Miscellanea was narrowly acquitted over the destruction of Mistridge.

The next meeting is in summer 1221, at the ruins of Glanum near St-Rémy, chosen by agreement as neutral ground. Its first business is the Presiding Quaesitor: Tibaut died last year, and his filia Beatrice of Guernicus, nominally of Castra Solis but living at Glanum on the edge of the Coenobium's lands, has acted in his place at the Praeco's suggestion. She is presumed to succeed him, but she is young and without standing among the factions, and the choice may be contested. After that the crusade will fill the meeting: the Hermetic faidits want licence to defend themselves and reclaim what they lost, and look to Garus and the milites of Castra Solis; the conservatives led by Aedes Mercurii, with Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia, want to keep out of it, and if the Tribunal intervenes they may boycott the meeting of 1227 and ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 for a Tribunal of their own. Many senior magi are uneasy at the Coenobium's growing reach, and Tolosa Paratge's war may be raised if anyone brings a case.

Votes at the meeting of 1221:
- The Coenobium Rhodanien: about 20
- Aedes Mercurii: 18
- Castra Solis: 17, to which the Praeco's and the Presiding Quaesitor's votes are added
- Tolosa Paratge: 9, split between its Black and White factions
- Ostal des Exiles: 6, although the Tribunal has not yet recognised it
- Bellaquin: 5
- Stella Durus: 5
- Ara Maxima Nova: 4
- Miniata Sophia: 4
- Tres' Band: 3, never cast: the band shuns Tribunal

Stories. The crusade is the background to everything: the Order is split over how to answer it, and the meeting at Glanum in 1221 will argue little else. Beside it run the Six Deadly Spirits in Gascony and the Narbonnais, the followers of the Procrustean League hiding among the faidits, Tolosa Paratge's war with itself and the Coenobium's growing reach. Two stories wait for the storyguide to begin them: the lost covenant of Val-Negra and what its Iron Door holds, and the Pyrenean covenants' threat to seek a Tribunal of their own at the Grand Tribunal of 1228. A smaller hook: Tres' Band, roving in the forests near Bazas, watches how each new covenant treats the common folk, and turns from indifference to hatred against magi who set themselves up as lords.
tribunals.history:
The Roman Provincia. In antiquity the Aquitanians, a Basque people, held what is now Gascony, and Greek traders from Massalia founded Marseilles and Trinquetaille and traded up the rivers with the Celts of Arelat. Rome came in 125 BC and split its Provincia into Novempopulania facing the Atlantic and Narbonensis facing the Mediterranean, and both prospered for five centuries. The one great revolt came in 106 BC, when a governor drained the sacred lake of the Tolosates to take the gold sunk in it; with the Cimbri's help the rebels beat Rome at Arausio in 105 BC, and the treasure was lost and never found.

The coming of Christianity. Tradition says Mary Magdalene and the Virgin landed at Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, and Lazarus became the first bishop of Marseilles. The land kept to the Roman gods until Bishop Sernin of Toulouse was dragged to death behind a bull in 257; his martyrdom broke the Cult of Mercury in the city, which became a centre of the new faith.

Visigothic Septimania. Rome withdrew in 419 and the Visigoths, Arian allies of the empire, settled Narbonensis by treaty in 462, gave up its lands east of the Rhône in 475 for full independence, and took Arles in 472. Their kingdom, named Septimania for its seven cities, ruled from Toulouse until Clovis beat them at Vouillé in 507. The Ostrogoths checked the Franks, and Visigothic kings held the Narbonnais until the 720s. Converted to the mainstream faith by the mid-sixth century, the Goths still kept old customs, and the last Roman flamens of the Cult of Mercury kept secrets that Priamitus and Apromor would later seek.

Franks and Moors. Under the Merovingian Franks a dark age of usurpation, plague and famine fell on the land; Roman cities in Arelat emptied, marshes swallowed old fields, and the lords of Toulouse made themselves dukes all but free of the crown. The Moors took Narbonne in 719 and marched on Toulouse, where Duke Odo of Gascony and Toulouse beat them in 721, buying time for Charles Martel's victory at Tours in 732. The Franks took Septimania in 759 and the Pyrenees by the century's end, but their southern dukes rebelled again and again.

Charlemagne. Charlemagne crushed the southern lords in 770 on his way to Spain. In 778 he besieged the Moor Mirat at Lourdes, who surrendered and was baptised, and on the way home from Spain his rearguard was cut down at the pass of Roncevaux. The deaths of Roland and Bishop Turpin are the troubadours' most beloved tale.

The counts of Toulouse. By the ninth century Toulouse's counts had again slipped free of the distant Frankish throne, reaching their height under Raimond IV, count of St Gilles and marquis of Arelat (1093 to 1105), when Occitan letters and the troubadours flowered. The counts feuded with Foix and with the Trencavel of Carcassonne and Béziers, clashed with the bishops who share justice in Toulouse and with the rising capitouls, and bought popular support with privileges, so that the county is full of knights and ladies holding their own castles. Notaries, heirs of Roman law, appeared in the Narbonnais in the 1140s alongside the consular towns.

Heresy. Cathar belief took root in the tenth century and by 1220 rivals the Church in the south. Bernard of Clairvaux preached against it for one summer in 1145, with success in Albi and Toulouse and scorn in the countryside. The Council of Tours condemned the heretics and those who sheltered them in 1163; churchmen found them heretical at Lombers in 1165 but let them go, and by 1167 they had bishops of their own. The Third Lateran Council called for arms against them in 1179, a legate's army besieged Lavaur in 1181 to little effect, and two legates sent in 1203 found the southern bishops corrupt and immovable. Arnaud Amaury was made legate and Foulques bishop of Toulouse, a see so low he dared not live in it. Dominic of Guzman walked barefoot among the heretics from 1206 to 1208, winning more love than converts.
tribunals.meeting_place: The ruins of Glanum, near St-Rémy (Arelat)

cases.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
cases.charge: Tibaut of Guernicus died in 1219 (some accounts say 1214). His filia Beatrice of Guernicus has acted as Presiding Quaesitor since, at the Praeco's suggestion, and is presumed to take the office; but she is young, has no standing with the factions, has fallen out with Primus Garus, and would hand the office to a better candidate of her House if one appeared. Confirming or replacing her is the first business of the meeting.

cases.title: The deaths of Senex and Tibaut
cases.charge: Presiding Quaesitor Senex vanished in 1210, last seen going into a village to look into something, and was declared lost when he missed the meeting of 1214. Tibaut, who found in Senex's notes that he had been investigating a mystery cult, believed him dead and was himself looking into the Tribunal's cults when he died on the road near Foix. Beatrice suspects foul play but has no proof.
cases.evidence:
Senex's laboratory notes on an unnamed cult
Tibaut's suspicions, shared with Beatrice
Tibaut missed his meeting with Beatrice
Luc of Ara Maxima Nova fought Tibaut in certamen over his questions about the Via Domitia

cases.title: Recognition of the Ostal des Exiles
cases.charge: The House of Exiles, founded since 1214 under Castle d'Aguilar by survivors of Mistridge, Lariander and other fallen covenants, asks to be recognised as a covenant of the Tribunal, with its six votes.

cases.title: The faidits' petition
cases.brought_by: The Hermetic faidits (Ostal des Exiles and refugees)
cases.charge: The magi who lost their covenants to de Montfort's armies ask for licence to defend themselves against the crusaders and to win back their magical power, and want Garus and the milites of Castra Solis behind them, even with open magic. The Mercurian conservatives oppose any intervention in mundane affairs.

cases.title: A Tribunal of the Pyrenees
cases.brought_by: Aedes Mercurii and the conservative covenants
cases.charge: If the Tribunal intervenes against the crusade and the Church, Aedes Mercurii, Ara Maxima Nova, Stella Durus and Miniata Sophia may boycott the meeting of 1227 and, being the four covenants a Tribunal needs, ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to make them a Tribunal of their own. Bellaquin dreams of a Catalan Tribunal instead.

cases.title: Tolosa Paratge's civil war
cases.against: The Black and White factions of Tolosa Paratge
cases.charge: Since Marc killed Augustus in Wizard's War in 1218 and St. Tropez killed Marc, the covenant has split: the pro-Cathar Blacks hold the regio, the Whites wait in the city to retake it. Both sides are plainly depriving each other of magical resources, but the Quaesitores have not acted, out of respect for the covenant and because no one has brought a case. The Whites may appeal to the Tribunal in 1221.

cases.title: The Procrustean League's followers
cases.charge: After Tolomae was Marched in 1218, several of his rumoured supporters fled to other covenants or vanished among the faidits of the langue d'oc. Some magi fear his cause will return, embittered by the war.

cases.title: Marie of Merinita and the northern border
cases.charge: Marie keeps a manor at Poitiers, in lands usually held to be Normandy's, as a chapter of Castra Solis, attends Tribunal in Provence, and works to push the Tribunal's border north by spreading southern language and culture through Aquitaine, so that the 1129 rule of the Occitan tongue would carry the land with it.

cases.title: An undeclared covenant in the Hyères
cases.brought_by: (no one: the Tribunal does not know of it)
cases.charge: Secret. Ahmad ibn Nasr of Tytalus and two Moorish magi keep an undeclared covenant among the Hyères islands, backing raids on the coast and harvesting vis on the islands, afraid that Fraxinetum's memory would bring a Wizard's War on them if they declared it. Aucassin of Tytalus lives as an eremite at Beaucaire under a false name. A case can only be brought once someone finds them out.

rulings.title: Founding a covenant
rulings.says: A covenant comes into being when its magi agree on a common aim, write a charter setting out their oath, and swear it together; the swearing is what counts. The one legal step is to have a Quaesitor notarise the charter, which makes it enforceable under the Code, and some groups put this off. No vote or approval of the Tribunal is needed, though it is polite to tell the nearest Mercer House and to send someone to the next meeting to announce the new covenant. A settlement never notarised (Glanum I and II, Portus Termini) was never a recognised covenant. The Provence package records this as its Open founding custom.

rulings.title: Covenant oaths enforceable
rulings.says: A covenant's oath is part of the Peripheral Code here, and a Tribunal can rule on it. As a result many small quarrels within a council, settled elsewhere by certamen or among the members, are brought before the whole Tribunal.

rulings.title: Covenants on many sites
rulings.says: A covenant need not live in one place. Its members may keep separate homes and meet in council only when needed: Castra Solis counts the Praeco at Mimizan and Marie of Merinita at Poitiers as members, and the Coenobium is a chain of chapters along the Rhône and the coast.

rulings.title: Residency
rulings.says: A magus is resident who attended one of the last three meetings, or is voted resident at the first he attends. A magus Gauntleted in the Tribunal is resident until he has missed three meetings in a row. Residency lasts until the magus claims it in another Tribunal or attends and votes at another Tribunal's meeting.

rulings.title: Registering arrivals and departures
rulings.says: Magi who settle in the Tribunal between meetings register either with both the Redcaps and the Praeco, or with their nearest neighbouring covenant, a Redcap guiding them there if they do not know the way. A magus who takes residency elsewhere must first register his leaving with the Provençal Redcaps or the Praeco, before voting at another Tribunal, or he breaks the Peripheral Code.

rulings.title: The border of the Occitan tongue
rulings.says: After quarrels with Normandy over the newly enlarged Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal fixed the border as running wherever the people speak Occitan. Disliked at first, the rule is now embraced as the ground of the Tribunal's claims to vis and other resources, and the Tribunal writes its minutes, proclamations and many other documents in Occitan as well as Latin.

rulings.title: The Praeco
rulings.says: By custom the eldest magus of the Tribunal presides as Praeco.

rulings.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
rulings.says: The Presiding Quaesitor, who runs the meeting, is appointed at the close of each meeting together with two advisers. When the office falls vacant between meetings an acting Presiding Quaesitor serves until the next meeting confirms or replaces him, as Tibaut did for Senex and Beatrice does for Tibaut.

rulings.title: The flamen of Mercury
rulings.says: By ancient tradition a priest of the Cult of Mercury, in mask and robes of office, opens every day of a meeting with a rite, speaking for the gods and reading omens in the Tribunal's ceremonies. The rite goes unchallenged for its age, though few take it seriously.

rulings.title: Val-Negra must not rise again
rulings.says: After the fall of Val-Negra in the Schism War, and the panic over what was found sealed there, the Quaesitores decided in secret that the covenant must never be refounded, and House Flambeau made Castra Solis its domus magna instead. Few magi know the reason, and even the site is now lost.

rulings.title: Fraxinetum's destruction
rulings.says: The magi of the eastern Tribunal who banded together against Fraxinetum's Moorish raiders worked through William I of Provence's army rather than a declared Wizard's War, and narrowly escaped the Quaesitores' censure for destroying a covenant that way. The league they formed became the Coenobium.

rulings.title: Bellaquin and mundane lordship
rulings.says: Twice jealous neighbours charged Bellaquin with breaking its oath by its deep entanglement in feudal affairs; twice the Tribunal found it had brought no ruin on its accusers or the Order. The precedent: even heavy mundane involvement is tolerated so long as it causes no ruin to magi.

rulings.title: No ruling on the Cathars
rulings.says: The meeting at Aedes Mercurii debated the Church's campaign against the Cathars for a whole day and made no decision; the Mercurians' counsel of staying out of mundane affairs prevailed by default. No case has yet been brought against an avowedly Cathar magus.

rulings.title: Grogs in a Wizard's War
rulings.says: Tres Ex Miscellanea armed a company of mercenaries with magical weapons, called them his grogs, and used them and his magical siege engines to level Mistridge's tower. As his Wizard's War had been properly declared, and nothing in the Code forbids using grogs to wage one, the Tribunal acquitted him by a narrow vote. He then went into hiding from Mistridge's friends.

rulings.title: The March of Tolomae
rulings.says: Tolomae, once of the Coenobium and Bellaquin, led the Procrustean League in calling for open war on the Church. Renounced by the Mercurians and the Coenobium, he was cast out of House Jerbiton as orbus in 1216, fled rather than answer a Quaesitor's questions over the murder of the legate Pierre de Castelnau, and early in 1218 was Marched for repeated interference with mundanes and slain.

rulings.title: Glanum held neutral
rulings.says: The ruins of Glanum, agreed as the compromise site for the meeting of 1221, may not be formally resettled until that question is settled. Only Beatrice of Guernicus lives there, as the Coenobium's guest.

rulings.title: The Coenobium's toll and code of hospitality
rulings.says: A local custom of the Coenobium's towns, not a Tribunal ruling, but one every visitor meets. Magi openly visiting Avignon announce themselves and how long they will stay, and are asked to give a silver florin holding a pawn of vis, which pays for the covenant's non-Jerbiton specialists. In return they get food, lodging, laboratory space and a consul as patron, who answers for their conduct and protects them. The guest's part: give notice of the visit by Redcap if possible, bring the florin, state the purpose and length of the stay and say when leaving, behave with restraint and help the patron if asked, and go at once if told to. Magi who refuse are thought crass, watched, and quietly obstructed, even with charges at Tribunal. The Coenobium keeps its members' Latin names, and has let no new covenant thrive in southern Provence for over a century unless it joined as a chapter.

diary.title: Regional Tribunals created
diary.details: As the Order grows, the Second Grand Tribunal sets up regional Tribunals, made of covenants that lie near one another rather than of lands with fixed borders. The rules for founding and governing them come out of a quarrel over Val-Negra's charter: Flambeau wanted lordship over every covenant his home helped to found.

diary.title: Val-Negra recognized
diary.details: After years of argument between Flambeau and Guernicus over its charter, the covenant of Val-Negra in the Pyrenees is formally recognized, and a regional Tribunal forms around it. Flambeau is the only Founder to make his home there, though Trianoma and Mercere visit often. Tolosa Paratge, a large Diedne covenant in a lake regio at Toulouse, is one of the four first covenants of the new Tribunal, and most of the region's other covenants belong to House Diedne.

diary.title: Gelon becomes Primus of Verditius
diary.details: Gelon, the first apprentice of Verditius, becomes Primus of his House. He lives for decades at Val-Negra, forging his famous enchanted swords, and his followers go on to found the Confraternity of Roland.

diary.title: Kaeso joins House Flambeau
diary.details: The Christian wizard Kaeso, whose power rests on an old underground temple of Mithras by the Garonne, joins House Flambeau. Training under Apromor and Flambeau in the Pyrenees, he forms the Hoplites, soldier-magi who hurl Pilum of Fire from behind a strong Parma Magica, and leads many of them into the Legion of Mithras. Many count him the first Hoplite.

diary.title: Apromor becomes Primus of Flambeau
diary.details: Apromor, the Founder's first apprentice, who has drifted from his master's ways, becomes the first Primus of House Flambeau, and Kaeso's Hoplites carry on Flambeau's war against the sahirs of Iberia. Apromor welcomes pagan and non-Hermetic wizards into the Order, works with Priamitus of Mercere to revive the Cult of Mercury from the last Roman priests of the region, and spreads Val-Negra's outposts across the Pyrenees.

diary.title: Portus Cottiae and Yf founded
diary.details: Julius Donnus, an outcast Mercurian of House Flambeau from the Greater Alps, founds Portus Cottiae outside Briançon as a second home for the revived Cult of Mercury, after Harco. It becomes the first Mercer House of the region and grows into a covenant of several sites, with chapter houses at Gap, Chorges and Embrun and a post at Oulx guarding the passes. In the same year Diedne magi found Yf on an island off the coast of Arelat.

diary.title: Lapurdum founded
diary.details: Flambeau magi found Lapurdum where the Adour meets the sea in Gascony, around a mithraeum in what was once a Roman army camp.

diary.title: Campus Elysii founded
diary.details: A small group of spirit masters, necromancers of Ex Miscellanea, settles in the crypts of the Alyscamps at Arles as the covenant of Campus Elysii.

diary.title: Vikings on the Garonne
diary.details: King Pepin II of Aquitaine, seeking freedom from Charles the Bald, is accused of apostasy for letting the Viking Jarl Oscar sail his raiders up the Garonne to Toulouse. Northmen camp all along the western coast, and Marseilles has already been sacked by Arab pirates (838); Byzantine freebooters (849) and Normans based in the Camargue follow. Tales of rune-wizards among the raiders finally draw the magi in, and Flambeau comes to resent how little the Diedne do to help.

diary.title: Castra Solis founded
diary.details: Raids on Gascon villages have grown since 840, and the Flambeau wrongly believe an organized Order of Odin is behind them. Kaeso returns to Bordeaux and fortifies his temple as a covenant, Castra Solis, the encampment of the sun, under the sign of a quartered sun.

diary.title: Bordeaux falls to the Northmen
diary.details: Before the Hoplites can do more than raise hasty defences, the northern pagans take Bordeaux. Unwilling to harm the townsfolk, the magi spend five years trying to end the war by force against the rune-wizards alone, and many die in their traps, Kaeso among them.

diary.title: Sinapis founded
diary.details: With Bordeaux too near the front, the surviving Flambeau build a fortified covenant, Sinapis, further north in Anjou. Castra Solis becomes a camp of tents for quick strikes, and to outsiders it looks like an offshoot of Sinapis.

diary.title: Lapurdum abandoned
diary.details: Worn down by Viking raids and quarrels among its magi, Lapurdum is given up. Its ruins lie somewhere under the city of Bayonne.

diary.title: Seven Tribunals defined
diary.details: The Grand Tribunal draws up seven regional Tribunals. Val-Negra goes to the Iberian Tribunal, along with the mountains and the Basque lands north of them; the bulk of France goes to the West Franks, and a strip from Friesland through Burgundy to Arelat forms the Lotharingian Tribunal.

diary.title: Fraxinetum founded
diary.details: Two Tytalan war-magi, Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda (who called himself a Flambeau, though the House denies him) and his lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf, settle in the Massif des Maures above St Tropez with a band of Andalusian raiders. Their covenant, named for the ash groves Sayyid planted, stays hidden from the Tribunal for its first century while it backs Moorish attacks on Provençal towns.

diary.title: Barbegal founded
diary.details: Three Verditius mage-smiths found a covenant in the Roman watermill complex of Barbegal, just north of Arles.

diary.title: Lotharingia divided
diary.details: The Grand Tribunal hands the northern covenants of the Lotharingian Tribunal to Normandy or the Rhine. What is left, the Kingdom of Arles along the Rhône and a few covenants in the Toulousain (a Mercer House at Arles, a strong Diedne covenant at Lyon, and a handful of others), comes to be called the Provençal Tribunal.

diary.title: The Birds of Camargue founded
diary.details: Bjornaer magi found a covenant in the marshes at the mouth of the Rhône.

diary.title: Portus Cottiae overrun
diary.details: Berber mountaineers overrun the scattered sites of Portus Cottiae, one of the first Lotharingian covenants to fall to the Saracens. Its magi flee down the Durance; at the motherhouse near Briançon the defenders bring the mountain down on the raiders and bury themselves in their own sancta. The one surviving maga, Anaïs of Jerbiton, reaches Avignon and becomes a loud voice for the Hermetic league that becomes the Coenobium.

diary.title: Yf falls
diary.details: The Diedne covenant of Yf falls to the raids of Fraxinetum. One of its magae later joins the Coenobium to avenge it, but her line dies out shortly before the Schism War.

diary.title: Barbegal abandoned
diary.details: The undefended mills of Barbegal are abandoned under Saracen raiding. The surviving smiths help to found the Rhône covenant of Coenobium Rhodanien.

diary.title: Askelarre founded
diary.details: A coven of Hermetic sorginak, Basque witches spread across the Basque country, founds the covenant of Askelarre.

diary.title: Sorginak join Ex Miscellanea; Donjon Leyre founded
diary.details: A few sorginak at last join House Ex Miscellanea, resented by their hedge sisters and anxious to keep their distance from the Diedne, who had long taken sorginak into their own House. In the same year Donjon Leyre, an early vassal of Montverte, is founded at the fork of the Leyre in the Landes as a base for raids into the Basque Pyrenees.

diary.title: The Birds of Camargue merge into the Coenobium
diary.details: Threatened by Fraxinetum, the Bjornaer of the Birds of Camargue join the wider league of Rhône magi that becomes the Coenobium Rhodanien.

diary.title: Maieul of Cluny captured
diary.details: The Moors of the Massif des Maures capture and ransom Maieul, abbot of Cluny, and push into the foothills of the Alps. The alarm this raises moves the mostly Jerbiton magi of eastern Provence to band together in a pact of mutual defence. Working through their families, churchmen and noble allies, they quietly back the army of William I of Provence, which routs the Moors at Tourtour.

diary.title: Fraxinetum destroyed
diary.details:
William's army takes the Moorish base and the Fraxinetum magi vanish into the forest. The history chapter says the Coenobium Rhodanien, which it calls newly formed (the Birds of Camargue had joined it in 970), destroyed the covenant by Wizard's War; the Arelat chapter says no war was ever openly declared and the league narrowly escaped the Quaesitors' anger for acting through mundane arms. Either way, the victors stay together as a covenant of many sites along the Rhône and the coast. In the same year Anaïs of Toulouse, a renegade Criamon expelled from her House, brings her followers, the Gorgiastic Cathars, into House Ex Miscellanea.

Secrets
The Fraxinetum magi did not perish. Their heirs live on in secret as Fraxinetum Redux on the Hyères islands, never declared to the Tribunal.

diary.title: Grand Tribunal: the Northmen driven out
diary.details: At the Grand Tribunal the Hoplites declare the rune-wizards rooted out of the region after more than a century of war: all three Danish settlements on the coast have been burned. Many of their fortified outposts, such as the tower at Mimizan, later grow into covenants counted as offshoots of Castra Solis. The Diedne, uneasy with the Mithraic piety of the Hoplites, took no part, which deepens Flambeau's suspicion of them.

diary.title: Donjon Leyre falls
diary.details: All the founding magi of Donjon Leyre die fighting in the Schism War, which rages through Gascony as Val-Negra's forces storm the Diedne covenants one after another; many Gascon Diedne burn their own sites and flee.

diary.title: Campus Elysii driven out
diary.details:
The spirit masters of Campus Elysii, who hid underground through the war, are forced out of the Alyscamps when the Coenobium stirs up the townsfolk with tales of diabolists under the necropolis. They try to begin again in a cave network in the Verdon gorge as Portus Termini, but all contact is lost before the next Tribunal and the new covenant is never registered.

Secrets
Many suspect that Hoplites in the Coenobium's pay hunted down the survivors.

diary.title: Askelarre destroyed
diary.details: The sorginak covenant of Askelarre is destroyed in the Schism War. Two of Val-Negra's magi, the Flambeau Leo Augustus and the Tremere Vegetius, die in the attack.

diary.title: The fall of Val-Negra
diary.details:
As the Schism War draws to its close, while its zealous magi are away striking at the Diedne, five Diedne archmagi storm Val-Negra. Of twenty-five magi at the war's start, only four are left. Shortly before the war many of its Flambeau had left, after a vision, to found Aedes Mercurii in Val-Negra's outlying halls; now the survivors join it, and it declares itself a Provençal covenant and the heir of Val-Negra. Many other covenants change to the Provençal Tribunal at this time, partly to keep Tytalus from claiming the spoils of the fallen Diedne. The domus magna of Flambeau moves to Castra Solis, and the Quaesitors strike nine or more Diedne sites from the records. Why Val-Negra was never rebuilt, and even where it stood, is soon forgotten.

Secrets
The Diedne reached the Iron Door in the depths of Val-Negra, and in the fighting the Adulteration of Flambeau was loosed. It killed three defenders and all the attackers before the last two archmagi forced it back and sealed the door with a Hermetic ward, one that breaks if the door is simply opened. The Quaesitors kept it quiet and ruled that Val-Negra must never rise again.

diary.title: Bellaquin founded
diary.details: As the Schism War dies down, Flambeau magi restore an abandoned castle, the Château de Penne in Tarn above the Aveyron, as a stronghold. The war ends before it is needed, and they hand it to House Jerbiton, who make it one of the most admired covenants in the Order and, in time, the lords of a fief of their own.

diary.title: Mistridge founded
diary.details: A covenant is founded in the Val du Bosque, in a tower raised by magic at the brink of a sheer drop.

diary.title: Windgraven founded
diary.details: Necromancers found Windgraven in the squat stone towers of a ruined Visigothic fort on a rocky plateau in the southern part of the County of Toulouse.

diary.title: Filii Sinapis founded
diary.details: Flambeau magi from the abandoned Normandy covenant of Sinapis found Filii Sinapis.

diary.title: Berinor founded
diary.details: Jerbiton magi found Berinor, a small covenant in the County of Toulouse that becomes a patron of troubadours and trobairitz.

diary.title: Gascony joins the Provençal Tribunal
diary.details: When the Normandy Tribunal splits, Castra Solis leads a faction into the enlarged Provençal Tribunal. The magi of Sinapis leave their site to join the domus magna, and smaller covenants of the area, Mimizan among them, come too.

diary.title: Bentalone founded
diary.details: A covenant is founded in a castle in the Toulousain; it stays in Summer for a century.

diary.title: Grand Tribunal: the Occitan border
diary.details: To settle quarrels between Normandy and the newly enlarged Provençal Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal rules that the border between them runs wherever Occitan stops being spoken. Unpopular at first, the rule is soon embraced by the southern magi to secure their claims to vis, and the Tribunal's minutes and proclamations are written in both Latin and Occitan.

diary.title: The Golden Court at Beaucaire
diary.details:
Count Henry II of Provence holds a festival in the meadows north of Beaucaire to mark the reconciliation of the Duke of Narbonne and the King of Aragon. A chronicler praises its hundred thousand knights, its gold sown in the earth and its herds roasted over wax torches.

Secrets
Most of the knights were faeries revelling in the troubadours' spirit of foolishness, and the gold was glamour; the meadow still holds Faerie vis.

diary.title: Saint Jean Pied-de-Port razed
diary.details: When Richard the Lionheart sacks Saint Jean Pied-de-Port, the large outpost Aedes Mercurii kept there is lost; its covenfolk had already fallen under the townsfolk's suspicion of witchcraft.

diary.title: Miniata Sophia founded
diary.details: A Criamon eremite founds Miniata Sophia in the cave system of Niaux, about forty years before 1220. For a decade and more it keeps to itself.

diary.title: Lariander founded
diary.details: Tremere magi found Lariander, a young covenant in a faerie wood near the village of Montgey in the Toulousain.

diary.title: Tribunal: Miniata Sophia announced
diary.details: Miniata Sophia makes itself known at the Tribunal and registers its site, the village of Niaux, with the Redcaps. It has attended every meeting since, voting on each question as seems most apt or abstaining, and making no alliances.

diary.title: Ara Maxima Nova founded
diary.details: Merinita magi who have explored the labours of Heracles in the east come west to follow the rest of his journey and found Ara Maxima Nova among the vineyards outside Perpignan, close to the Via Domitia. Their charter binds them to seek the Hesperides every five years.

diary.title: Windgraven destroyed
diary.details: Magi of Mistridge destroy Windgraven in a properly declared Wizard's War, battering its towers flat with giant stones conjured by magic. Few mourn its necromancers, who were widely thought diabolists, and the war foreshadows Mistridge's own end.

diary.title: Bellaquin falls
diary.details:
Overstretched by its feudal ties, Bellaquin tries to help two warring lords at once and is accused by both of stirring up their war. With churchmen urging them on, and a companion betraying the covenant, they storm the Château de Penne by surprise and kill several magi. The survivors, warned to prepare by archmagi, take their hidden reserves, destroy what they cannot carry and leave the site to their mundane proxies. Since the harm fell only on Bellaquin, no charges are brought.

Secrets
Some suspect other magi had a hand in arranging the mundane attack.

diary.title: Bellaquin moves to Andorra
diary.details: Bellaquin settles in a house in the parish of Ordino in Andorra, keeping its charter but changing its ways: subtler, richer and turned toward banking.

diary.title: Bentalone overrun
diary.details: The book's list of fallen covenants ends Bentalone in 1207: Simon de Montfort's army takes its castle for a Cathar stronghold and storms it in a surprise attack, though his campaigns in the south only begin in 1209.

diary.title: Raimond VI excommunicated
diary.details: In May Count Raimond VI of Toulouse is excommunicated for sheltering heretics. He promises the pope to drive them out, and the sentence is lifted in August.

diary.title: Tribunal at Aedes Mercurii
diary.details: The Tribunal meets at Aedes Mercurii and spends a whole day on the Church's drive against the Cathars, without deciding anything. Oxioun of Tytalus, leader of the host covenant, urges the Order to stay out of mundane affairs, and the Mercurian bloc is content to wait in its mountains, despite the worries of the lowland covenants of the Toulousain, the Narbonnais and the Rhône.

diary.title: Protantus dies; Tibaut chief Quaesitor
diary.details: A few months after the 1207 Tribunal, Protantus, the Traditionalist chief Quaesitor, dies and is followed by the more flexible Tibaut, a Transitionalist with no ties to the Mercurians. Few magi remark the coincidence with the legate's death, but it marks a turning point. The history chapter tells it so; the Gascony chapter names Senex as chief Quaesitor until 1210, with Tibaut acting in his place only from 1214.

diary.title: Interdict in Gascony
diary.details:
Innocent III lays all of King John's lands under interdict. Many Gascon churches close their doors and say no Mass for six years.

Secrets
During the interdict a band of demons, the Six Deadly Spirits, settles in the wild lands of Gascony away from the pilgrim roads, and some linger there still.

diary.title: The legate murdered
diary.details: In January Raimond meets the papal legates at St Gilles, stalls, and threatens them in anger as they leave. At dawn, waiting for the ferry to Arles, the legate Pierre de Castelnau is run through by a knight, forgiving his killer as he dies. Innocent III blames the count and proclaims a crusade; Arnaud Amaury and Bishop Foulques preach it, promising the crusaders a share of heretic lands and release from their debts to Jewish lenders.

diary.title: Raimond joins the crusade
diary.details: As the crusaders muster at Lyon, Raimond is scourged barefoot before a crowd at St Gilles and accepts hard terms. In June he takes the cross himself, robbing the crusade of its main target, which turns on the Trencavel lands instead. Raimond-Roger Trencavel is refused leave to join.

diary.title: The sack of Béziers
diary.details: Béziers refuses to hand over two hundred heretics. When its young men sally against the crusade's camp followers, the rabble surges through the open gate and the knights follow. Asked how to tell the faithful from the heretics, Arnaud Amaury is said to have answered that God would know His own. Fifteen to thirty thousand die, many in the churches.

diary.title: Carcassonne surrenders
diary.details: In August Viscount Raimond-Roger Trencavel leaves Carcassonne to parley and is seized and imprisoned. The city yields; its people are spared but its treasures plundered. Why so strong a city gave in so soon remains a mystery.

diary.title: Simon de Montfort leads the crusade
diary.details: When the great lords go home after their forty days, the legate's council chooses Simon de Montfort, a minor knight of the Île de France, to lead. With his wife Alice, thirty knights and five hundred foot he holds Carcassonne and takes the Trencavel titles of Béziers and Carcassonne, but Pedro II of Aragon will not take his homage. Revolts follow, the abbot of St Gilles is murdered, and de Montfort answers with the atrocity at Bram. In Toulouse Bishop Foulques forms his White Brotherhood against heretics, Jews and moneylenders, and a Black Brotherhood rises against it.

diary.title: Mistridge destroyed
diary.details: The Rusticani magus Tres declares Wizard's War on every magus of Mistridge. With two other magi of his tradition and a company of mercenaries armed with his enchanted weapons, he levels the tower with magical siege engines and kills its defenders. Some say he avenged Windgraven; others that Mistridge had scorned him as a hedge wizard.

diary.title: Minerve and Termes fall
diary.details: When the castle of Aguilar holds out, de Montfort turns to besiege Minerve, where a hundred and thirty-seven Cathars are burned and only three women recant. Termes and more castles follow, making him master of the Trencavel lands. So few heretics have died that the war is plainly one of conquest.

diary.title: Berinor falls; Senex vanishes
diary.details:
Berinor falls when de Montfort's men dispossess the lord who held its castle, and its survivors take refuge at Tolosa Paratge. The same year Senex of Guernicus, the chief Quaesitor, goes into a village to look into something and is never seen again.

Secrets
Senex had begun to look into Dama's cult of the Matres and Matrones. While she was away at an akelarre he slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan; she came back early and caught him there. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's venom killed him, Maju devoured the body as a drake, and Dama told no one. In law he had forfeited his immunity by entering her sanctum.

diary.title: Lavaur, and the first siege of Toulouse
diary.details: Pedro II at last accepts de Montfort's homage and tries to broker peace, but the legates' terms are too harsh and the south rises. Lavaur is sacked, sixty Cathars taken at Les Casses are burned, and de Montfort besieges Toulouse. Bishop Foulques tells the faithful to give up the city and their count or share the heretics' fate; they drive him out instead, and the siege fails.

diary.title: Montgey and the fall of Lariander
diary.details:
Peasants and southern knights massacre some three hundred German crusaders marching through a faerie forest near Montgey to Lavaur. In reprisal the crusaders destroy the village, burn the woods and slaughter the Tremere of Lariander, taking their black robes for those of Cathar perfecti. Garsenda of Lariander believes she is the only survivor.

Secrets
Garsenda had stirred the villagers to the ambush, and the white ladies and walking trees the survivors spoke of were real.

diary.title: Battle of St Martin-Lalande
diary.details: Raimond gathers his army against de Montfort's small force, but the crusaders keep raiding and seizing the initiative, and when the southerners finally attack they are routed in open battle.

diary.title: The Children's Crusade; Las Navas de Tolosa
diary.details: Thousands of children and peasants follow a young visionary from the Rhineland through France to Marseilles, sure the sea will open for them. It does not; many board ships for Africa and vanish, feared sold as slaves. In Iberia the Christian kings win the great victory of Las Navas de Tolosa.

diary.title: Battle of Muret
diary.details: Pedro II of Aragon, Raimond and the count of Foix take Muret, ten miles up the Garonne from Toulouse, with a great army. De Montfort crosses the marshes to fall on their flank: Pedro is killed and some ten thousand die in under half an hour, many drowning in the river, where their cries are still heard in flood. Resistance is broken for years, and Raimond seeks redress in Rome.

diary.title: Tribunal at Castra Solis
diary.details: The meeting set for Toulouse moves to Castra Solis, with de Montfort's army outside the city, to the Mercurians' annoyance. It is the most bitter gathering since the Schism War, taken up with the crusade and charges of meddling with mundanes: some blame Normandy magi, some Flambeau blame Tytalus for the crusade itself. Tolomae of Jerbiton calls for open Hermetic resistance and is thrown out of the debate, swearing revenge on the Mercurians and on the Coenobium. Aedes Mercurii threatens to walk out and so void the Tribunal, until Tibaut and the chief Redcap Alazais, who threatens to stop all Redcap service, avert anarchy. Senex is absent, and Tibaut acts as chief Quaesitor.

diary.title: Ruling: Tres acquitted
diary.details: Charges are brought against Tres for arming mercenaries with enchanted weapons, calling them his grogs, and using them to destroy Mistridge. However deplored, it was a lawfully declared Wizard's War and no ruling forbids grogs in one; the vote goes narrowly his way. Tres flees into hiding from Mistridge's friends, and after the meeting the Hermetic faidits begin to gather at Aguilar as the Ostal des Exiles, Rixenda of Mistridge first and Gilbert of Flambeau their leader.

diary.title: De Montfort enters Toulouse; Filii Sinapis abandoned
diary.details: Simon de Montfort enters Toulouse in triumph and takes up residence in the Château Narbonnais. The Waldensians are condemned as heretics, though Innocent III thought them good Christians. Filii Sinapis is abandoned in the wake of the crusade.

diary.title: Tolomae declared orbus; Tibaut confirmed
diary.details: House Jerbiton expels Tolomae of Bellaquin, leader of the Procrustean League, which calls for open war on the Church, and declares him orbus. He is suspected of the legate's murder and flees rather than answer the Quaesitor's questions. With Senex absent two years, Tibaut is confirmed as chief Quaesitor. In Toulouse an autumn rising is put down with great effort, and de Montfort names himself count of Toulouse.

diary.title: Raimond returns to Toulouse
diary.details:
While de Montfort campaigns in the north, Raimond slips back into Toulouse to the citizens' joy. De Montfort finds the gates shut against him and lays siege for months.

Secrets
Tibaut, who found the first threads of Senex's inquiry in his laboratory notes, begins this year to investigate the Tribunal's mystery cults, the Cathars and the sorginak, sharing his suspicions with his filia Beatrice. A letter he sent her lies in the satchel of a Redcap who died of crusaders' wounds along the Via Domitia.

diary.title: Tolomae Marched
diary.details: Early in the year Tolomae is Marched for repeatedly meddling with mundanes, and slain. His suspected supporters scatter among other covenants or hide among the faidits.

diary.title: Simon de Montfort killed
diary.details:
A stone from a siege engine on the walls of Toulouse strikes Simon de Montfort on the head and kills him. Amaury de Montfort claims his titles, and Alice remains a leader of the campaign, but Simon's great domain begins to fall apart.

Secrets
Some suspect the engine was one of those Tres built to destroy Mistridge.

diary.title: Wizard's Wars at Tolosa Paratge
diary.details:
In the weeks before de Montfort's death, Augustus of Tolosa Paratge, a senior Quaesitor, is persuaded by Bishop Foulques that Toulouse will fall and asks the covenant's Gorgiastic Cathars to leave for their safety. They refuse; Marc declares Wizard's War on him and, believing him possessed, kills him in the tower. Within the month St Tropez declares Wizard's War on the unresisting Marc and kills him. Under Mariola, the covenant splits into the Blacks, who hold it, and the Whites, who plot in the city to retake it.

Through the Aegis has the civil war already broken out by 1214, when it drove Alyssa from the covenant to Jardin.

diary.title: Siege of Marmande
diary.details: Soon after Christmas, Prince Louis's crusaders under Centule d'Astarac besiege Marmande.

diary.title: Tibaut dies
diary.details:
Tibaut, the Presiding Quaesitor, dies in the care of the monks of Saint Hilaire, taken for a Cathar by crusaders who later raid the abbey. His body is buried there and his belongings sit locked in the abbot's chest. At Dama's suggestion his filia Beatrice of Guernicus fills the office until the 1221 Tribunal. (The Hermetic culture chapter also says once that he died in 1214; the 1221 Tribunal takes 1219.)

Secrets
Warned by Luc of Ara Maxima Nova of Tibaut's questions, Dama ambushed him with Maju near the road to Foix. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus shattered his Parma, but Maju's venom worked slowly; he staggered into the road and divinely blessed crusader knights carried him to the abbey before she could reach him. Before he died he confided something to the knights.

diary.title: Marmande massacred; Toulouse besieged
diary.details: After nine months Marmande surrenders on terms. Amaury de Montfort, urged by the Bishop of Saintes, then kills all five thousand townsfolk and their beasts and burns the town. Prince Louis's royal crusade besieges Toulouse but withdraws when pestilence breaks out in his army, and Raimond begins to win back his county.

tribunals.secrets:
Fraxinetum Redux, the hidden successor of Fraxinetum on the Hyères islands, holds 3 votes it has never claimed, since the Tribunal does not know it exists.

The Praeco killed both of the last two Presiding Quaesitors. Senex, investigating her cult of Matres & Matrones, slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan in 1210 while she was away at an akelarre and was caught there; his death was lawful under the Code, but she hid it. Tibaut took up his trail, and in 1219 Dama and her familiar Maju ambushed him near the road to Foix, stripping his Parma with Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus; he died of the serpent's poison at the Abbey of Saint Hilaire, where crusaders had carried him, and his belongings are still locked in the abbot's chest. A letter he sent Beatrice by an Iberian Redcap lies in the satchel of the Redcap, who died of his wounds beside the Via Domitia. Dama bought the Chief Redcap's tacit support with a Longevity Ritual for Alazais's mundane lover. Beatrice is suspected of sympathy with the cult, and Alazais and Mariola of Tolosa Paratge are rumoured to be members.

The Tribunal next meets in summer 1221 at the ruins of Glanum, a neutral site agreed on by all; its first business is whether Beatrice of Guernicus succeeds Tibaut as Presiding Quaesitor. If the Tribunal resolves to act against the crusade and the Church, the Pyrenean covenants may boycott the meeting of 1227 and, with the four covenants a Tribunal needs, ask the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to let them secede. If the saga follows history, Guy de Montfort is killed near Castelnaudary in April 1220, James I of Aragon comes of age in 1223, the count of Foix defies Louis in 1226 and 1227, and the crusade ends in 1229.

Dama must renew her Longevity Ritual before 1232.

Fraxinetum Redux. Heirs of the raider covenant the Coenobium destroyed in 975, led by Ahmad ibn Nasr of Tytalus, keep a pirate base on the Hyères islands with two magi, a third aboard a ship, and still sponsor raids on the Provençal coast and on Catalan and Genoese shipping, steering clear of the Coenobium's fleet. They have never declared themselves for fear their ancestors' name would bring a Wizard's War; their three votes go unused. They oppose only a new maritime stronghold or an island covenant off the south coast.

The Drac of Beaucaire. The monster said to have returned beneath the Rhône is a Tytalus eremite, Aucassin, who never comes to Tribunal and lives as the merchant Rene of Dragonianum, ruling the town council by subtle Mentem magic. He has learned he is heir to the Drac's blood and seeks a Mystery that would make him a true elder Drac; he has kidnapped children and servants to serve him.

neighbours.name: The Fort at Belfort
neighbours.summary:
A rocky bluff in the vineyards a day south of Cahors, a mile from the Toulouse road, ringed by old earth ramparts that now terrace the vines. Within the crumbling walls of a Visigothic fort stand a red-brick library under a green copper dome and a golden brick tower, among lawns, sandy paths, pools, a fountain and shade trees, all laid out as one garden of colour and scent. Strange talking animals and butterflies that turn with the mood of those who rest there come and go; only clergy seem proof against the place, thinking of Eden.

The tower has four floors on a spiral stair: Serena's rooms and a guard chamber, Beatriz's laboratory, Joia's sanctum, and Joia's laboratory at the top. The guesthouse, the Montdumerc manor of red brick, has rooms for guests, four great bedchambers above, and at the top the sancta of Alyssa and Ahenobarbus. The brick kitchen doubles as a bakehouse. The other laboratories are stone buildings against the fort's walls. One corner, the bower, is a tangle of wild roses over mossy rocks, where lovers go and Joia sits sewing.

In the wall is a sky-blue door. From the corner of the eye it opens on high summer. It stays locked, and Joia keeps the key.

details.tethers: The Door Marked Summer, in the fort's wall, opens on the first level. The maze on that level leads to the second.

levels.name: The Summer Garden
levels.see: Through the corner of the eye, at the Door Marked Summer
levels.enter: Joia's key, given only to one she judges a true lover
levels.notes:
A walled garden that mirrors the fort: a great pool where the library stands, a maze of dark hedges at the tower, avenues of shade, statues of classical goddesses and the sun always high. Joia holds her masked entertainments here, dazzling her guests with open magic. The bower is here too, mirrored, deeper and stranger.

The pool, gone from the mundane world, is a strong initiatory site for Bjornaer with sanguine Heartbeasts, its mossy rocks holding Visigothic magic of an old shapechanging tradition; many shapechangers hold it holy.

The maze is Xenophanes's topiary. At its heart stands a tree of shining fruit that no mundane way can reach, and the fruit is deadly poison. To pass on, simply become lost in it.

levels.name: The Night Garden
levels.enter: Get lost in the maze of the Summer Garden
levels.notes:
A full moon over a warm night, distant walls, tangled briar and tree, paths among mossy rocks, bluebell clearings, and brooks that end in deep pools. The magi avoid it and do not tend it. Its shy, deadly monsters and strange beings take forms that suit the quester, and the book leaves them to the storyguide: several must be overcome on any quest.

The Lake: only one seeking a first Heart's Desire finds the path. Black, still water, with the bower on an island and a one-person boat with a paddle. Other ways across work, but leave the crosser alone. Some who entered the water have drowned for ever. Mist takes the crosser, and her own emotion attacks; True Love passes free.

Secrets
The fight's outcome. Dead: gone, perhaps drowned. Incapacitated: wakes in the Garden with a Major Flaw or two Minor (Curse of Venus, Fury, Low Self-Esteem, Lost Love; or Compulsion, Delusion, Depressed, Obsessed, Oversensitive, Pessimistic, Weakness, Weak Willed, Wrathful), and darker Traits. Worst wound Heavy, enemy beaten: one new Minor Personality Flaw of the player's choice, replacing like for like if the Trait fought was a Flaw. Medium: a Confidence Point, and the Flaw behind the Trait may go. Light: the same, with 3 Confidence Points. Unwounded: Self-Confident (a grog gains Confidence 1).

The Bower of Your Heart's Desire: on the island a pale maiden in noble dress kisses the quester once and whispers the secret, and she wakes in the bower of the Garden with it. The player chooses the Desire, which may bring a Personality Flaw and at most one Virtue. Those Tainted with Evil may find ghastly things. Perdo Mentem sometimes takes away what a broken quester learned. No magus knows if the Desire is true or a faerie ploy.

neighbours.secrets: The site was Magic until Joia built the troubadours' garden here. Over the last decade the song has taken hold: Magic gave way to Faerie, two strong Faerie regiones replaced the old magical ones, and the wild hilltop Androcles sought was tamed. It was once a Clan Maruhs ancestor site, where Panthera the Terrible was sometimes found.

neighbours.name: The Wood of the Highest Tree
neighbours.summary: A small faerie wood on a hilltop some sixteen miles east of Jardin, under a tall tree of a kind unknown in the region. Minor goblin fae harass anyone who walks in, so visitors usually reach the treetop by magic.

links.note: Jardin gathers the Highest Leaf here

neighbours.name: Belfort du Quercy
neighbours.summary:
A prosperous village of well-built cottages on the slopes a mile from the Toulouse road, grown round the manor the Montdumercs built in 1130. Most of its people are the covenant's folk, who tend market gardens, vines and sheep and who hold themselves Lady Joia's subjects. They know, or guess, that she is a magician, and keep it from outsiders. There is no inn, but cottagers will take a respectable traveller for a few coins.

Three-quarters are Cathars, the rest faithful to the Church, and the line runs through families without quarrel. Even the curé would shelter the heretics, and the Cathars file into church for the Bishop of Cahors's visitation to help him. The village has a Dominion aura of 1.

neighbours.name: Chapel of Saint Desiderius
neighbours.summary: A tiny red-brick chapel to the Merovingian bishop of Cahors, showing what the grape has earned. Father Augustine says Sunday mass to a small flock and hears confession at Easter, Christmas and the saint's day, November 15th. Every magus but Lexora comes on Easter Sunday. Dominion aura 2, 4 at the altar, 1 in the graveyard, where goats graze.

neighbours.name: The Unaud Barn
neighbours.summary: A barn of stone and wood by the Unaud house, where the Cathars have long prayed; hence its Dominion aura of 3. Raissa Unaud, the family's ancient matriarch, is a Perfecta and a good friend of Xenophanes, though she mildly disapproves of magic. Other Perfecti stay with the clan.

neighbours.name: Vazerac
neighbours.summary: A black-wine village west of Jardin with no lord: twelve consuls, men and women born there, run it. They know a little of the Order.

characters.name: Joia du Lua

invented_spells.name: Confusion of the Numbed Will
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

invented_spells.name: Piercing the Magical Veil
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
A very petite woman whose charms outlast her years, her hair always flecked with spring blossom. Casting sigil: the delicate perfume of summer flowers. Twilight Scars: flowers grow where she sleeps; she smells faintly of summer flowers; blossom appears in her hair. Her Longevity Ritual gives -6 to aging rolls. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack +1, Defense 0, Damage -2; gardening trowel Init -1, Attack +2, Defense -1, Damage -1. Soak 0.

Level of a General spell: Ward Against Faeries of the Wood 25, The Invisible Eye Revealed 15, Watching Ward 30.

Talisman: an iron gardening trowel with a hazel handle, capacity 20 pawns, 2 invested, 17 effect levels. Effect: Rope of Bronze (MuHe 17, Pen 0, 3 a day, Touch, Sun, Individual, as ArM5 p. 137). Attunements: +7 harm or repel faeries, +2 building, +3 divination.

characters.summary: First Maga and chatelaine in the eyes of the world, born Joia Montdumerc on this very ridge, and the most celebrated patroness of the troubadours. Over the years she has reshaped the covenant into the Garden of Love of their songs. A patriot of Occitania, she backs Count Raimond, stands quietly against the French and the de Montforts, and shelters faidits who love Toulouse. Many have adored her in fin amor; none has ever been her lover in fact. She treated her French-born apprentice Beatriz poorly for her birth. She alone holds the key to the Door Marked Summer.
characters.secrets: Her charmed look is sorcery, and the aura's turn to Faerie, which she did not mean, is her doing. Sooner or later her politics will bring armies down on the covenant, as they came to Bellaquin and Lariander. The magi hide the fates of questers she let into the Night Garden, altering memories where they must.

links.note: Writes to her on Courtly Love

characters.name: Lexora

invented_spells.name: Breath of Flames
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
A rough mane of uncontrollable blonde hair, brown eyes and a courtly gown. Casting sigil: warm sunlight; under Intellego Vim her spells wear a dazzling golden aura, and what they touch may feel warm or look brighter. Twilight Scars: she can eat only raw meat; she seems to grow when angry; her hair is a wild mane. Her Longevity Ritual gives -6 to aging rolls. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init +1, Defense +7; fist Init +1, Attack +7, Defense +6, Damage +3; kick Init 0, Attack +7, Defense +5, Damage +6. Soak +1.

Level of a General spell: Gather the Essence of the Beast 15, Aegis of the Hearth 20 (the errata's correction of the 15 printed). The book lists Fur That Turns Blades at 15 and Endurance of the Lion as ReCo in her block; their own entries give MuAn 20 and ReAn 20.

Sensory Magic: Sound and Spectacle are Targets from that Mystery (Sound, all who hear the caster; Spectacle, all who see her), which only those Initiated can design or cast.

Lioness form, Size +2: Int +1, Per 0, Pre +1, Com 0, Str +6, Sta +3, Dex +2, Qik +1. The shape adds Ferocity (self-defense), Tough and Weakness (submission). Qualities: Aggressive, Ambush Predator, Crafty, Good Jumper, Hardy, Imposing Appearance, Large Claws, Large Teeth, Tough Hide, Vocal. Claws Init +1, Attack +15, Defense +12, Damage +10; bite Init +1, Attack +13, Defense +9, Damage +9. Soak +8 (+2 from Tough Hide). Fatigue OK, 0/0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Changed Abilities: Area Lore: County of Toulouse 1 (7) (wilds), Athletics 5 (pouncing), Awareness 2 (smell), Brawl 5+2 (1) (claws), Hunt 4 (deer), Stealth 4 (stalking), Survival 5 (arid climates). Weak Magic Resistance does not apply in this form. Add 2 to her casting totals in it, from Stamina.

With Lion of Outlandish Size she is Size +3, Str +8, Qik 0: claws Init +1, Attack +15, Defense +11, Damage +12; bite Init +1, Attack +13, Defense +8, Damage +11.

characters.summary: Second Maga, and furious to be so: slightly older than Joia and Gauntleted with her, but outranked by family. A proud Bjornaer of Clan Maruhs, lioness in heart, she opposes whatever Joia proposes and roams the country in beast shape to wear off her temper. She holds Androcles's site sacred and despises the Garden and its faeries, but she and Joia grew up together and quarrel like sisters who would close ranks against an outsider. She has Initiated Sensory Magic (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 27) and means to visit Crintera for more. Her paganism is a vague classical one, and she bows to no one. Her Heart's Desire, to rule over magi: first Jardin, then a Tribunal as Praeco, then House Bjornaer as Prima. Only Hypatia's friendship keeps her and Xenophanes speaking.
characters.secrets: She alone sees the threat in Serena, and suspects her of sympathy with the crusade. She talks at Ara Maxima Nova as if Joia were mad and dangerous, and secretly copied Joia's tractatus on viticulture for them.

links.note: She is friends with his covenant

invented_spells.name: Piercing the Magical Veil
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
A white-haired, ruddy man in bright peasant clothes, boots, leather gloves and a wide-brimmed hat, with a scarf to hide the tattoos on his neck; fifteen tattoos cover him in all. Casting sigil: a soft feeling of bliss, which even things his spells touch seem to share. Twilight Scars: his tattoos writhe and change; a leaf or blade of grass in his hair comes back whenever removed; cats befriend him at once; people feel calm near him; he purrs loudly in his sleep; vis on his person crackles and glows. His Longevity Ritual gives -6 to aging rolls, -5 in his unhealthy laboratory. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0. Soak +3. He carries a small bronze sickle.

From the Path of Walking Backwards (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp. 70-71): Gentle Gift from the Avenue of Surrender and the Station of Service to Harmony; Pious and Vow from the Avenue of Healing and the Station of Rice and Honey; Free Expression and Inspirational from the Avenue of Adulation and the Station of Expression, by which Enigmatic Wisdom can replace Craft: Flower Arranging.

Level of a General spell: Disenchant 25, Demon's Eternal Oblivion 10, The Invisible Eye Revealed 15, Aegis of the Hearth 20, Watching Ward 25. The book calls The Healthy Vine Health of the Vine here, and lists Detect the Gift at 15 here and at 20 under Joia.

Talisman: a small bronze sickle, 7 pawns invested, 60 effect levels. Effects: Well Without Light (PeIg 25, Pen 0, 1 a day, Touch, Sun, Structure, ArM5 p. 142); Break the Hard Soil (ReTe 7, Pen 0, 6 a day, Touch, Momentary, Part: readies a circle of soil 15 paces across); Beckoning in the Unwelcome Twilight (CrVi 25, Pen +20, 1 a day, Touch, Momentary, Individual: two Warping Points to the one touched, and a Twilight roll for a magus). Attunements: +3 Terram, +5 Darkness, +2 Harvesting. These bonuses are in the book's totals for his Terram spells.

characters.summary: The fool of a Criamon experiment in teaching wisdom to the simple: highly educated, capable in the laboratory, and without common sense, trained at the Cave of Twisting Shadows and sent to the Tribunal in 1179. A gentle soul who tends the garden by moonlight while his familiar Hypatia prowls beside him and keeps him out of trouble. His Heart's Desire was a True Friend, and he found her. He is fond of the local Cathars and has written on them, but each time he nears renouncing his House for the Gorgiastic Cathars he talks to Father Augustine and comes away too muddled to leave the Church. He stands at the third station of the Path of Walking Backwards.
characters.secrets: Two of his three books could bring the Church down on Jardin.

links.note: Sister in the same parens, who detests him

characters.name: Beatriz

description.biography:
A plain woman who wears her dark hair in a severe bun, never smiles, and changes her looks by magic as her mood shifts. Casting sigil: an absence of red, drained from all her spells touch; she cannot create true red by magic, though ruddy skin is allowed. Twilight Scars: her reflection never quite matches her; red things fade at her touch. Her Longevity Ritual gives -5 to aging rolls. Encumbrance 0 (burden 1).

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack -2, Defense 0, Damage +1; kick Init -1, Attack -2, Defense -1, Damage +4; short sword Init +1, Attack +1, Defense +1, Damage +6. Soak +1.

Level of a General spell: Sight of the True Form 10, Gather the Essence of the Beast 15.

Talisman: a simple wooden necklace with an amber bead carved with a crown, worn at all times, 7 pawns invested, 54 effect levels. Effects: The Ever Changing Guise (MuIm 14, Pen 0, 12 a day, Personal, Sun, Individual, as Disguise of the New Visage; outside the covenant she never appears as herself, and she spares the night and her sanctum, so it does not warp her); The Invisible Eye Revealed (InVi 25, Pen 0, 1 a day, Personal, Concentration, Touch, shows scrying up to level 50); Whispers Through The Black Gate (InCo(Me) 15, Pen 0, 1 a day, Touch, Concentration, Individual). Attunements: +3 Corpus, +4 affect breathing and speaking, +4 affect dead wood. These bonuses are in the book's totals for her spells marked T: Bind Wound, Sight of the True Form, Rise of the Feathery Body, Endurance of the Berserkers, Conjure the Sturdy Vine.

characters.summary: Joia's French-born former apprentice, who stayed on at the covenant though the two despise each other. She escaped the massacre at Béziers in 1209, and a few years ago quested for her Heart's Desire, fought her own stubbornness on the Lake as a magic mule, and lost. She is the broken thing the quest left: bitter, friendless by choice, taking and discarding lovers in a mockery of fin amor. Most of the magi pity her. She is obsessed with old shapeshifters and backs Ahenobarbus when he seeks reform, though she mistrusts Serena.
characters.secrets: She claims a terrible vision of Tolosa Paratge's future and will not tell it. Her failure let Skullface slip through the Aegis.

characters.name: Ahenobarbus

invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
Casting sigil: zig-zag lines; even his Circle spells show jagged edges under Intellego Vim, and his earthworks zig-zag sharply. Twilight Scar: people feel slightly awed after talking to him. His Longevity Ritual gives -6 to aging rolls. He wears wizardly robes. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +3; kick Init -2, Attack +4, Defense +1, Damage +3; dagger Init -1, Attack +7, Defense +3, Damage +3. Soak +2.

Mighty Viper's Gaze is Viper's Gaze raised a magnitude for animals up to Size +4. The book lists The Tremere Trench at 25 in his block and 20 in its entry, and The Shrouded Glen at 45. Level of a General spell: Watching Ward 20.

Talisman: a wand tipped with amber, with a hollow in the handle for an Arcane Connection to his laboratory, 9 pawns invested, 86 effect levels. Effects: The Touch Of Morpheus (ReMe 47, Pen +64, 24 a day, Touch, Sun, Individual, a Touch version of The Call to Slumber); Take Me Home! (ReCo 39, Pen +8, 1 a day, Personal, Momentary, Individual, as The Leap of Homecoming). Attunements: wand +4 control things at a distance; amber +3 Corpus. These bonuses are in the book's totals for his spells marked T: all his Corpus, Herbam, Terram and Rego Mentem spells but Aura of Rightful Authority and The Shrouded Glen, and Mighty Viper's Gaze.

The Collars of Slavery: two small iron collars, invested devices of Enslave the Mortal Mind (ReMe 44, Pen 0, 2 a day, Environmental Trigger, Touch, Sun, Individual). The wearer has no will of his own and takes any suggestion, and remembers it all once freed. One is for captives, who then lose the memory to his spells; the other he may give to Protendus.

characters.summary: A Rego specialist of ambition, trained for war by indirection, who has enslaved hedge wizards and dabbled in necromancy, and made enemies by both. Sent to the Tribunal in 1209 after Lariander fell, to help covenants hide and hold, he found Jardin badly exposed and has improved its grogs' armour and made the Shield of Dismissal. He thinks the Garden a reckless folly and wants to steer clear of crusaders and southern lords alike. He is smitten with Serena. He has never entered the Night Garden.
characters.secrets: Coeris sent him to prove Protendus incompetent, for his parens Janus's politics at home; his parens holds his sigil, and he avoids reporting to Protendus for as long as he can. Serena's love is real, but he has not seen how far her ambition goes. He agrees with her that Lexora and Xenophanes should be eased out of the Tribunal, and that Jardin should side with the Whites and expel its heretics.

links.note: His regional commander, whom he avoids
