description.biography:
A petite woman of almost childlike looks, with a kind smile and hazel hair and eyes. She travels in practical men's clothes and around the covenant wears a tatty black cloak and a peacock-feathered hat over a peasant's dress. Casting sigil: the smell of goat's cheese. Twilight Scar: goats find her Gift pleasant and calming. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense +3; kick Init -1, Attack +2, Defense +1, Damage +3. Soak +1.

Level of a General spell: Gather the Essence of the Beast 15.

Talisman: a golden ring on her right hand, 10 pawns invested, 24 effect levels. Effect: Endure Pain & Fatigue (ReCo 24, Pen 0, 12 a day, Touch, Diameter, as Endurance of the Berserkers), which she gives to grogs when a fight looks near. Attunements: +4 affect wealth, +2 constant effect.

reputations.name: Trouble on two legs (Order of Hermes)

characters.summary: A cheerful maga Trianomae, born noble near Narbonne and taken as an apprentice at nine, who roams France and Iberia settling local problems and seeking out Islamic wizards; her Gentle Gift opens doors, and her meddling has annoyed a couple of covenants. She reached Jardin in 1214 after the civil war at Tolosa Paratge, her former home, and is last in precedence. She usually votes with Xenophanes, for her soft spot for odd magi and for the Cathars, dislikes Serena's cruelty, and respects Lexora enough to back her against Joia. She wants peace at home and has not yet quested.
characters.secrets: She has been scrying the Whites unseen and means to force a way into the regio to save the Gorgiastic Cathars. She raids the Whites' vis, a flat breach of the Code, and holds 30 or more pawns of it to tempt magi into Wizard's War against Carolus St. Tropez, with whom she is in love.

links.note: Her enemy and her secret love

characters.name: Serena Montdumerc

description.biography:
Pale-skinned and auburn-haired, a great beauty who looks like Joia yet is still outshone by her. Noble clothing in the latest styles. Worth 6 Build Points to the covenant. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack 0, Defense 0, Damage 0; kick Init -1, Attack 0, Defense -1, Damage +3. Soak 0.

characters.summary: Joia's niece, born in 1189 to Esquiva and the merchant Ramundus, last of the Montdumerc line and heir to the lady's title. She serves as autocrat from rooms on the tower's ground floor, and takes her frustration out on the covenfolk with threats and rages. Vain, she bitterly resents Joia's beauty.
characters.secrets: Her Heart's Desire is to take back her rightful home and title from the magi. She may yet turn to crusaders or southern lords to do it, and only her love for Ahenobarbus, whom she pretends is her pawn, holds her back.

characters.name: Rosamonde Unaud

description.biography:
Still a muscular woman, though her greying hair and creaking bones show her age. Worth 8 Build Points to the covenant. Her Heart's Desire: to live out her years at Belfort du Quercy.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +5; fist Init -1, Attack +4, Defense +4, Damage +2; kick Init -2, Attack +4, Defense +3, Damage +5; dagger Init -1, Attack +6, Defense +4, Damage +5; javelin Init -1, Attack +7, Defense +5, Damage +7; pole axe Init +2, Attack +14, Defense +11, Damage +10; short bow Init -2, Attack +8, Defense +5, Damage +7. Soak +10, in Full Chain Mail (Protection 9). Encumbrance 3 (burden 4). She carries six arrows.

characters.summary: Captain of the turb, slowing with arthritis, who holds on for want of a woman to succeed her and will not go more than a day from home.

characters.name: John the Gardener

description.biography: The book prints only his Communication and Abilities. Worth 5 Build Points to the covenant.

characters.summary: A cheerful, handsome young man with an eye for the ladies, who keeps the gardens and treats the magi as his equals. Serena has a soft spot for him. His big ginger tom is Auranja.

characters.name: Bohella the Librarian

description.biography: The book names these two among her many Abilities, with her Communication. Worth 9 Build Points to the covenant.

characters.summary: Librarian for twenty-five years, watching every visitor from her little desk. Only Joia and Lexora know the covenant's past better. She gets about two seasons' study a year from the mundane books, and the covenant keeps her as Wealthy.

characters.name: Sicart the Scribe

description.biography: The book prints only these and his Communication. Worth 11 Build Points to the covenant.

characters.summary: A short-sighted former tinker and grog, who makes the inks, vellum and bindings in his old pots and pans and teaches the scribe's trade.

rooms.name: Top of the tower
rooms.description: Humbert's, renovated: a circular room 25 feet across and 500 square feet, under the dome, its high carved beams brightly painted, a glazed window over the Garden of Love, flowers heady everywhere, and all immaculately kept. Virtues: Elevated, Highly Organized, Superior Construction, Lesser Feature (Lofty Ceiling), Lesser Feature (Window), Potted Plants. Four fewer botch dice, as printed. Cost 30 Build Points.

rooms.name: Against the fort's wall
rooms.description: A filthy menagerie of a place, with birds in the rafters, cats and dogs by the fire, a small pond and a pen for wolves, boars or a stag, and in truth perfectly ordered. Virtues: Highly Organized, Lesser Feature (Animal Pen), Menagerie. Flaw: Dirty. One fewer botch die; -1 to Recovery in a year of two seasons here. Cost 20 Build Points.

rooms.name: Against the fort's wall
rooms.description: Austere: he sleeps here on a straw mat beside a single stool. Flaw: Living Quarters. -2 to Recovery and -1 to aging rolls. Cost 10 Build Points.

rooms.name: Second floor of the tower
rooms.description: The room of her apprenticeship, its murals painted over, spotless and spare, with a bed, table and chairs, and a magnificent full-length curved mirror that subtly distorts. Virtues: Highly Organized, Spotless, Greater Feature (Mirror). Flaws: Living Quarters, Missing Equipment (Binding Familiar, Teaching), Missing Ingredients (Perdo), Undecorated. No binding a familiar or teaching here; Perdo totals are halved until supplies come from Toulouse or Cahors, a few days' work. -1 to Recovery. Cost 10 Build Points.

rooms.name: Between Xenophanes's and Lexora's
rooms.description: A standard laboratory in every respect, not yet improved.

rooms.name: Near the main gate
rooms.description: Very ordinary, personalized to the usual standard; she travels too much to improve it, and might lend it, at a price in favours.

rooms.name: Against the fort's wall
rooms.description: A stone building like the others, stocked as a standard laboratory, for visiting magi or a new recruit.

rooms.name: Against the fort's wall
rooms.description: Very basic: -3 to Laboratory Totals as it stands, put right by a season's work. The two guest laboratories cost 100 Build Points.

creatures.name: The Emotion on the Lake
creatures.appearance: An allegory of what bars the quester from Love: a knight in red armor for wrath, a succubus for lust, a green-eyed monster for envy.
creatures.notes:
Built from the Personality Trait the player judges the greatest obstacle (or Intelligence, as Reason, if none fits): Initiative equal to the Trait, Attack 3 times it, Defense 9 + it, Damage equal to it, Soak it + 1. No Fatigue Levels; Body Levels OK, 0 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Dead (16+).

An ordinary fight in which spells can be cast, but hand to hand. The quester uses weapon statistics, without the weapon Ability: any Ability, Virtue or Trait that opposes the emotion stands in (a Minor Virtue counts 3, a Major 9). Armor gives no Protection; Soak and shields work.

Beatriz, Stubborn +3, met a mule: Init +3, Attack +9, Defense +12, Damage +3, Soak +4. Her Minor Magical Focus stood in for Single Weapon at 3, and she lost.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 58

creatures.name: Panthera the Terrible
creatures.appearance: An immense, red-toothed predator.
creatures.notes: A Great Beast of Clan Maruhs. The book gives no statistics.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal pp. 41, 44
creatures.secrets: A lion-heartbeast Bjornaer who took the pool from shapeshifters in the early tenth century, then passed into Final Twilight here. Androcles came hunting this ancestor site, and Lexora means to seek him for the House's Inner Mysteries. He may return and find his pool corrupted.

creatures.name: Skullface
creatures.appearance: Her true form is unknown; a loved one's face turns to a hideous skull.
creatures.notes: A relatively powerful spirit of the County of Toulouse. She makes a loved face look like a skull to her victim, drives the pair apart with her Guide power, then helps a new love of equal strength to grow. Some Merinita say she is why fortunetellers read death as change. The book gives no statistics.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 67
creatures.secrets: She escaped through the Aegis on the night Beatriz failed, and has come back to Jardin for a new victim.

creatures.name: Auranja
creatures.appearance: A big ginger tom who basks on the stable roof.
creatures.notes: John the Gardener's cat, a magical cat of unknown powers and Hypatia's lover. The book gives no statistics.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 46
creatures.secrets: A power lets him walk through the Door Marked Summer, and he gossips with the cats of the region about what he hears there.

creatures.name: Tibout
creatures.notes: The magical cat companion of the bearded minstrel Izarns. The book gives no statistics.
creatures.source: Faith & Flame: The Provençal Tribunal p. 46
creatures.secrets: He tells his master the low gossip he picks up from cats.

creatures.name: Hypatia

powers.name: Aura of Rightful Authority
powers.description: Inclines humans to obey and steadies them at the shock of a talking cat (ArM5 p. 151).

powers.name: Humans Are Easily Misplaced
powers.description: A feline Inexorable Search (ArM5 p. 131), by a map of scents and textures; she rubs on humans to mark them. 4 Mastery points reduced its Might cost.

powers.name: Master of the Undergrowth
powers.description: A feline Intuition of the Forest (ArM5 p. 136).

powers.name: Pass the Unyielding Portal
powers.description: For doors with no human to open them (ArM5 p. 137).

powers.name: Prying Eyes
powers.description: Looks inside buildings, a cat on the roof seeing through it (ArM5 p. 144).

powers.name: The Wise Guide
powers.description: Nudges Xenophanes to act sensibly, as if he had Common Sense, with no compulsion and no Warping, being tailored to him. ReMe 30 (base 5, +2 Voice, +1 Concentration, +2 Group; 3 Mastery points on cost, 1 on Init).

creatures.appearance: An unremarkable female black cat with a snub nose, green eyes and a kink in her tail, older and leaner than the village cats.
creatures.notes: A sardonic commentator with far more wits than her magus. Vis: 2 pawns of Vim. Bond: Mental Communication, both ways, complex thoughts, unlimited; Speech, unlimited and maintaining concentration, which Xenophanes can withdraw for a time. She knows not to speak before visitors unless they wear red caps. Awareness carries +2 from Puissant Awareness.

creatures.name: Nec

powers.name: Theft of Voice
powers.description: Steals the voice of a human who meets her eye until the next sunrise, as The Captive Voice (ArM5 p. 147).

powers.name: Eyes Like Lanterns
powers.description: Holding eye contact, paralyzes a victim who fails a Brave roll against 9; if attacked, shaken or distracted he may roll against 6 each round to break free. ReMe 10 (base 4, +1 Eye, +1 Concentration).

powers.name: Leave No Trace
powers.description: She leaves no tracks when running, as The Trackless Step (ArM5 p. 155).

creatures.appearance: A magnificent white she-wolf with large eyes, far bigger than any natural wolf.
creatures.notes: Of the white wolves of Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 129. She came from Transylvania to escape trouble in her pack, which may yet follow; she allows Ahenobarbus no superiority and longs to outdo Lexora's heartbeast. She leads a small wolf pack that spies for him, and the villagers think her a big friendly dog. She understands Latin and South Slavonic but cannot speak them. Careless with Stealth is from Grogs p. 77. Vis: 2 pawns of Animal in her tail. Bond: Mental Communication, both ways, complex thoughts, unlimited.

creatures.name: Fauconrouge

powers.name: Human Shape
powers.description: Takes human shape (Realms of Power: Magic p. 39).

powers.name: Iron Grip of the Raptor
powers.description: Handles and carries things as with human hands and Strength +5, concentrating for anything but carrying, even to let go. ReTe 15 (base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Const); Personal Power of 15 levels, cost reduced by 2.

creatures.appearance: A magnificent red gyrfalcon.
creatures.notes: Fish Out of Water (flying) is from Grogs p. 80. Vis: 5 pawns of Corpus in his talons. Bond: Mental Communication, constant, complex images and emotions. Binding Total 35.

enchanted_devices.name: Shield of Dismissal
enchanted_devices.description: A shield embossed with panpipes in gold leaf, carried by the grog at the gate, made by Ahenobarbus. Those of rank or wealth are always let in; troublemakers, nobodies, the French and friends of the crusade are sent away. Cost 15 Build Points.

effects.name: Subtle Shift of the Intended Destination
effects.description: The user slaps the panpipes and calls to visible targets, who feel the urge to leave the covenant and seek some place dear to them, and later recall meaning to come but not why they did not. ReMe 37 with its uses (base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group; +2 for 3 a day).

was.title: Regional Tribunals created
was.details: As the Order grows, the Second Grand Tribunal sets up regional Tribunals, made of covenants that lie near one another rather than of lands with fixed borders. The rules for founding and governing them come out of a quarrel over Val-Negra's charter: Flambeau wanted lordship over every covenant his home helped to found.

was.title: Val-Negra recognized
was.details: After years of argument between Flambeau and Guernicus over its charter, the covenant of Val-Negra in the Pyrenees is formally recognized, and a regional Tribunal forms around it. Flambeau is the only Founder to make his home there, though Trianoma and Mercere visit often. Tolosa Paratge, a large Diedne covenant in a lake regio at Toulouse, is one of the four first covenants of the new Tribunal, and most of the region's other covenants belong to House Diedne.

was.title: Gelon becomes Primus of Verditius
was.details: Gelon, the first apprentice of Verditius, becomes Primus of his House. He lives for decades at Val-Negra, forging his famous enchanted swords, and his followers go on to found the Confraternity of Roland.

was.title: Kaeso joins House Flambeau
was.details: The Christian wizard Kaeso, whose power rests on an old underground temple of Mithras by the Garonne, joins House Flambeau. Training under Apromor and Flambeau in the Pyrenees, he forms the Hoplites, soldier-magi who hurl Pilum of Fire from behind a strong Parma Magica, and leads many of them into the Legion of Mithras. Many count him the first Hoplite.

was.title: Apromor becomes Primus of Flambeau
was.details: Apromor, the Founder's first apprentice, who has drifted from his master's ways, becomes the first Primus of House Flambeau, and Kaeso's Hoplites carry on Flambeau's war against the sahirs of Iberia. Apromor welcomes pagan and non-Hermetic wizards into the Order, works with Priamitus of Mercere to revive the Cult of Mercury from the last Roman priests of the region, and spreads Val-Negra's outposts across the Pyrenees.

was.title: Portus Cottiae and Yf founded
was.details: Julius Donnus, an outcast Mercurian of House Flambeau from the Greater Alps, founds Portus Cottiae outside Briançon as a second home for the revived Cult of Mercury, after Harco. It becomes the first Mercer House of the region and grows into a covenant of several sites, with chapter houses at Gap, Chorges and Embrun and a post at Oulx guarding the passes. In the same year Diedne magi found Yf on an island off the coast of Arelat.

was.title: Lapurdum founded
was.details: Flambeau magi found Lapurdum where the Adour meets the sea in Gascony, around a mithraeum in what was once a Roman army camp.

was.title: Campus Elysii founded
was.details: A small group of spirit masters, necromancers of Ex Miscellanea, settles in the crypts of the Alyscamps at Arles as the covenant of Campus Elysii.

was.title: Vikings on the Garonne
was.details: King Pepin II of Aquitaine, seeking freedom from Charles the Bald, is accused of apostasy for letting the Viking Jarl Oscar sail his raiders up the Garonne to Toulouse. Northmen camp all along the western coast, and Marseilles has already been sacked by Arab pirates (838); Byzantine freebooters (849) and Normans based in the Camargue follow. Tales of rune-wizards among the raiders finally draw the magi in, and Flambeau comes to resent how little the Diedne do to help.

was.title: Castra Solis founded
was.details: Raids on Gascon villages have grown since 840, and the Flambeau wrongly believe an organized Order of Odin is behind them. Kaeso returns to Bordeaux and fortifies his temple as a covenant, Castra Solis, the encampment of the sun, under the sign of a quartered sun.

was.title: Bordeaux falls to the Northmen
was.details: Before the Hoplites can do more than raise hasty defences, the northern pagans take Bordeaux. Unwilling to harm the townsfolk, the magi spend five years trying to end the war by force against the rune-wizards alone, and many die in their traps, Kaeso among them.

was.title: Sinapis founded
was.details: With Bordeaux too near the front, the surviving Flambeau build a fortified covenant, Sinapis, further north in Anjou. Castra Solis becomes a camp of tents for quick strikes, and to outsiders it looks like an offshoot of Sinapis.

was.title: Lapurdum abandoned
was.details: Worn down by Viking raids and quarrels among its magi, Lapurdum is given up. Its ruins lie somewhere under the city of Bayonne.

was.title: Seven Tribunals defined
was.details: The Grand Tribunal draws up seven regional Tribunals. Val-Negra goes to the Iberian Tribunal, along with the mountains and the Basque lands north of them; the bulk of France goes to the West Franks, and a strip from Friesland through Burgundy to Arelat forms the Lotharingian Tribunal.

was.title: Fraxinetum founded
was.details: Two Tytalan war-magi, Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda (who called himself a Flambeau, though the House denies him) and his lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf, settle in the Massif des Maures above St Tropez with a band of Andalusian raiders. Their covenant, named for the ash groves Sayyid planted, stays hidden from the Tribunal for its first century while it backs Moorish attacks on Provençal towns.

was.title: Barbegal founded
was.details: Three Verditius mage-smiths found a covenant in the Roman watermill complex of Barbegal, just north of Arles.

was.title: Lotharingia divided
was.details: The Grand Tribunal hands the northern covenants of the Lotharingian Tribunal to Normandy or the Rhine. What is left, the Kingdom of Arles along the Rhône and a few covenants in the Toulousain (a Mercer House at Arles, a strong Diedne covenant at Lyon, and a handful of others), comes to be called the Provençal Tribunal.

was.title: The Birds of Camargue founded
was.details: Bjornaer magi found a covenant in the marshes at the mouth of the Rhône.

was.title: Portus Cottiae overrun
was.details: Berber mountaineers overrun the scattered sites of Portus Cottiae, one of the first Lotharingian covenants to fall to the Saracens. Its magi flee down the Durance; at the motherhouse near Briançon the defenders bring the mountain down on the raiders and bury themselves in their own sancta. The one surviving maga, Anaïs of Jerbiton, reaches Avignon and becomes a loud voice for the Hermetic league that becomes the Coenobium.

was.title: Yf falls
was.details: The Diedne covenant of Yf falls to the raids of Fraxinetum. One of its magae later joins the Coenobium to avenge it, but her line dies out shortly before the Schism War.

was.title: Barbegal abandoned
was.details: The undefended mills of Barbegal are abandoned under Saracen raiding. The surviving smiths help to found the Rhône covenant of Coenobium Rhodanien.

was.title: Askelarre founded
was.details: A coven of Hermetic sorginak, Basque witches spread across the Basque country, founds the covenant of Askelarre.

was.title: Sorginak join Ex Miscellanea; Donjon Leyre founded
was.details: A few sorginak at last join House Ex Miscellanea, resented by their hedge sisters and anxious to keep their distance from the Diedne, who had long taken sorginak into their own House. In the same year Donjon Leyre, an early vassal of Montverte, is founded at the fork of the Leyre in the Landes as a base for raids into the Basque Pyrenees.

was.title: The Birds of Camargue merge into the Coenobium
was.details: Threatened by Fraxinetum, the Bjornaer of the Birds of Camargue join the wider league of Rhône magi that becomes the Coenobium Rhodanien.

was.title: Maieul of Cluny captured
was.details: The Moors of the Massif des Maures capture and ransom Maieul, abbot of Cluny, and push into the foothills of the Alps. The alarm this raises moves the mostly Jerbiton magi of eastern Provence to band together in a pact of mutual defence. Working through their families, churchmen and noble allies, they quietly back the army of William I of Provence, which routs the Moors at Tourtour.

was.title: Fraxinetum destroyed
was.details:
William's army takes the Moorish base and the Fraxinetum magi vanish into the forest. The history chapter says the Coenobium Rhodanien, which it calls newly formed (the Birds of Camargue had joined it in 970), destroyed the covenant by Wizard's War; the Arelat chapter says no war was ever openly declared and the league narrowly escaped the Quaesitors' anger for acting through mundane arms. Either way, the victors stay together as a covenant of many sites along the Rhône and the coast. In the same year Anaïs of Toulouse, a renegade Criamon expelled from her House, brings her followers, the Gorgiastic Cathars, into House Ex Miscellanea.

Secrets
The Fraxinetum magi did not perish. Their heirs live on in secret as Fraxinetum Redux on the Hyères islands, never declared to the Tribunal.

was.title: Grand Tribunal: the Northmen driven out
was.details: At the Grand Tribunal the Hoplites declare the rune-wizards rooted out of the region after more than a century of war: all three Danish settlements on the coast have been burned. Many of their fortified outposts, such as the tower at Mimizan, later grow into covenants counted as offshoots of Castra Solis. The Diedne, uneasy with the Mithraic piety of the Hoplites, took no part, which deepens Flambeau's suspicion of them.

was.title: Donjon Leyre falls
was.details: All the founding magi of Donjon Leyre die fighting in the Schism War, which rages through Gascony as Val-Negra's forces storm the Diedne covenants one after another; many Gascon Diedne burn their own sites and flee.

was.title: Campus Elysii driven out
was.details:
The spirit masters of Campus Elysii, who hid underground through the war, are forced out of the Alyscamps when the Coenobium stirs up the townsfolk with tales of diabolists under the necropolis. They try to begin again in a cave network in the Verdon gorge as Portus Termini, but all contact is lost before the next Tribunal and the new covenant is never registered.

Secrets
Many suspect that Hoplites in the Coenobium's pay hunted down the survivors.

was.title: Askelarre destroyed
was.details: The sorginak covenant of Askelarre is destroyed in the Schism War. Two of Val-Negra's magi, the Flambeau Leo Augustus and the Tremere Vegetius, die in the attack.

was.title: The fall of Val-Negra
was.details:
As the Schism War draws to its close, while its zealous magi are away striking at the Diedne, five Diedne archmagi storm Val-Negra. Of twenty-five magi at the war's start, only four are left. Shortly before the war many of its Flambeau had left, after a vision, to found Aedes Mercurii in Val-Negra's outlying halls; now the survivors join it, and it declares itself a Provençal covenant and the heir of Val-Negra. Many other covenants change to the Provençal Tribunal at this time, partly to keep Tytalus from claiming the spoils of the fallen Diedne. The domus magna of Flambeau moves to Castra Solis, and the Quaesitors strike nine or more Diedne sites from the records. Why Val-Negra was never rebuilt, and even where it stood, is soon forgotten.

Secrets
The Diedne reached the Iron Door in the depths of Val-Negra, and in the fighting the Adulteration of Flambeau was loosed. It killed three defenders and all the attackers before the last two archmagi forced it back and sealed the door with a Hermetic ward, one that breaks if the door is simply opened. The Quaesitors kept it quiet and ruled that Val-Negra must never rise again.

was.title: Bellaquin founded
was.details: As the Schism War dies down, Flambeau magi restore an abandoned castle, the Château de Penne in Tarn above the Aveyron, as a stronghold. The war ends before it is needed, and they hand it to House Jerbiton, who make it one of the most admired covenants in the Order and, in time, the lords of a fief of their own.

was.title: Mistridge founded
was.details: A covenant is founded in the Val du Bosque, in a tower raised by magic at the brink of a sheer drop.

was.title: Windgraven founded
was.details: Necromancers found Windgraven in the squat stone towers of a ruined Visigothic fort on a rocky plateau in the southern part of the County of Toulouse.

was.title: Filii Sinapis founded
was.details: Flambeau magi from the abandoned Normandy covenant of Sinapis found Filii Sinapis.

was.title: Berinor founded
was.details: Jerbiton magi found Berinor, a small covenant in the County of Toulouse that becomes a patron of troubadours and trobairitz.

was.title: Gascony joins the Provençal Tribunal
was.details: When the Normandy Tribunal splits, Castra Solis leads a faction into the enlarged Provençal Tribunal. The magi of Sinapis leave their site to join the domus magna, and smaller covenants of the area, Mimizan among them, come too.

was.title: Bentalone founded
was.details: A covenant is founded in a castle in the Toulousain; it stays in Summer for a century.

was.title: Grand Tribunal: the Occitan border
was.details: To settle quarrels between Normandy and the newly enlarged Provençal Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal rules that the border between them runs wherever Occitan stops being spoken. Unpopular at first, the rule is soon embraced by the southern magi to secure their claims to vis, and the Tribunal's minutes and proclamations are written in both Latin and Occitan.

was.title: The Golden Court at Beaucaire
was.details:
Count Henry II of Provence holds a festival in the meadows north of Beaucaire to mark the reconciliation of the Duke of Narbonne and the King of Aragon. A chronicler praises its hundred thousand knights, its gold sown in the earth and its herds roasted over wax torches.

Secrets
Most of the knights were faeries revelling in the troubadours' spirit of foolishness, and the gold was glamour; the meadow still holds Faerie vis.

was.title: Saint Jean Pied-de-Port razed
was.details: When Richard the Lionheart sacks Saint Jean Pied-de-Port, the large outpost Aedes Mercurii kept there is lost; its covenfolk had already fallen under the townsfolk's suspicion of witchcraft.

was.title: Miniata Sophia founded
was.details: A Criamon eremite founds Miniata Sophia in the cave system of Niaux, about forty years before 1220. For a decade and more it keeps to itself.

was.title: Lariander founded
was.details: Tremere magi found Lariander, a young covenant in a faerie wood near the village of Montgey in the Toulousain.

was.title: Tribunal: Miniata Sophia announced
was.details: Miniata Sophia makes itself known at the Tribunal and registers its site, the village of Niaux, with the Redcaps. It has attended every meeting since, voting on each question as seems most apt or abstaining, and making no alliances.

was.title: Ara Maxima Nova founded
was.details: Merinita magi who have explored the labours of Heracles in the east come west to follow the rest of his journey and found Ara Maxima Nova among the vineyards outside Perpignan, close to the Via Domitia. Their charter binds them to seek the Hesperides every five years.

was.title: Windgraven destroyed
was.details: Magi of Mistridge destroy Windgraven in a properly declared Wizard's War, battering its towers flat with giant stones conjured by magic. Few mourn its necromancers, who were widely thought diabolists, and the war foreshadows Mistridge's own end.

was.title: Bellaquin falls
was.details:
Overstretched by its feudal ties, Bellaquin tries to help two warring lords at once and is accused by both of stirring up their war. With churchmen urging them on, and a companion betraying the covenant, they storm the Château de Penne by surprise and kill several magi. The survivors, warned to prepare by archmagi, take their hidden reserves, destroy what they cannot carry and leave the site to their mundane proxies. Since the harm fell only on Bellaquin, no charges are brought.

Secrets
Some suspect other magi had a hand in arranging the mundane attack.

was.title: Bellaquin moves to Andorra
was.details: Bellaquin settles in a house in the parish of Ordino in Andorra, keeping its charter but changing its ways: subtler, richer and turned toward banking.

was.title: Bentalone overrun
was.details: The book's list of fallen covenants ends Bentalone in 1207: Simon de Montfort's army takes its castle for a Cathar stronghold and storms it in a surprise attack, though his campaigns in the south only begin in 1209.

was.title: Raimond VI excommunicated
was.details: In May Count Raimond VI of Toulouse is excommunicated for sheltering heretics. He promises the pope to drive them out, and the sentence is lifted in August.

was.title: Tribunal at Aedes Mercurii
was.details: The Tribunal meets at Aedes Mercurii and spends a whole day on the Church's drive against the Cathars, without deciding anything. Oxioun of Tytalus, leader of the host covenant, urges the Order to stay out of mundane affairs, and the Mercurian bloc is content to wait in its mountains, despite the worries of the lowland covenants of the Toulousain, the Narbonnais and the Rhône.

was.title: Protantus dies; Tibaut chief Quaesitor
was.details: A few months after the 1207 Tribunal, Protantus, the Traditionalist chief Quaesitor, dies and is followed by the more flexible Tibaut, a Transitionalist with no ties to the Mercurians. Few magi remark the coincidence with the legate's death, but it marks a turning point. The history chapter tells it so; the Gascony chapter names Senex as chief Quaesitor until 1210, with Tibaut acting in his place only from 1214.

was.title: Interdict in Gascony
was.details:
Innocent III lays all of King John's lands under interdict. Many Gascon churches close their doors and say no Mass for six years.

Secrets
During the interdict a band of demons, the Six Deadly Spirits, settles in the wild lands of Gascony away from the pilgrim roads, and some linger there still.

was.title: The legate murdered
was.details: In January Raimond meets the papal legates at St Gilles, stalls, and threatens them in anger as they leave. At dawn, waiting for the ferry to Arles, the legate Pierre de Castelnau is run through by a knight, forgiving his killer as he dies. Innocent III blames the count and proclaims a crusade; Arnaud Amaury and Bishop Foulques preach it, promising the crusaders a share of heretic lands and release from their debts to Jewish lenders.

was.title: Raimond joins the crusade
was.details: As the crusaders muster at Lyon, Raimond is scourged barefoot before a crowd at St Gilles and accepts hard terms. In June he takes the cross himself, robbing the crusade of its main target, which turns on the Trencavel lands instead. Raimond-Roger Trencavel is refused leave to join.

was.title: The sack of Béziers
was.details: Béziers refuses to hand over two hundred heretics. When its young men sally against the crusade's camp followers, the rabble surges through the open gate and the knights follow. Asked how to tell the faithful from the heretics, Arnaud Amaury is said to have answered that God would know His own. Fifteen to thirty thousand die, many in the churches.

was.title: Carcassonne surrenders
was.details: In August Viscount Raimond-Roger Trencavel leaves Carcassonne to parley and is seized and imprisoned. The city yields; its people are spared but its treasures plundered. Why so strong a city gave in so soon remains a mystery.

was.title: Simon de Montfort leads the crusade
was.details: When the great lords go home after their forty days, the legate's council chooses Simon de Montfort, a minor knight of the Île de France, to lead. With his wife Alice, thirty knights and five hundred foot he holds Carcassonne and takes the Trencavel titles of Béziers and Carcassonne, but Pedro II of Aragon will not take his homage. Revolts follow, the abbot of St Gilles is murdered, and de Montfort answers with the atrocity at Bram. In Toulouse Bishop Foulques forms his White Brotherhood against heretics, Jews and moneylenders, and a Black Brotherhood rises against it.

was.title: Mistridge destroyed
was.details: The Rusticani magus Tres declares Wizard's War on every magus of Mistridge. With two other magi of his tradition and a company of mercenaries armed with his enchanted weapons, he levels the tower with magical siege engines and kills its defenders. Some say he avenged Windgraven; others that Mistridge had scorned him as a hedge wizard.

was.title: Minerve and Termes fall
was.details: When the castle of Aguilar holds out, de Montfort turns to besiege Minerve, where a hundred and thirty-seven Cathars are burned and only three women recant. Termes and more castles follow, making him master of the Trencavel lands. So few heretics have died that the war is plainly one of conquest.

was.title: Berinor falls; Senex vanishes
was.details:
Berinor falls when de Montfort's men dispossess the lord who held its castle, and its survivors take refuge at Tolosa Paratge. The same year Senex of Guernicus, the chief Quaesitor, goes into a village to look into something and is never seen again.

Secrets
Senex had begun to look into Dama's cult of the Matres and Matrones. While she was away at an akelarre he slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan; she came back early and caught him there. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's venom killed him, Maju devoured the body as a drake, and Dama told no one. In law he had forfeited his immunity by entering her sanctum.

was.title: Lavaur, and the first siege of Toulouse
was.details: Pedro II at last accepts de Montfort's homage and tries to broker peace, but the legates' terms are too harsh and the south rises. Lavaur is sacked, sixty Cathars taken at Les Casses are burned, and de Montfort besieges Toulouse. Bishop Foulques tells the faithful to give up the city and their count or share the heretics' fate; they drive him out instead, and the siege fails.

was.title: Montgey and the fall of Lariander
was.details:
Peasants and southern knights massacre some three hundred German crusaders marching through a faerie forest near Montgey to Lavaur. In reprisal the crusaders destroy the village, burn the woods and slaughter the Tremere of Lariander, taking their black robes for those of Cathar perfecti. Garsenda of Lariander believes she is the only survivor.

Secrets
Garsenda had stirred the villagers to the ambush, and the white ladies and walking trees the survivors spoke of were real.

was.title: Battle of St Martin-Lalande
was.details: Raimond gathers his army against de Montfort's small force, but the crusaders keep raiding and seizing the initiative, and when the southerners finally attack they are routed in open battle.

was.title: The Children's Crusade; Las Navas de Tolosa
was.details: Thousands of children and peasants follow a young visionary from the Rhineland through France to Marseilles, sure the sea will open for them. It does not; many board ships for Africa and vanish, feared sold as slaves. In Iberia the Christian kings win the great victory of Las Navas de Tolosa.

was.title: Battle of Muret
was.details: Pedro II of Aragon, Raimond and the count of Foix take Muret, ten miles up the Garonne from Toulouse, with a great army. De Montfort crosses the marshes to fall on their flank: Pedro is killed and some ten thousand die in under half an hour, many drowning in the river, where their cries are still heard in flood. Resistance is broken for years, and Raimond seeks redress in Rome.

was.title: Tribunal at Castra Solis
was.details: The meeting set for Toulouse moves to Castra Solis, with de Montfort's army outside the city, to the Mercurians' annoyance. It is the most bitter gathering since the Schism War, taken up with the crusade and charges of meddling with mundanes: some blame Normandy magi, some Flambeau blame Tytalus for the crusade itself. Tolomae of Jerbiton calls for open Hermetic resistance and is thrown out of the debate, swearing revenge on the Mercurians and on the Coenobium. Aedes Mercurii threatens to walk out and so void the Tribunal, until Tibaut and the chief Redcap Alazais, who threatens to stop all Redcap service, avert anarchy. Senex is absent, and Tibaut acts as chief Quaesitor.

was.title: Ruling: Tres acquitted
was.details: Charges are brought against Tres for arming mercenaries with enchanted weapons, calling them his grogs, and using them to destroy Mistridge. However deplored, it was a lawfully declared Wizard's War and no ruling forbids grogs in one; the vote goes narrowly his way. Tres flees into hiding from Mistridge's friends, and after the meeting the Hermetic faidits begin to gather at Aguilar as the Ostal des Exiles, Rixenda of Mistridge first and Gilbert of Flambeau their leader.

was.title: De Montfort enters Toulouse; Filii Sinapis abandoned
was.details: Simon de Montfort enters Toulouse in triumph and takes up residence in the Château Narbonnais. The Waldensians are condemned as heretics, though Innocent III thought them good Christians. Filii Sinapis is abandoned in the wake of the crusade.

was.title: Tolomae declared orbus; Tibaut confirmed
was.details: House Jerbiton expels Tolomae of Bellaquin, leader of the Procrustean League, which calls for open war on the Church, and declares him orbus. He is suspected of the legate's murder and flees rather than answer the Quaesitor's questions. With Senex absent two years, Tibaut is confirmed as chief Quaesitor. In Toulouse an autumn rising is put down with great effort, and de Montfort names himself count of Toulouse.

was.title: Raimond returns to Toulouse
was.details:
While de Montfort campaigns in the north, Raimond slips back into Toulouse to the citizens' joy. De Montfort finds the gates shut against him and lays siege for months.

Secrets
Tibaut, who found the first threads of Senex's inquiry in his laboratory notes, begins this year to investigate the Tribunal's mystery cults, the Cathars and the sorginak, sharing his suspicions with his filia Beatrice. A letter he sent her lies in the satchel of a Redcap who died of crusaders' wounds along the Via Domitia.

was.title: Tolomae Marched
was.details: Early in the year Tolomae is Marched for repeatedly meddling with mundanes, and slain. His suspected supporters scatter among other covenants or hide among the faidits.

was.title: Simon de Montfort killed
was.details:
A stone from a siege engine on the walls of Toulouse strikes Simon de Montfort on the head and kills him. Amaury de Montfort claims his titles, and Alice remains a leader of the campaign, but Simon's great domain begins to fall apart.

Secrets
Some suspect the engine was one of those Tres built to destroy Mistridge.

was.title: Wizard's Wars at Tolosa Paratge
was.details: In the weeks before de Montfort's death, Augustus of Tolosa Paratge, a senior Quaesitor, is persuaded by Bishop Foulques that Toulouse will fall and asks the covenant's Gorgiastic Cathars to leave for their safety. They refuse; Marc declares Wizard's War on him and, believing him possessed, kills him in the tower. Within the month St Tropez declares Wizard's War on the unresisting Marc and kills him. Under Mariola, the covenant splits into the Blacks, who hold it, and the Whites, who plot in the city to retake it.

was.title: Siege of Marmande
was.details: Soon after Christmas, Prince Louis's crusaders under Centule d'Astarac besiege Marmande.

was.title: Tibaut dies
was.details:
Tibaut, the Presiding Quaesitor, dies in the care of the monks of Saint Hilaire, taken for a Cathar by crusaders who later raid the abbey. His body is buried there and his belongings sit locked in the abbot's chest. At Dama's suggestion his filia Beatrice of Guernicus fills the office until the 1221 Tribunal. (The Hermetic culture chapter also says once that he died in 1214; the 1221 Tribunal takes 1219.)

Secrets
Warned by Luc of Ara Maxima Nova of Tibaut's questions, Dama ambushed him with Maju near the road to Foix. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus shattered his Parma, but Maju's venom worked slowly; he staggered into the road and divinely blessed crusader knights carried him to the abbey before she could reach him. Before he died he confided something to the knights.

was.title: Marmande massacred; Toulouse besieged
was.details: After nine months Marmande surrenders on terms. Amaury de Montfort, urged by the Bishop of Saintes, then kills all five thousand townsfolk and their beasts and burns the town. Prince Louis's royal crusade besieges Toulouse but withdraws when pestilence breaks out in his army, and Raimond begins to win back his county.

value.title: Regional Tribunals created
value.details: As the Order grows, the Second Grand Tribunal sets up regional Tribunals, made of covenants that lie near one another rather than of lands with fixed borders. The rules for founding and governing them come out of a quarrel over Val-Negra's charter: Flambeau wanted lordship over every covenant his home helped to found.

value.title: Val-Negra recognized
value.details: After years of argument between Flambeau and Guernicus over its charter, the covenant of Val-Negra in the Pyrenees is formally recognized, and a regional Tribunal forms around it. Flambeau is the only Founder to make his home there, though Trianoma and Mercere visit often. Tolosa Paratge, a large Diedne covenant in a lake regio at Toulouse, is one of the four first covenants of the new Tribunal, and most of the region's other covenants belong to House Diedne.

value.title: Gelon becomes Primus of Verditius
value.details: Gelon, the first apprentice of Verditius, becomes Primus of his House. He lives for decades at Val-Negra, forging his famous enchanted swords, and his followers go on to found the Confraternity of Roland.

value.title: Kaeso joins House Flambeau
value.details: The Christian wizard Kaeso, whose power rests on an old underground temple of Mithras by the Garonne, joins House Flambeau. Training under Apromor and Flambeau in the Pyrenees, he forms the Hoplites, soldier-magi who hurl Pilum of Fire from behind a strong Parma Magica, and leads many of them into the Legion of Mithras. Many count him the first Hoplite.

value.title: Apromor becomes Primus of Flambeau
value.details: Apromor, the Founder's first apprentice, who has drifted from his master's ways, becomes the first Primus of House Flambeau, and Kaeso's Hoplites carry on Flambeau's war against the sahirs of Iberia. Apromor welcomes pagan and non-Hermetic wizards into the Order, works with Priamitus of Mercere to revive the Cult of Mercury from the last Roman priests of the region, and spreads Val-Negra's outposts across the Pyrenees.

value.title: Portus Cottiae and Yf founded
value.details: Julius Donnus, an outcast Mercurian of House Flambeau from the Greater Alps, founds Portus Cottiae outside Briançon as a second home for the revived Cult of Mercury, after Harco. It becomes the first Mercer House of the region and grows into a covenant of several sites, with chapter houses at Gap, Chorges and Embrun and a post at Oulx guarding the passes. In the same year Diedne magi found Yf on an island off the coast of Arelat.

value.title: Lapurdum founded
value.details: Flambeau magi found Lapurdum where the Adour meets the sea in Gascony, around a mithraeum in what was once a Roman army camp.

value.title: Campus Elysii founded
value.details: A small group of spirit masters, necromancers of Ex Miscellanea, settles in the crypts of the Alyscamps at Arles as the covenant of Campus Elysii.

value.title: Vikings on the Garonne
value.details: King Pepin II of Aquitaine, seeking freedom from Charles the Bald, is accused of apostasy for letting the Viking Jarl Oscar sail his raiders up the Garonne to Toulouse. Northmen camp all along the western coast, and Marseilles has already been sacked by Arab pirates (838); Byzantine freebooters (849) and Normans based in the Camargue follow. Tales of rune-wizards among the raiders finally draw the magi in, and Flambeau comes to resent how little the Diedne do to help.

value.title: Castra Solis founded
value.details: Raids on Gascon villages have grown since 840, and the Flambeau wrongly believe an organized Order of Odin is behind them. Kaeso returns to Bordeaux and fortifies his temple as a covenant, Castra Solis, the encampment of the sun, under the sign of a quartered sun.

value.title: Bordeaux falls to the Northmen
value.details: Before the Hoplites can do more than raise hasty defences, the northern pagans take Bordeaux. Unwilling to harm the townsfolk, the magi spend five years trying to end the war by force against the rune-wizards alone, and many die in their traps, Kaeso among them.

value.title: Sinapis founded
value.details: With Bordeaux too near the front, the surviving Flambeau build a fortified covenant, Sinapis, further north in Anjou. Castra Solis becomes a camp of tents for quick strikes, and to outsiders it looks like an offshoot of Sinapis.

value.title: Lapurdum abandoned
value.details: Worn down by Viking raids and quarrels among its magi, Lapurdum is given up. Its ruins lie somewhere under the city of Bayonne.

value.title: Seven Tribunals defined
value.details: The Grand Tribunal draws up seven regional Tribunals. Val-Negra goes to the Iberian Tribunal, along with the mountains and the Basque lands north of them; the bulk of France goes to the West Franks, and a strip from Friesland through Burgundy to Arelat forms the Lotharingian Tribunal.

value.title: Fraxinetum founded
value.details: Two Tytalan war-magi, Sayyid Shajarat al-Darda (who called himself a Flambeau, though the House denies him) and his lieutenant Nasr ibn Amaf, settle in the Massif des Maures above St Tropez with a band of Andalusian raiders. Their covenant, named for the ash groves Sayyid planted, stays hidden from the Tribunal for its first century while it backs Moorish attacks on Provençal towns.

value.title: Barbegal founded
value.details: Three Verditius mage-smiths found a covenant in the Roman watermill complex of Barbegal, just north of Arles.

value.title: Lotharingia divided
value.details: The Grand Tribunal hands the northern covenants of the Lotharingian Tribunal to Normandy or the Rhine. What is left, the Kingdom of Arles along the Rhône and a few covenants in the Toulousain (a Mercer House at Arles, a strong Diedne covenant at Lyon, and a handful of others), comes to be called the Provençal Tribunal.

value.title: The Birds of Camargue founded
value.details: Bjornaer magi found a covenant in the marshes at the mouth of the Rhône.

value.title: Portus Cottiae overrun
value.details: Berber mountaineers overrun the scattered sites of Portus Cottiae, one of the first Lotharingian covenants to fall to the Saracens. Its magi flee down the Durance; at the motherhouse near Briançon the defenders bring the mountain down on the raiders and bury themselves in their own sancta. The one surviving maga, Anaïs of Jerbiton, reaches Avignon and becomes a loud voice for the Hermetic league that becomes the Coenobium.

value.title: Yf falls
value.details: The Diedne covenant of Yf falls to the raids of Fraxinetum. One of its magae later joins the Coenobium to avenge it, but her line dies out shortly before the Schism War.

value.title: Barbegal abandoned
value.details: The undefended mills of Barbegal are abandoned under Saracen raiding. The surviving smiths help to found the Rhône covenant of Coenobium Rhodanien.

value.title: Askelarre founded
value.details: A coven of Hermetic sorginak, Basque witches spread across the Basque country, founds the covenant of Askelarre.

value.title: Sorginak join Ex Miscellanea; Donjon Leyre founded
value.details: A few sorginak at last join House Ex Miscellanea, resented by their hedge sisters and anxious to keep their distance from the Diedne, who had long taken sorginak into their own House. In the same year Donjon Leyre, an early vassal of Montverte, is founded at the fork of the Leyre in the Landes as a base for raids into the Basque Pyrenees.

value.title: The Birds of Camargue merge into the Coenobium
value.details: Threatened by Fraxinetum, the Bjornaer of the Birds of Camargue join the wider league of Rhône magi that becomes the Coenobium Rhodanien.

value.title: Maieul of Cluny captured
value.details: The Moors of the Massif des Maures capture and ransom Maieul, abbot of Cluny, and push into the foothills of the Alps. The alarm this raises moves the mostly Jerbiton magi of eastern Provence to band together in a pact of mutual defence. Working through their families, churchmen and noble allies, they quietly back the army of William I of Provence, which routs the Moors at Tourtour.

value.title: Fraxinetum destroyed
value.details:
William's army takes the Moorish base and the Fraxinetum magi vanish into the forest. The history chapter says the Coenobium Rhodanien, which it calls newly formed (the Birds of Camargue had joined it in 970), destroyed the covenant by Wizard's War; the Arelat chapter says no war was ever openly declared and the league narrowly escaped the Quaesitors' anger for acting through mundane arms. Either way, the victors stay together as a covenant of many sites along the Rhône and the coast. In the same year Anaïs of Toulouse, a renegade Criamon expelled from her House, brings her followers, the Gorgiastic Cathars, into House Ex Miscellanea.

Secrets
The Fraxinetum magi did not perish. Their heirs live on in secret as Fraxinetum Redux on the Hyères islands, never declared to the Tribunal.

value.title: Grand Tribunal: the Northmen driven out
value.details: At the Grand Tribunal the Hoplites declare the rune-wizards rooted out of the region after more than a century of war: all three Danish settlements on the coast have been burned. Many of their fortified outposts, such as the tower at Mimizan, later grow into covenants counted as offshoots of Castra Solis. The Diedne, uneasy with the Mithraic piety of the Hoplites, took no part, which deepens Flambeau's suspicion of them.

value.title: Donjon Leyre falls
value.details: All the founding magi of Donjon Leyre die fighting in the Schism War, which rages through Gascony as Val-Negra's forces storm the Diedne covenants one after another; many Gascon Diedne burn their own sites and flee.

value.title: Campus Elysii driven out
value.details:
The spirit masters of Campus Elysii, who hid underground through the war, are forced out of the Alyscamps when the Coenobium stirs up the townsfolk with tales of diabolists under the necropolis. They try to begin again in a cave network in the Verdon gorge as Portus Termini, but all contact is lost before the next Tribunal and the new covenant is never registered.

Secrets
Many suspect that Hoplites in the Coenobium's pay hunted down the survivors.

value.title: Askelarre destroyed
value.details: The sorginak covenant of Askelarre is destroyed in the Schism War. Two of Val-Negra's magi, the Flambeau Leo Augustus and the Tremere Vegetius, die in the attack.

value.title: The fall of Val-Negra
value.details:
As the Schism War draws to its close, while its zealous magi are away striking at the Diedne, five Diedne archmagi storm Val-Negra. Of twenty-five magi at the war's start, only four are left. Shortly before the war many of its Flambeau had left, after a vision, to found Aedes Mercurii in Val-Negra's outlying halls; now the survivors join it, and it declares itself a Provençal covenant and the heir of Val-Negra. Many other covenants change to the Provençal Tribunal at this time, partly to keep Tytalus from claiming the spoils of the fallen Diedne. The domus magna of Flambeau moves to Castra Solis, and the Quaesitors strike nine or more Diedne sites from the records. Why Val-Negra was never rebuilt, and even where it stood, is soon forgotten.

Secrets
The Diedne reached the Iron Door in the depths of Val-Negra, and in the fighting the Adulteration of Flambeau was loosed. It killed three defenders and all the attackers before the last two archmagi forced it back and sealed the door with a Hermetic ward, one that breaks if the door is simply opened. The Quaesitors kept it quiet and ruled that Val-Negra must never rise again.

value.title: Bellaquin founded
value.details: As the Schism War dies down, Flambeau magi restore an abandoned castle, the Château de Penne in Tarn above the Aveyron, as a stronghold. The war ends before it is needed, and they hand it to House Jerbiton, who make it one of the most admired covenants in the Order and, in time, the lords of a fief of their own.

value.title: Mistridge founded
value.details: A covenant is founded in the Val du Bosque, in a tower raised by magic at the brink of a sheer drop.

value.title: Windgraven founded
value.details: Necromancers found Windgraven in the squat stone towers of a ruined Visigothic fort on a rocky plateau in the southern part of the County of Toulouse.

value.title: Filii Sinapis founded
value.details: Flambeau magi from the abandoned Normandy covenant of Sinapis found Filii Sinapis.

value.title: Berinor founded
value.details: Jerbiton magi found Berinor, a small covenant in the County of Toulouse that becomes a patron of troubadours and trobairitz.

value.title: Gascony joins the Provençal Tribunal
value.details: When the Normandy Tribunal splits, Castra Solis leads a faction into the enlarged Provençal Tribunal. The magi of Sinapis leave their site to join the domus magna, and smaller covenants of the area, Mimizan among them, come too.

value.title: Bentalone founded
value.details: A covenant is founded in a castle in the Toulousain; it stays in Summer for a century.

value.title: Grand Tribunal: the Occitan border
value.details: To settle quarrels between Normandy and the newly enlarged Provençal Tribunal, the Grand Tribunal rules that the border between them runs wherever Occitan stops being spoken. Unpopular at first, the rule is soon embraced by the southern magi to secure their claims to vis, and the Tribunal's minutes and proclamations are written in both Latin and Occitan.

value.title: The Golden Court at Beaucaire
value.details:
Count Henry II of Provence holds a festival in the meadows north of Beaucaire to mark the reconciliation of the Duke of Narbonne and the King of Aragon. A chronicler praises its hundred thousand knights, its gold sown in the earth and its herds roasted over wax torches.

Secrets
Most of the knights were faeries revelling in the troubadours' spirit of foolishness, and the gold was glamour; the meadow still holds Faerie vis.

value.title: Saint Jean Pied-de-Port razed
value.details: When Richard the Lionheart sacks Saint Jean Pied-de-Port, the large outpost Aedes Mercurii kept there is lost; its covenfolk had already fallen under the townsfolk's suspicion of witchcraft.

value.title: Miniata Sophia founded
value.details: A Criamon eremite founds Miniata Sophia in the cave system of Niaux, about forty years before 1220. For a decade and more it keeps to itself.

value.title: Lariander founded
value.details: Tremere magi found Lariander, a young covenant in a faerie wood near the village of Montgey in the Toulousain.

value.title: Tribunal: Miniata Sophia announced
value.details: Miniata Sophia makes itself known at the Tribunal and registers its site, the village of Niaux, with the Redcaps. It has attended every meeting since, voting on each question as seems most apt or abstaining, and making no alliances.

value.title: Ara Maxima Nova founded
value.details: Merinita magi who have explored the labours of Heracles in the east come west to follow the rest of his journey and found Ara Maxima Nova among the vineyards outside Perpignan, close to the Via Domitia. Their charter binds them to seek the Hesperides every five years.

value.title: Windgraven destroyed
value.details: Magi of Mistridge destroy Windgraven in a properly declared Wizard's War, battering its towers flat with giant stones conjured by magic. Few mourn its necromancers, who were widely thought diabolists, and the war foreshadows Mistridge's own end.

value.title: Bellaquin falls
value.details:
Overstretched by its feudal ties, Bellaquin tries to help two warring lords at once and is accused by both of stirring up their war. With churchmen urging them on, and a companion betraying the covenant, they storm the Château de Penne by surprise and kill several magi. The survivors, warned to prepare by archmagi, take their hidden reserves, destroy what they cannot carry and leave the site to their mundane proxies. Since the harm fell only on Bellaquin, no charges are brought.

Secrets
Some suspect other magi had a hand in arranging the mundane attack.

value.title: Bellaquin moves to Andorra
value.details: Bellaquin settles in a house in the parish of Ordino in Andorra, keeping its charter but changing its ways: subtler, richer and turned toward banking.

value.title: Bentalone overrun
value.details: The book's list of fallen covenants ends Bentalone in 1207: Simon de Montfort's army takes its castle for a Cathar stronghold and storms it in a surprise attack, though his campaigns in the south only begin in 1209.

value.title: Raimond VI excommunicated
value.details: In May Count Raimond VI of Toulouse is excommunicated for sheltering heretics. He promises the pope to drive them out, and the sentence is lifted in August.

value.title: Tribunal at Aedes Mercurii
value.details: The Tribunal meets at Aedes Mercurii and spends a whole day on the Church's drive against the Cathars, without deciding anything. Oxioun of Tytalus, leader of the host covenant, urges the Order to stay out of mundane affairs, and the Mercurian bloc is content to wait in its mountains, despite the worries of the lowland covenants of the Toulousain, the Narbonnais and the Rhône.

value.title: Protantus dies; Tibaut chief Quaesitor
value.details: A few months after the 1207 Tribunal, Protantus, the Traditionalist chief Quaesitor, dies and is followed by the more flexible Tibaut, a Transitionalist with no ties to the Mercurians. Few magi remark the coincidence with the legate's death, but it marks a turning point. The history chapter tells it so; the Gascony chapter names Senex as chief Quaesitor until 1210, with Tibaut acting in his place only from 1214.

value.title: Interdict in Gascony
value.details:
Innocent III lays all of King John's lands under interdict. Many Gascon churches close their doors and say no Mass for six years.

Secrets
During the interdict a band of demons, the Six Deadly Spirits, settles in the wild lands of Gascony away from the pilgrim roads, and some linger there still.

value.title: The legate murdered
value.details: In January Raimond meets the papal legates at St Gilles, stalls, and threatens them in anger as they leave. At dawn, waiting for the ferry to Arles, the legate Pierre de Castelnau is run through by a knight, forgiving his killer as he dies. Innocent III blames the count and proclaims a crusade; Arnaud Amaury and Bishop Foulques preach it, promising the crusaders a share of heretic lands and release from their debts to Jewish lenders.

value.title: Raimond joins the crusade
value.details: As the crusaders muster at Lyon, Raimond is scourged barefoot before a crowd at St Gilles and accepts hard terms. In June he takes the cross himself, robbing the crusade of its main target, which turns on the Trencavel lands instead. Raimond-Roger Trencavel is refused leave to join.

value.title: The sack of Béziers
value.details: Béziers refuses to hand over two hundred heretics. When its young men sally against the crusade's camp followers, the rabble surges through the open gate and the knights follow. Asked how to tell the faithful from the heretics, Arnaud Amaury is said to have answered that God would know His own. Fifteen to thirty thousand die, many in the churches.

value.title: Carcassonne surrenders
value.details: In August Viscount Raimond-Roger Trencavel leaves Carcassonne to parley and is seized and imprisoned. The city yields; its people are spared but its treasures plundered. Why so strong a city gave in so soon remains a mystery.

value.title: Simon de Montfort leads the crusade
value.details: When the great lords go home after their forty days, the legate's council chooses Simon de Montfort, a minor knight of the Île de France, to lead. With his wife Alice, thirty knights and five hundred foot he holds Carcassonne and takes the Trencavel titles of Béziers and Carcassonne, but Pedro II of Aragon will not take his homage. Revolts follow, the abbot of St Gilles is murdered, and de Montfort answers with the atrocity at Bram. In Toulouse Bishop Foulques forms his White Brotherhood against heretics, Jews and moneylenders, and a Black Brotherhood rises against it.

value.title: Mistridge destroyed
value.details: The Rusticani magus Tres declares Wizard's War on every magus of Mistridge. With two other magi of his tradition and a company of mercenaries armed with his enchanted weapons, he levels the tower with magical siege engines and kills its defenders. Some say he avenged Windgraven; others that Mistridge had scorned him as a hedge wizard.

value.title: Minerve and Termes fall
value.details: When the castle of Aguilar holds out, de Montfort turns to besiege Minerve, where a hundred and thirty-seven Cathars are burned and only three women recant. Termes and more castles follow, making him master of the Trencavel lands. So few heretics have died that the war is plainly one of conquest.

value.title: Berinor falls; Senex vanishes
value.details:
Berinor falls when de Montfort's men dispossess the lord who held its castle, and its survivors take refuge at Tolosa Paratge. The same year Senex of Guernicus, the chief Quaesitor, goes into a village to look into something and is never seen again.

Secrets
Senex had begun to look into Dama's cult of the Matres and Matrones. While she was away at an akelarre he slipped into her sanctum at Mimizan; she came back early and caught him there. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus and Maju's venom killed him, Maju devoured the body as a drake, and Dama told no one. In law he had forfeited his immunity by entering her sanctum.

value.title: Lavaur, and the first siege of Toulouse
value.details: Pedro II at last accepts de Montfort's homage and tries to broker peace, but the legates' terms are too harsh and the south rises. Lavaur is sacked, sixty Cathars taken at Les Casses are burned, and de Montfort besieges Toulouse. Bishop Foulques tells the faithful to give up the city and their count or share the heretics' fate; they drive him out instead, and the siege fails.

value.title: Montgey and the fall of Lariander
value.details:
Peasants and southern knights massacre some three hundred German crusaders marching through a faerie forest near Montgey to Lavaur. In reprisal the crusaders destroy the village, burn the woods and slaughter the Tremere of Lariander, taking their black robes for those of Cathar perfecti. Garsenda of Lariander believes she is the only survivor.

Secrets
Garsenda had stirred the villagers to the ambush, and the white ladies and walking trees the survivors spoke of were real.

value.title: Battle of St Martin-Lalande
value.details: Raimond gathers his army against de Montfort's small force, but the crusaders keep raiding and seizing the initiative, and when the southerners finally attack they are routed in open battle.

value.title: The Children's Crusade; Las Navas de Tolosa
value.details: Thousands of children and peasants follow a young visionary from the Rhineland through France to Marseilles, sure the sea will open for them. It does not; many board ships for Africa and vanish, feared sold as slaves. In Iberia the Christian kings win the great victory of Las Navas de Tolosa.

value.title: Battle of Muret
value.details: Pedro II of Aragon, Raimond and the count of Foix take Muret, ten miles up the Garonne from Toulouse, with a great army. De Montfort crosses the marshes to fall on their flank: Pedro is killed and some ten thousand die in under half an hour, many drowning in the river, where their cries are still heard in flood. Resistance is broken for years, and Raimond seeks redress in Rome.

value.title: Tribunal at Castra Solis
value.details: The meeting set for Toulouse moves to Castra Solis, with de Montfort's army outside the city, to the Mercurians' annoyance. It is the most bitter gathering since the Schism War, taken up with the crusade and charges of meddling with mundanes: some blame Normandy magi, some Flambeau blame Tytalus for the crusade itself. Tolomae of Jerbiton calls for open Hermetic resistance and is thrown out of the debate, swearing revenge on the Mercurians and on the Coenobium. Aedes Mercurii threatens to walk out and so void the Tribunal, until Tibaut and the chief Redcap Alazais, who threatens to stop all Redcap service, avert anarchy. Senex is absent, and Tibaut acts as chief Quaesitor.

value.title: Ruling: Tres acquitted
value.details: Charges are brought against Tres for arming mercenaries with enchanted weapons, calling them his grogs, and using them to destroy Mistridge. However deplored, it was a lawfully declared Wizard's War and no ruling forbids grogs in one; the vote goes narrowly his way. Tres flees into hiding from Mistridge's friends, and after the meeting the Hermetic faidits begin to gather at Aguilar as the Ostal des Exiles, Rixenda of Mistridge first and Gilbert of Flambeau their leader.

value.title: De Montfort enters Toulouse; Filii Sinapis abandoned
value.details: Simon de Montfort enters Toulouse in triumph and takes up residence in the Château Narbonnais. The Waldensians are condemned as heretics, though Innocent III thought them good Christians. Filii Sinapis is abandoned in the wake of the crusade.

value.title: Tolomae declared orbus; Tibaut confirmed
value.details: House Jerbiton expels Tolomae of Bellaquin, leader of the Procrustean League, which calls for open war on the Church, and declares him orbus. He is suspected of the legate's murder and flees rather than answer the Quaesitor's questions. With Senex absent two years, Tibaut is confirmed as chief Quaesitor. In Toulouse an autumn rising is put down with great effort, and de Montfort names himself count of Toulouse.

value.title: Raimond returns to Toulouse
value.details:
While de Montfort campaigns in the north, Raimond slips back into Toulouse to the citizens' joy. De Montfort finds the gates shut against him and lays siege for months.

Secrets
Tibaut, who found the first threads of Senex's inquiry in his laboratory notes, begins this year to investigate the Tribunal's mystery cults, the Cathars and the sorginak, sharing his suspicions with his filia Beatrice. A letter he sent her lies in the satchel of a Redcap who died of crusaders' wounds along the Via Domitia.

value.title: Tolomae Marched
value.details: Early in the year Tolomae is Marched for repeatedly meddling with mundanes, and slain. His suspected supporters scatter among other covenants or hide among the faidits.

value.title: Simon de Montfort killed
value.details:
A stone from a siege engine on the walls of Toulouse strikes Simon de Montfort on the head and kills him. Amaury de Montfort claims his titles, and Alice remains a leader of the campaign, but Simon's great domain begins to fall apart.

Secrets
Some suspect the engine was one of those Tres built to destroy Mistridge.

value.title: Wizard's Wars at Tolosa Paratge
value.details:
In the weeks before de Montfort's death, Augustus of Tolosa Paratge, a senior Quaesitor, is persuaded by Bishop Foulques that Toulouse will fall and asks the covenant's Gorgiastic Cathars to leave for their safety. They refuse; Marc declares Wizard's War on him and, believing him possessed, kills him in the tower. Within the month St Tropez declares Wizard's War on the unresisting Marc and kills him. Under Mariola, the covenant splits into the Blacks, who hold it, and the Whites, who plot in the city to retake it.

Through the Aegis has the civil war already broken out by 1214, when it drove Alyssa from the covenant to Jardin.

value.title: Siege of Marmande
value.details: Soon after Christmas, Prince Louis's crusaders under Centule d'Astarac besiege Marmande.

value.title: Tibaut dies
value.details:
Tibaut, the Presiding Quaesitor, dies in the care of the monks of Saint Hilaire, taken for a Cathar by crusaders who later raid the abbey. His body is buried there and his belongings sit locked in the abbot's chest. At Dama's suggestion his filia Beatrice of Guernicus fills the office until the 1221 Tribunal. (The Hermetic culture chapter also says once that he died in 1214; the 1221 Tribunal takes 1219.)

Secrets
Warned by Luc of Ara Maxima Nova of Tibaut's questions, Dama ambushed him with Maju near the road to Foix. Her Revoke the Protection of Bonisagus shattered his Parma, but Maju's venom worked slowly; he staggered into the road and divinely blessed crusader knights carried him to the abbey before she could reach him. Before he died he confided something to the knights.

value.title: Marmande massacred; Toulouse besieged
value.details: After nine months Marmande surrenders on terms. Amaury de Montfort, urged by the Bishop of Saintes, then kills all five thousand townsfolk and their beasts and burns the town. Prince Louis's royal crusade besieges Toulouse but withdraws when pestilence breaks out in his army, and Raimond begins to win back his county.

saga.name: Guardians of the Forests: the Rhine Tribunal

covenants.name: Collem Leonis
covenants.notes:
Story seeds. The Winter Litter: a whole litter of albino stoats in the snow, hunted by a crafty snow leopard from the portal that lays false trails; only Bjornaer leave lets it be hunted. The Mischievous Kobold: respected with food and asking, he only plays; slighted, he leads miners astray, steals tools or brings down the rock. Impossible Thefts: a visitor knows his plate, sold to him and stolen back overnight, before the armoire was found. A Simple Request: Vorderhagen would borrow the silverware for a week for the count's visit. Agents Provocateurs: mercenaries of the archbishop raid Mark from a camp in Berg. The Church Lands: to end a war, Adolph may cede a wild valley due south of the covenant for an abbey, through the archbishop's man Max von Beiderbecke, while Dortmund bids for it. The Enemy of My Enemy: Erich learns Count Frederick of Isenberg, tied to the Cologne diabolists, plots against the archbishop. Old Alliances: a Redcap's letter calls in forgotten pacts, from Urgen, Prima Falke or Waddenzee, who found a creature on the Norwegian coast. The Army of King Gorm: a faerie lord arrives through the portal to honour a pact of a year and a day, and assumes the archbishop is the enemy. The Ravens Fly Again: ravens over the woods toward Dortmund mark a lindorm's birth, as they did for the one Scipio went to stop.

Storylines. Rebuilding: recover the lost resources, sell wood from the Woodshed and metal from the mine, and mind Dortmund's guilds. Counts and Bishops: the struggle of Mark and Cologne, with the Code ever near; the archbishop does not at first know of the lodge, and Adolph keeps the wizards in reserve. Reforging Relations: the Tribunals of 1221 and before 1228, Murion's wish to act against the Order of Odin, Daria la Gris's Lotharingian Tribunal, and the Harmonist and Wilderist rift. The Portals: save the great events until the covenant is strong; Scipio's sacrifice has bought decades.

If the saga follows history: Adolph loses his northern lands between Dortmund and Soest to Engelbert until reconciled with the next archbishop, inherits from Frederick of Isenberg, and dies in 1249; Duke Henry III of Limburg is followed by Waleran III in 1221, and Henry IV takes Berg in 1225 and Limburg in 1226; Engelbert is murdered by his cousin Frederick in 1225 and Heinrich I von Mullnarken follows; Cologne becomes a Free Imperial City in 1288.

Ferra suits the troupe as a lightly used adviser; the four young magi suit players. Elsewhere: the covenant could move to any frontier Tribunal, which voids the gild Virtues. As a background covenant it offers trade, diplomacy and old lore.
