creatures.name: Lindorm of Jotunheim

reputations.name: Lethal and venomous (local, in Nordic cultures only)

powers.name: Blood of Venom
powers.description: Always on. Its blood turns corrosive as it leaves the body: whoever deals a Medium or worse wound rolls Qik - Enc against 9, 12 for Heavy, 15 for Incapacitating or worse; those near roll against 9. Failure takes +25 damage, repeated each round at -1 damage and -1 Protection until the roll is 0, the armor or poison is off, or two minutes pass.

powers.name: Breath of Venom
powers.description: In place of a bite, spews venom on a target within 15 paces: it hits automatically and does +25 if it Penetrates, and may splash others for +12 unless they make Qik - Enc against 9.

powers.name: Magical Senses
powers.description: Always on. Smells auras, vis, enchanted devices, creatures with Might and the Gifted within a mile, and is drawn to consume, rest, fight or seize.

creatures.appearance: A vast serpent, some 10 feet thick and almost 400 long, with angry red eyes, teeth like greatswords, dark spiny ridges, bright green scales and a wrinkled bilious belly.
creatures.notes:
Magic Animal, Magical Monster; Improved Characteristics (x6); Poor Communication (x2), Poor Presence. Qualities also: Reduced Communication, Reduced Presence, Minor Flaw (Poor Presence). Mundane Qualities: Grapple, Keen Sense of Smell, Large Teeth, Loathsome Appearance, Spiny, Tough Hide, Thick Scales, Sharp Ears, Slippery, Venomous. Brawl has +2 from Puissance. Wounds -1 (1-18), -3 (19-36), -5 (37-54), Incapacitated (55-72), Dead (73+).

Constriction, not magical: it grapples and constricts targets up to a total Size of +7, who suffer air Deprivation; those of Size +2 or less it rolls under its body. Scales, not magical: Soak +17 normally; +10 against blows at the belly (Finesse or Athletics against 12 suggested); +25 fortified, good against massed arrows. Venomous, not magical: a bite whose Attack Advantage beats the target's Protection adds a Light wound, as does any combat botch in melee, on a spine.
creatures.secrets:
Ravens over the woods mark its birth from the earth, and their flight shows its path. It stops to eat vis and burrows to digest it, sometimes for months, growing all the while.

Vis: 4 pawns of Perdo in the heart, 2 of Animal in the body, and whatever it has eaten in its stomach.

creatures.name: Agnes

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: A body of wood, tough as old oak and supple as flesh, with sap for blood. It is renewed each sunrise and sunset, ages and hungers, and is remade at least monthly to stay young; if it is killed she is destroyed, but she can dissolve it at will. RoP: Magic pp. 38-39, 102.

powers.name: Crafter of Herbam
powers.description: 1 point a magnitude, Init 1 - magnitude: any Creo Herbam effect to level 25.

powers.name: Master of Herbam
powers.description: 1 point a magnitude, Init - magnitude: any Rego or Muto Herbam effect to level 20.

creatures.equipment: A simple dress in the forest's present colours, a woven leather belt, a bronze sickle.
creatures.appearance: A healthy young woman with golden almond eyes and dark curly hair with oak leaves growing in it.
creatures.notes: A minor forest spirit, lonely since the sanctum fell empty, who has kept it adequately. Wounds -1 (1-4), -3 (5-8), -5 (9-12), Incapacitated (13-16), Dead (17+). Vis: 2 pawns of Herbam in the leaves of her hair.
creatures.secrets: Bound by her own will to Holzstein's laboratory. Suspicious of intruders, but with respect and kindness she will gladly bond with a new master.

creatures.name: The kobold of the mine
creatures.notes: The book gives no statistics or realm, and calls him old. Treated with respect and small gifts he merely moves things and makes noises in the dark, and may answer a sincere plea; abused, he leads men into dangerous tunnels by illusions, steals their gear, or weakens the rock. Many a vis harvest has met him.

creatures.name: Adler
creatures.appearance: A very large, near-perfect eagle.
creatures.notes: The book gives Size -1, Perception +5 and Might 30 only, with only Cunning, and refers to the Eagle of Virtue (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 41).
creatures.secrets: The founding maga, who took her eagle heartbeast as a Great Beast at her Final Twilight, and watches the peak where Franka's books lie. She hinders climbers, the non-Bjornaer most, with her powers, and stays hidden unless a Bjornaer seeks her with respect.

creatures.name: Gorm
creatures.notes: A powerful faerie lord who plays a king of the northmen; the book gives no statistics. He knows the current politics but nothing of magi, and takes any magus to speak for Collem Leonis. He can reshape his host's look and wear any heraldry. Diplomacy may turn him to subtler help.

was.title: A season at Durenmar
was.says: From the Tribunal's founding: every apprentice trained in the Rhine spends at least one season at Durenmar, taught by a magus of House Bonisagus.

was.title: The laws of hospitality (961 AA)
was.says: A magus may ask hospitality of any lawful Rhine covenant, which must publish its conditions; a guest who accepts them is guaranteed at least three and at most seven years, pays at least three pawns of vis a year, and the conditions are the same for every guest in residence and change only when there are none. A later ruling lets a season's service stand for the vis, and once a guest is accepted the host may not ask him to leave for three whole years while he keeps the conditions (Guardians of the Forests p. 20).

was.title: Proxy sigils (1017 AA)
was.says: Firm rules on the voting of retired magi, ending twenty years of dispute: a master is entrusted with one retired magus's sigil, an archmage with a second, cast in the retired magus's name and, by custom, by his likely wishes. A magus no one has seen for two Tribunals or more counts as retired; his sigil stays valid until his death is shown, and the Redcaps report who has been seen and who has died (Guardians of the Forests p. 16).

was.title: Ranks
was.says: Only a master may take an apprentice (a journeyman's filius is treated as a new hedge recruit); three masters of other covenants, Houses and gilds confer the rank; in any dispute certamen would otherwise settle, the higher rank has the right. House Tremere contests this, as it was made to curb them.

was.title: Founding a covenant (1024 AA)
was.says: A new covenant needs a sponsoring magus from every existing covenant of the Tribunal; one sponsor speaks for a covenant, and none may be one of the founders (the Waldherz ruling). Refused, the founders may try again in seven years; until recognised their covenant has no communal rights or legal recourse, though its magi keep theirs as individuals. Once it is recognised every other covenant gives it a gift. Arae Flaviae and Schwarzburg abolished the same year. Chapter houses need no such leave, which is how Fengheld grows (Guardians of the Forests pp. 16-17).

was.title: Guardians of the Forests (1192 AA)
was.says: Magi have a duty to preserve the forests and magical sites, defend their vis and slow mundane intrusion. A clause House Guernicus had added binds them never to act so as to bring the mundanes' wrath, on pain of the Oath. The ruling has no way of its own to be enforced and its precedents contradict each other. In 1194 Caecilius ruled that the Danish occupation of Rügen is no such destruction, as no wilderness was invaded (Guardians of the Forests p. 18).

was.title: A day's march (1248 AA)
was.says: A magical site within a day's march of a covenant belongs to it; Valdus of Tytalus, who harvested Treverorum's, was fined a pawn as the covenant had lost nothing, and told to ask in future.

was.title: A covenant without a site
was.says: At the Ash Gild's urging the Tribunal founded Oculus Septentrionalis to learn of the Norse wizards, ruling that a covenant needs no site at founding, only magi bound by a charter. In 1158 its magi were fined three pawns each for keeping neither.

was.title: Dankmar against Durenmar
was.says: Durenmar, found to have molested the fay and plundered faerie sites, paid a rook of vis to every other covenant and was barred from faerie sites for fourteen years unless it made peace with them.

was.title: No magic in the Rhine Gorge (1339 AA)
was.says: After Rheinstein was destroyed by the archbishop of Trier's army, largely through its own doing, no magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years: a ban that ends in 1220.

was.title: Waddenzee is Terschelling
was.says: The two survivors of Terschelling renamed it Waddenzee with a new charter and symbol; a vote to call it a new covenant needing leave failed, by the Oak and Ash Gilds. The same year Rethra, silent for decades, was declared abolished.

value.says: After Rheinstein was destroyed by the archbishop of Trier's army, largely through its own doing, no magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years: a ban that ends in 1220.

value.title: Waddenzee is Terschelling
value.says: The two survivors of Terschelling renamed it Waddenzee with a new charter and symbol; a vote to call it a new covenant needing leave failed, by the Oak and Ash Gilds. The same year Rethra, silent for decades, was declared abolished.

value.title: The right of veto
value.says: Existing covenants may veto the founding of a new covenant; a single veto is enough to stop it.

gilds.name: Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
gilds.agenda: The oldest and largest gild, a quarter of the Tribunal: tradition, respect for elders and the Founders, the Rhine's old glory. Bonisagus, Guernicus and Tremere favour it.

gilds.name: Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
gilds.agenda: The smallest: protects the wild places and beasts from mundanes and shuns contact with them; mostly Wilderist Bjornaer.

gilds.name: Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
gilds.agenda: Dominion over the land, a forthright Order, and (unspoken) war on the Order of Odin; Flambeau, Tremere and Tytalus.

gilds.name: Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
gilds.agenda: Split from the Hawthorn: the fae and friendship with them above all; nearly all of Irencillia and Dankmar, with a few Harmonist Bjornaer.

gilds.agenda: Founded after the Schism War by former Fengheld magi: co-operation, peace and an end to apathy; nearly a fifth of the Tribunal, the go-between. Mercere, Jerbiton, Verditius, Tremere and Trianoma's Bonisagus.

A Westphalian town known among those who know of such things as the principal seat of the Holy Vehm, the secret courts of the north.

Rebuilt after a great fire in 1152 and swollen by Frederick Barbarossa's long stay, it became a Free Imperial City in 1220, its trade and craft guilds now a power in the land. The Tremere of Collem Leonis have traded here since the covenant's founding, and evil tongues say they helped it rise.

covenants.name: Didyma
covenants.notes:
Offices and votes. Ten votes sit on the Council of Magi: Alexander 3 (Patriarch, Librarian, resident), Nikola 2 (Strategos, resident), Ariane 2 (Chancellor, resident), Herakles 1, William 1, and Magarethe 1 as archon. The agenda: those present name themselves and their offices; current prophecies are discussed, and the Patriarch presents a new one if a Tribunal is next; new residents are voted on; Chancellor, Strategos, Librarian and archon report; each maga reports her service for the Patriarch's approval; he confirms or names officers; other business.

The Council of Archai rules the covenfolk under the magi, meeting monthly on turb training, laboratory supplies and mundane dealings. Five archai serve five years each, one retiring and one elected each midwinter feast, by majority with equal votes: Magarethe the archon, Callista, Sebasten, Basil and Philip. Visiting magi are expected to follow their hosts' wishes, and visiting grogs and companions the archai's direction.

The turb is 18 fighters (the Standard Soldier, ArM5 p. 22) under two leaders, Philip and Sebasten, and William's four Franks. Two bands of four are based at the warehouses, one on duty, changing with a covenant band each week, the Franks taking their turn. With William leading, the Franks fight as a trained group at +18, or +9 led by one of their own. The Didyma turb often fight in pairs, one with a Defender Sword covering both.

Specialists, 58 Build Points in all: Basil (12), Abbas (8), five young scribes lent by Niketas's monasteries from 15 until each turns 20, with Artes Liberales 2 (logic) and Scribe 4 (quickly) (20), three stonemason's apprentices (12) and Cleon (6).

Branchidae beyond Didyma. Unknown numbers of the line of Bastards, Gifted children of unGifted Branchidae, may be in any House unaware of their birth-right. One magus of the line of Tessa and two of the line of Damen live, and in a great crisis may come to help what is in effect their domus magna. Nikola's tutor's work, with the Diamond of Hermes, should recover some of the Bastards.

Earlier residents. Soteria, Basil, Jason, Brasidas, Tessa, Damen, Lydia and Cora, Branchidae, and Cletus of the Lineage of Pralix; Orion, Verditius then Merinita, and the Merinita Hector, Achillios, Lana and Nicodemus. See the Diary for their dates.

Theme: responding to change. The covenant hangs on threads: the few Branchidae, the tolerance of city and church, the demon's sleep, Miletos's trade. One breaking may tip it into winter. Any resident here suits a player, and further magi may be added or replace them; the oldest Gifted Branchidae holds the title, and new votes shift the balance from Alexander and Nikola, who will resent it. Moved elsewhere, it needs a Mediterranean shore for its temple, or a secret regio; the demon may lie under it anywhere.

Story seeds. Taxation Audit: Nicaea sends auditors after Leander, and Cleon, though clean, looks too close to the covenant. Spice Harvest: the market's vis comes from somewhere, and following it may anger magi at other markets, or another may cut off the supply. The Children of Olympos: its members come to worship and contact the faerie gods, and would dearly like Herakles, who sympathises but thinks himself a god already; Ariane leans their way too.

Storyline, A Sanctuary: nothing changes, and the covenant is a safe, rich base. Herakles and William join adventures, Chloris spies out Constantinople for Ariane, and Torvus steals things.

Storyline, City, Church and War. Niketas dies, and 35 voters (quorum 20, two thirds to win) gather: 25 Miletos priests, 3 of Panormos, 5 abbots and 2 village priests. Father Christos, a charismatic Christian Branchidae, is Alexander's choice; Father Yannis, a sarcastic old deacon from Constantinople, would purge the priests and try the Didyma magi as pagans, and may appeal to Patriarch Manuel. Or lost decrees of the 300s banning the oracle come before the Strategos' court, genuine or forged. Or Quaesitors look into old or new interference. Or Venetians bring in Franks and grab property; a riot hurts a Latin priest, and if he dies Templars may come, so the Strategos asks the magi to heal him. Or Rum strikes the coast; refugees slum outside Miletos, a starving mob walks to Didyma, the Strategos drafts the turb, and Omar Allaid of Panormos offers the pagans a Seljuk licence for magic against Miletos. Neutrality will see the cult outlawed by whoever wins.

Using it from outside. Theban magi and pagans come for prophecy; Christians to destroy the cult; Merinita for the Sacred Way; hunters for a base, with William and Herakles as guides; travellers to take ship for North Africa; Quaesitors for interference; officials to see Nikola.

covenants.summary:
The temple of Apollo at Didyma has had its oracles, on and off, for two thousand years, and Miletos was a rival to Athens when they began. Its symbol is the Eye of the Branchidae. Over a hundred covenfolk live here, most of them born to the family; the magi and some of the people go about in the hooded togas of Roman-era pagan priests, while the rest look and talk like any Greek of Miletos. Visitors are welcome, pagans above all, and any magus without a bad name. An arche meets them, Sebasten or Philip at the temples or Callista in the city, and the Patriarch or the Strategos comes out to anyone exotic.

The covenant's purpose before the Tribunal is to make and interpret prophecies. The Greek magi once escaped the worst of the Schism War on its advice, and magi still come before a great venture. It lives by fees for prophecy and other rites from the Christians of Miletos and the villages, a tenth of them paid to the city, under second-century imperial decrees still good in law, and by renting warehouses at the Lion Harbour, at a premium for their wards. It has also dredged the harbour for over two hundred years.

charter_of_covenant.name: The Charter of the Council of the Magi
charter_of_covenant.preamble: Drafted by Soteria in 990 from the old ways of the Branchidae.

clauses.text: The Patriarch or Matriarch is the most senior resident Gifted Branchidae.

All resident magi meet as a Council of Magi at the winter and summer solstices. A magus becomes resident by a majority vote there or by taking his Gauntlet under a resident. The Patriarch may revoke residency at any time, and a magus away for more than five solstices running has resigned residency and every office.
The Patriarch may call an extraordinary Council on a Moon's notice or more.
Each resident owes a season's service a year, approved by the Patriarch, or else pays 3 pawns of Vim vis to the coffers. Service may be put off, but not past the next Tribunal meeting.
At the Council before each Tribunal meeting the Patriarch must lay before it a prophecy for the covenant.

The Patriarch names a resident Chancellor, who gathers and keeps the coffers. She may trade vis with resident and visiting magi if the coffers end no fewer in pawns; the Patriarch and Strategos may requisition vis; she reports on the coffers to the Council.

The Patriarch names a resident Strategos to answer for all defenses, with the Aegis of the Hearth, whose tokens only the Strategos may give. The Strategos nominally leads and trains the turb, a task Nikola has handed to able servants.
The Patriarch names a resident Librarian, who keeps and copies books and Lab Texts, settles disputes over access, and finds and trains the scriptorium's scribes.
The covenfolk rule themselves through a Council of Archai, elected by them for staggered five-year terms; the longest serving, the archon, speaks for them at the Council of Magi.
Decisions go by majority. Each resident magus and each office has a vote; there are no proxies, so a voter must be present.

covenants.secrets:
Hook: Monster (Major, unknown to all). Agamenoth, a demon prince, sleeps under the plain; his stirring caused the earthquakes.

Storyline, The Sleeping Beast. Woken by the fall of Constantinople, Agamenoth means only destruction. Earthquakes wreck Miletos season after season, leaving a stench of sulphur that may pass for a sigil. His powers should not pierce the Aegis; if it fails, laboratories lose the season, and suffer -3 until a season's tidying. Infernal Lore against 12 knows his Reputation. Mileta smells him but fears questions, and may suggest asking Apollo; he would use her past against her. Old church records in Miletos mention him.

Storyline, The Branchidae. Alexander dies. Lana, with Alexander, cast two wards after Jason's loss that barred the lines of Tessa and Damen (The Tessa and Damen Wards, ReCo(In) 60, Touch, Fire, Boundary, ritual, Base 15; a bloodline primogenitor's Arcane Connection is needed). Their braziers went out by accident in the 1190s and Alexander could not recast them, though Lab Texts may lie in Lana's effects with Herakles. Nestor of Polyaigos, of Damen's line and older than Nikola, comes secretly to Miletos, hires agents to put out flames that are already dead, and claims the title at the solstice, with Io and Kaia waiting in Panormos. Age and descent can be shown by Intellego Corpus. Years later Aristocles the Wanderer comes with three Tremere, Anica, Octavian and Petre, gracious about the title, with a secret purpose: to slay Apollo Didyma, behind a declared Wizard War. Apollo sends the trireme Diakopho, with 200 faerie ghosts of dead Branchidae and a squadron of talkative dolphins, to fetch Erginos the Argonaut, son of a Branchidae woman and Poseidon, from the faerie seas in the Apeiro. If the characters side with Aristocles, Apollo recruits at Panormos.

Niketas's two predecessors of 1170, hostile to pagans, both died suddenly after election, and Michael (metropolitan to 1170) was a Branchidae under a Longevity Ritual: the covenant has long meddled with its bishops.

tribunals.name: The Theban Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Tribunal of the Greek-speaking lands that were the Roman Empire of the East until the crusaders took Constantinople in 1204: mainland Greece and the Morea, Macedonia and Thrace, the Aegean islands and Candia, and the western coasts of Asia Minor, with the half-ruined Queen of Cities at the crossing between the Aegean and the Black Sea. The sea binds it together more than in any other Tribunal: one covenant lives aboard ships, one under the waves, and most of the rest within a short sail of the coast. It holds about a hundred magi. Old gods and spirits crowd the land, and vis is so plentiful that its magi treat it as food, needful but not money; freed of the scramble for it, they have built a society of equals that prizes service to the common good.

Its magi speak Romaic Greek and work the Art in Classical Greek, not Latin; incomers and some Houses keep to Latin, and Gigas campaigns for it. All politai are equal: titles such as Primus or Archmage carry no weight here, though callings such as Quaesitor, Redcap and hoplite are respected.

The polity. Every decision belongs to the Hermetic Assembly, the magi themselves, voting once each by a show of voting sigils, politai and metoikoi alike. A polites (citizen) passed Gauntlet in the Tribunal and keeps his good standing; a metoikos is a guest from elsewhere or a polites who has lost his rights, and wears grey at meetings. Only politai hold tokens and shards or serve as magistrates. Each polites belongs to the phyle of the covenant where his sanctum lies: the Ionian (Erebos, Epidauros, Hedyosmos), the Aegean (Aegaea, Oikos tou Eleous, Ingasia), the Kretan (Alexandria, Favonius, Polyaigos) and the Propontian (Moero's Garden, Gigas, Xylinites, Michael's Tabula).

The Council of Magistrates. Sixteen archai, four from each phyle, are drawn by lot at each meeting for seven years. They prepare and carry out the Assembly's business but decide nothing: three sit on each of the Judicial, Legislative and Conciliatory Boards, and the remaining seven form the Treasury Council (the apodektai), one of them drawn as tamias, four gathering vis and Gifted children, and two as tutors of the children. The book names none of the sixteen or of the board members, nor the present tamias. The archai elect the archon, who chairs the Council and is the Tribunal's Praeco: Aiakia of Hedyosmos since 1214. They also elect the polemarch, who carries out sentences and leads Wizard's Marches with the Tribunal's restraining devices: Maria Laskarina of Polyaigos, chosen in 1207 and again in 1214. The logothete, the Chief Redcap, has held office for life since 1186 and keeps the register of tokens and shards: Leontius of Alexandria, who means to resign in 1221. There is no Presiding Quaesitor: the boards do the Quaesitors' work, and Theban Quaesitors vote like anyone else.

Tokens and shards. A token, a bronze disc stamped with a gorgon's face, rewards a service to the community; a shard of pottery marks an act against the polity's unity, and anyone holding one may be ostracised. Tokens buy the sponsored Longevity Ritual and pay for neutralisation; they may be given away but never traded for vis. The logothete's register is known to be faulty, so the holdings entered here are only what the book implies, and the storyguide should treat the rest as in doubt.

The meeting. The Tribunal meets every seven years on Delos, the floating island that wanders the Cyclades; the last meetings were in 1207 and 1214 and the next is in 1221. The book gives no season, so summer is assumed. Each meeting is run by a principal phyle, in turn Ionian, Aegean, Kretan and Propontian; where the cycle stands now is left to the storyguide. Before it, each phyle dines in its own house on Delos to draw up its candidate list, and magi seeking apprentices interview the Gifted children. Then come four phases: the Hermetic Assembly (the Conciliatory Board's decrees, decrees of citizenship, defamation and contrition, news, the Apprentice Presentation and the ostracism vote), then the Law Council, then the People's Court, and last the Council of Archai (sentences, conduct reviews, the sortition of new archai and the election of archon and polemarch). The Rite of Dismissal closes it, and the magi go down to the sacred lake for the Ceremony of Propitiation, where each covenant honours its patron.

The treasury. Under a leaden trapdoor on Delos, copied from the one at Durenmar and opened only by the archon's iron key, lie several hundred pawns of vis and many old items and texts. The polity gathers about fifty pawns a year from its common sources, Creo and Vim above all, and spends half of it on one sponsored Longevity Ritual a year; the rest pays for the Propitiation, magic for the archai and Redcaps, healing and emergencies.

Questions for 1221: who follows Leontius as logothete (the Redcaps are likely to put forward Proximios); the League Against Idolatry's petition against the Ceremony of Propitiation; Frankish newcomers who chafe at the polity; and, further off, Tremere's appeal to the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to retry the last two magi of the League of Advisors.

Stories. Four are under way in 1220: the League of the Vigilant's first recruiting (An Enemy Within), the meeting on Delos in 1221, Epiros's war on Thessaloniki and Nicaea's on the Latins. Others wait for the storyguide to begin them, from Klymene's prison at Pergamos and the lost covenant of Wilusa to the Tremere appeal of 1228 and the Verditius Contest of 1234.

Smaller seeds. Young magi lending their Parma Magica to the Gifted children before the Apprentice Presentation, who whisper that unchosen children vanish; a Gifted boy who bonded with the arche lodging him, then fled his new Tytalus master with stolen enchanted items to rule a band of robbers. A god seen near Olympos who looks like a magus lost to Final Twilight; a girl at Delphi who says Pythia is gone and repeats a prophecy of her rescue; the Prince of Achaea fallen ill, his wife begging Epidauros for a cure that either way looks like meddling. The despot of Rodos, who has seized every book on his island and listens to a sinister hedge wizard; the scattered Julian Library, hunted by every Seeker; Formosos's crusade to prove Passara a court wizard; and the mysterious French knight who killed the Sultan of Rum in 1211 and saved the Nicene emperor, perhaps a magus in disguise, whom a senior magus wants unmasked before the meeting. In Constantinople the Latin clergy may suppress the procession of icons on the Feast of Orthodoxy, and riot will follow. Nearer home: a merchant ruined by swarms of flies, a Persian wizard hunting his ancestor's amulet, a triton lord at war with a covenant's fishermen, a family house-snake that follows its magus to a new covenant, a tree spirit freed when its fruit is all taken, and a guardian owl-spirit a covenant might court as its patron.
tribunals.history:
Heroes and city-states. The Greeks tell of five races of men, from the golden race under Kronos to the present race of iron, and St. Jerome's Chronicon sets the heroes' deeds beside the Bible's: Perseus and Medusa, the Argonauts, Theseus and the Trojan War. The historians who followed, Herodotus, Thucydides, Xenophon and Polybios, wrote the gods out of their accounts. Persia's invasions were beaten at Marathon, Salamis and Plataea, though its kings brought sorcerers, jinn and fly-spirits to war, and the Greek theurgists turned to the Witches of Thessaly to bind them. The Delian League met on Delos; Athens and Sparta then fought the Peloponnesian War from 431 to 404 BC.

Macedon and Rome. Philip II of Macedon mastered Greece, and Alexander conquered Persia, the romances say with sorcery learned from his true father Nectanabus, and cursed his sister into the half-fish Gorgona. His successors split the world into warring kingdoms, and the leagues of Greek cities rose and fell until Rome took Macedonia in 168 BC and the rest of Greece in 146 BC. Paul preached at Athens and Corinth, Diocletian divided the empire, and Constantine, after his vision at the Milvian Bridge, called the Council of Nicaea in 325 and in 330 founded Constantinople, ploughing its bounds to bind its spirits under a great Divine ward.

Justinian and the Arabs. The Goths beat the eastern army at Adrianople in 378 and lorded it in the capital until a riot drove them out in 400. Justinian codified Roman law, built Hagia Sophia and crushed the Nika riot of 532, at a cost of thirty thousand dead in the Hippodrome; demons may have steered its Blue and Green factions for centuries. Phocas's tyranny let the Slavs settle across Greece until Heraclius beheaded him in 610 and beat Persia at Nineveh. The Arabs took North Africa by 711 and besieged the capital in 674 to 678 and 717 to 718, and the empire was reordered into military themes.

Icons and Bulgars. The emperors' war on icons lasted a century, until the Regent Theodora restored them for good in 843; Empress Irene had already been exiled to Lesbos in 802. The Bulgars founded a state in the Balkans in 680 and, despite their conversion by Cyril and Methodius in 864, fought the empire for the Balkans, often with House Tremere's favour. From 800 the empire pushed the Slavs out of Greece, and under the Macedonian dynasty, from 867, it retook Crete, Cyprus, Antioch and Tarsus, though Sicily was lost in 902. The Image of Edessa came to Hagia Sophia in 944, the Great Lavra opened on Mount Athos in 955, Emperor Ioannes I broke the Rus with a thirteenth charge in 971, Basil II began his reign in 976, and the Paulicians won freedom of worship in 990.

cases.title: The logothete's succession
cases.charge: Leontius regrets taking the office and means to resign at the meeting of 1221, so a new logothete must be chosen. House Mercere's choice is the subject of much guessing; Proximios of Alexandria is the name most often heard.

cases.title: The faulty register of tokens and shards
cases.charge: Under Leontius records have gone astray and the book of tokens and shards has been found unreliable. He narrowly escaped ostracism in 1214, and the polity will want the register put right before ostracism or the Longevity Ritual depends on it.

cases.title: Against the Ceremony of Propitiation
cases.brought_by: The League Against Idolatry (Oikos tou Eleous and Gigas)
cases.charge: The league asks the Legislative Board to end the Ceremony of Propitiation and the Tribunal's recognition of patrons, saying the altars and vis offerings on Delos have passed from veneration into worship, a mortal sin that endangers every magus who takes part. Under the Code its petition must offer a replacement ruling. Artoud of Xylinites gives it fitful support; the issue stirs anger every time it is raised.

cases.title: Caterina da Vigonovo's citizenship
cases.charge: A Venetian Gauntleted in Rome and newly settled at Polyaigos, Caterina is a metoikos and distrusted for her city's part in the sack. She wants the Tribunal to sponsor her Longevity Ritual and is working to build her name; as a metoikos she can hold no tokens, so she needs a decree of citizenship, with an arche to sponsor her, first.

cases.title: Nanno and Ampelius
cases.charge: Ziper wants the craftsmen Nanno and Ampelius, unGifted makers of minor enchanted wares, taken into Moero's Garden as members of House Jerbiton; Proximios backs him and Syagricus does not object, but the rest of the covenant is appalled at admitting tradesmen. The two artisans threaten to sail to Delos and ask the whole Tribunal.

cases.title: Passara and the Latin emperor
cases.charge: Formosos, grandson in the Art of Vaanes, holds that Vaanes wrongly shielded Aella, the maker of the Magnaura's automata, and means to prove that Passara, her heir who tends them from rooms in the palace, actually works for the Latin emperor. He is looking for magi to investigate her quietly.

cases.title: The mysterious knight of 1211
cases.charge: Greek chroniclers say an unknown Frankish knight appeared from nowhere at Antioch-on-the-Maeander and killed Sultan Kaykhusraw as he stood over the fallen Theodore Laskaris, saving the Empire of Nicaea. Rumour says it was a magus in disguise, which would be gross interference; a senior magus wants it solved before the meeting of 1221.

cases.title: Normalising the Tribunal
cases.charge: Gigas condemns the polity's 'vulgar paganism' and works to bring the Tribunal into line with the rest of the Order: Latin over Greek, new precedents, and reviewing every law it can when one of its magi sits on the Legislative Board. It helped make the logothete permanent. The few Frankish magi who came east after 1204 are pushing for changes of their own.

cases.title: A covenant in Constantinople again
cases.brought_by: Young Jerbiton magi and their apprentices
cases.charge: Many Jerbiton, above all the apprentices soon to be Gauntleted, want to reclaim the city and found a covenant inside its walls, as Thermakopolis was. The Tribunal has not decided whether to encourage it, and most would rather wait and see.

cases.title: Tremere's appeal over the League of Advisors
cases.against: The two surviving magi of the League of Advisors
cases.charge: The League of Advisors sat openly at the emperor's court from 1185, claiming only to advise. After 1204 it was blamed for meddling and broke up, and the Tribunal failed to convict its members. Tremere has asked the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to hear the case of its last two members again; if it succeeds, the autonomy of every Tribunal, and the Theban polity above all, may suffer.

cases.title: Ingasia's sales to Nicaea
cases.charge: Secret. Without their parens Stouritus noticing, the twins sell more enchanted items to mundanes than the Code's five a year, favouring the Nicene Greeks, Venice's sworn enemies, and raise Ingasia's wealth slowly so no one remarks it. Their autocrat sees the money but asks no questions. A case can be brought only once someone finds out.

rulings.title: The polity
rulings.says: When the Tribunal was made, its magi brought its government back toward the Typikon of Prokopios. The Hermetic Assembly, every magus present, decides all things by majority, one voting sigil each, politai and metoikoi alike; the magistrates chosen by lot prepare and carry out its business but have no vote or power of their own. The magistrates, not the parties, gather the evidence in a case, and the Assembly, not the Quaesitores, settles guilt and sentence. The Code is judged afresh in each case, without precedent.

rulings.title: Politai and metoikoi
rulings.says: A polites passed Gauntlet in the Tribunal and stays in good standing. A metoikos is a magus from another Tribunal, or a polites who has lost his rights, and can hold neither tokens nor shards; he is punished by fines or ostracism instead. A metoikos may ask the Assembly for a decree of citizenship if he lives at an established covenant, can show he has served the polity, and has an arche to sponsor him; a new polites cannot be drawn as arche at the meeting that made him one.

rulings.title: The phylai and the sortition
rulings.says: Every polites belongs to the phyle of the covenant where his sanctum is: Ionian, Aegean, Kretan or Propontian. Each phyle sends four archai, drawn by lot from its politai who are not serving and consent to stand; a magus who is eligible but refuses earns a shard. Archai serve seven years, never two terms running, and never on the same board twice. Redcaps belong to the phylai but are not drawn; they fill board seats no arche can.

rulings.title: The officers
rulings.says: The archai elect one of their number as archon, the Tribunal's Praeco and chair of the Council, who may serve more than once; by custom an arche with no preference votes for the eldest magus on the Council. They elect the polemarch from all the politai, and only a former polemarch may decline; the same magus is often chosen again and again. The polemarch may award tokens to the magi she names to help her carry out a Wizard's March, and has the use of the Tribunal's devices that bind a magus's body and Gift. The logothete, the Chief Redcap, was once chosen every seven years, but since 1186 holds office until death, Twilight, resignation or a vote of no confidence among the Redcaps, and earns no tokens for it.

rulings.title: The Judicial Board
rulings.says: Prepares every charge of a High Crime and may take over any matter before the other boards that plainly breaks the Oath. A prosecution and a defence principal are drawn by lot from its members and must share what they find. In haste, as over the unlawful slaying of a magus or diabolism, it may call an interim Tribunal of at least twelve magi from four covenants, and the polemarch fetches the accused.

rulings.title: The Legislative Board
rulings.says: Reviews the Peripheral Code. Any polites may ask for a change, but must offer a replacement: no ruling can simply be repealed. Two members drawn by lot argue for the old ruling and the new before the Law Council at the next meeting, where the Assembly votes. A polites who fears conviction may seek a review of the law first, at the risk of having no defence left if it fails.

rulings.title: The Conciliatory Board
rulings.says: Hears quarrels between magi, over land, resources, or between master and apprentice, and investigates an apprentice's death. It solemnises binding agreements, such as shares of vis sources, the founding of covenants and new members' Oaths, and issues decrees of contrition. A settlement is binding only when the whole board agrees it was fair; its decrees are read to the Assembly, which may overturn them.

rulings.title: Convening a board
rulings.says: No board can call itself together: a polites with a complaint applies through its Redcap, and the board must meet within six months, somewhere convenient or relevant. An arche who needs a board applies as a citizen, and may not sit when his own case is heard.

rulings.title: Tokens and shards
rulings.says: Tokens are earned by service: two for a term as arche, three as archon, five as polemarch; one for gathering a common vis source in a Tribunal period; one for a requested service, a Longevity Ritual made for the treasurer (two at tenth magnitude or more), a Gifted child delivered, or seven and fourteen years of apprentice training without abuse; one for a prosecution that convicts and three if it ends in a March; and what the polemarch awards those who join a March at her call. Shards punish harm: three for a High Crime and one for a Low, one for a failed prosecution, losing or suffering a decree of defamation, refusing candidacy, neglect of an arche's duty or a promised task, or abusing an apprentice, and two for withholding a Gifted child. A token holder may ask a shard holder for a season's service; if he agrees before a Redcap, each surrenders one, but not within one covenant. A decree of contrition, with a reparation the magus chooses, also clears a shard. Tokens may be given, never exchanged for vis.

rulings.title: Ostracism
rulings.says: Every polites holding a shard is named at the Assembly, and the magi vote which of them stand as candidates; then each writes a name, or 'no one', on a potsherd. The magus named most often loses his citizenship, must leave the Tribunal within a season, may not return for seven years, and comes back only as a metoikos.

rulings.title: Common vis sources
rulings.says: Vis from the shrines of the old gods and certain mythic sites is held to belong to everyone, and the Code lists these sources. The Treasury Council assigns their gathering, which earns a token, and the vis goes to the Tribunal's coffers.

rulings.title: The sponsored Longevity Ritual
rulings.says: Each year the Tribunal pays for one Longevity Ritual. Any polites with no shards and no working ritual may apply to the tamias by spring; the one with most tokens, the elder on a tie, wins and gives up all of them. Winners usually hold three or four. The rituals are customarily made at Epidauros.

rulings.title: Healing
rulings.says: A capable magus asked to heal a sodalis is expected to, paying the vis himself; the healed customarily gives back about half of it, and the healer earns a token. The coffers pay only when neither can. A covenant bears the cost of healing its own members at home, and no token is given.

rulings.title: Gifted children
rulings.says: Whoever finds a Gifted child must tell the Treasury Council, which houses and schools the children until the Apprentice Presentation before each meeting. Masters without a shard, and any Bonisagus, interview them and bid tokens; a child bid for by several chooses her master, and keeps his tokens. Under pressure from Tytalus, the Conciliatory Board holds that following the Book of Instruction is not abuse.

rulings.title: Covenant patrons
rulings.says: Every covenant is bound by a pact of mutual protection to a patron, a spirit, god, genius loci, saint or faerie living within it, and honours it at the Ceremony of Propitiation. A patron known to be Infernal would not be tolerated. A covenant whose patron dies must find another quickly, or is held to have died with it.

rulings.title: Founding a covenant
rulings.says: A new covenant must declare its purpose, secure a willing patron at its site and draw up a charter. The Conciliatory Board checks all three, and the Assembly then votes a decree of founding, usually a formality once the board approves.

rulings.title: The peace of Delos
rulings.says: No one may be killed or born on Delos: the magi still keep the old ban for fear of Zeus. No pregnant women or beasts, and no predatory animals, familiars included, are allowed there during a meeting, and executions are carried out at sea or on another island.

rulings.title: Certamen
rulings.says: Certamen is for real disputes only. Using it to claim precedence offends the equality of politai, and duelling over a vis find is thought especially rude: the finders share it, or the richer yields.

rulings.title: Enchanted items sold to mundanes
rulings.says: Through intermediaries, a Theban magus may sell up to five enchanted items a year to mundanes, where many Tribunals allow one. Items of Quality are not counted as enchanted items. Both rules are Stouritus of Ingasia's work.

rulings.title: No preying on Hermetic ships
rulings.says: Magi and covenants may not prey on one another's shipping. Piracy against mundanes is not forbidden, though frowned on.

rulings.title: Classical Greek
rulings.says: Just before the Sundering, the Tribunal's magi recast Hermetic magic in Classical Greek, chosen over the spoken tongue for its weight and the power of a dead language, and it remains the Tribunal's Hermetic language. A magus with no Classical Greek has -10 to tell the Form of a Greek spell, or -5 below an effective score of 4; Theban magi suffer the same against Latin. The app does not enforce this.

diary.title: The League of Iconophiles
diary.details: Early in the eighth century Greek wizards band together as the League of Iconophiles, to rescue holy images from the emperors bent on destroying them. It is the first league worth naming, and its charter is the typikon of Prokopios, a pre-Hermetic wizard with the Gentle Gift who said the spirit of Aristotle had dictated it to him. Some thirty years into their struggle the league's leaders meet Trianoma; they turn down her offer, but the meeting gives rise to House Jerbiton. (The book gives no exact year.)

diary.title: Tremere raids Greece; the Theban League
diary.details: House Tremere invades Greece, killing wizards and carrying off their vis and enchanted items. None of the dead belong to the Order, so no Oath is broken. The Greek wizards unite as the Theban League to drive the raiders back, and when followers of Jerbiton and Trianoma renew the invitation to join the Order, many accept, since the Tremere will not attack fellow members. That protection, more than any battle, ends the raids. Among the League are three wizards of Hedyosmos, the youngest of whom Guernicus himself teaches Hermetic magic, and the healers who had restored the old sanctuary of Epidauros. The enchanters of Hephaistos's forge on Lemnos join in the same years: Ingasia is younger than Verdi in law, though its members hold it the older forge.

diary.title: Dorostolon founded
diary.details: Tremere magi found Dorostolon, a fortress covenant on the south bank of the Danube in Bulgaria. Several of the Founder's most powerful lieutenants make it their base for his plan to rule the Order. In these years Tremere magi also seize the sanctuary of Epidauros for a time.

diary.title: The Sundering of Tremere
diary.details:
Theban magi intercept letters revealing Tremere's design to make himself master of the Order, and learn that his chief lieutenants will gather at Dorostolon. A hidden force slips into the covenant and shatters the minds and loyalties of the lieutenants, and the fortress is torn apart. No one claims the deed. Local opinion holds that magi of Hedyosmos, with others, loosed the Titan Typhon from its bonds, struck a pact with it and sent it against Dorostolon before binding it again. Tremere dies soon afterwards, and the Tremere usurpers are driven from Epidauros.

Secrets
Hedyosmos keeps its own records of these years. Tremere magi would dearly like to read them, and none is welcome there.

diary.title: Erebos founded
diary.details: Not long after the Sundering, envoys of the young House Ex Miscellanea reach Thebes, among them a filius of Pralix sent to deal with the Witches of Thessaly. A few of the witches, led by the maga Cyra, agree to join the Order. Unwilling to leave home, Cyra founds a covenant in the Cambunian mountains and charges it with keeping alive every native Greek tradition that Tremere had threatened, naming it Erebos, the darkness. (The book places this only in the second half of the ninth century.)

diary.title: The Theban Tribunal instituted
diary.details: The sixth Grand Tribunal formally creates the Theban Tribunal and names it for the Theban League. Its lands run from the Ionian Sea to the Black Sea, taking in the Bulgars' country and Anatolia; Coeris, Tremere's home, is its only domus magna, a sign of how little the Order then trusts that House. The League's heirs at once pass Peripheral Code rulings that bring the Tribunal's government closer to the typikon of Prokopios: the polity, in which the Hermetic Assembly decides everything and archai drawn by lot only prepare and carry out its business.

diary.title: The automata of the Magnaura
diary.details: Early in the tenth century the Cretan-born Aella of House Verditius builds the automata of the Palace of Magnaura in Constantinople. Accused more than once of serving the emperor as a court wizard, she is never convicted, thanks largely to the legal skill of her husband, Vaanes of House Guernicus; she is twice ostracised and twice comes back to tend her creations. (The book gives no exact year.)

diary.title: Estropi founded
diary.details: A sept of Bjornaer magi, every one with the heartbeast of a bird of prey, founds Estropi on Mount Erciyes, the highest peak of central Anatolia.

diary.title: The Transylvanian Tribunal split off
diary.details: The rise of the Bulgarian Empire some thirty years after 865, and House Tremere's slow recovery and growth, persuade the ninth Grand Tribunal that the Theban Tribunal is too large to govern. Its northern lands become the Transylvanian Tribunal, and the Theban borders have not moved since.

diary.title: Grammaton founded
diary.details: Grammaton of House Bonisagus and his filii found a covenant, named for him, to pursue original research into the magic of binding.

diary.title: Diadelphia founded
diary.details: The brothers Cosmas and Baztas of House Verditius found Diadelphia on the island of Kalymnos. Other Verditius magi join them, but the brothers' bitter rivalry drives the newcomers away again.

diary.title: Basil II invades Bulgaria
diary.details: As the Schism War dies away in the west (the Tribunal took almost no part, though a few Greek magi fought in it), a Byzantine army invades Bulgaria. After his victory at Kleidion, Basil II is said to blind fourteen thousand prisoners, sparing one eye in every hundred men to lead the rest home, and Tsar Samuel dies of the shock at the sight. House Tremere insists Theban magi helped the emperor; nothing is proved, though some Jerbiton with the Gentle Gift are close to the imperial family.

diary.title: Bulgaria conquered
diary.details: Basil II completes the conquest of the Bulgarian state, which becomes a part of the empire, and restores the old northern frontier on the Danube.

diary.title: Aegaea founded
diary.details: The Merinita maga Orithyia, coming back from Arcadia, says she was led through the sea by a golden man with a dolphin's tail, whom she takes for Triton, Poseidon's herald. She makes a pact with him to dwell in the undersea palace he showed her, which she takes for Poseidon's own, and names her covenant Aegaea after it, with Triton as patron. The Tribunal doubts her until Redcaps confirm the place and its splendour. (The book says only about two centuries ago.)

diary.title: Gigas founded
diary.details: Gigas is founded in the forests south-west of Sofia as a place for magi and trusted companions wounded in the Schism War to recover. The Tribunal suspects its purpose from the start.

diary.title: Death of Basil II
diary.details: Basil II, the Bulgar-Slayer, dies without an heir after the most victorious reign in the empire's history. Some say it was God's punishment for his cruelty, and for marrying his sister Anna, born in the purple, to Vladimir of Kiev against the law.

diary.title: The last emperor buried at the Holy Apostles
diary.details: Constantine VIII is laid to rest in the Church of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople, the last emperor buried there.

diary.title: The orphanage of St. Christopoulos
diary.details: Emperor Romanos III Argyros, Zoe's first husband, endows a school and orphanage at the monastery of St. Christopoulos in Constantinople, paid for by the treasury and run by the monks. The monastery itself dates from 823.

diary.title: The icon of St. Loukia
diary.details: Romanos III gives the monastery of St. Christopoulos a tiny and exquisite icon of a little-known saint, St. Loukia.

diary.title: Kyddopetre founded
diary.details: A group of Flambeau magi founds Kyddopetre at the Cilician Gates, the narrow pass through the Taurus mountains into southern Anatolia.

diary.title: Polyaigos founded
diary.details: Stringes witches nest on the Cycladic island of Polyaigos and plague the isles around it, Delos among them, sheltering a renegade Flambeau. At the Assembly's call the hoplite Quaesitor Laskaris fights his way ashore, allies with Varazes, a drakos giant native to the island, and shields him in a duel while the giant clubs the renegade to death. Having cleansed the island, Laskaris founds a covenant there and pledges it to the swift defence of the Tribunal. (The book says only that this happened in the 11th century.)

diary.title: The Great Schism
diary.details: Rome and Constantinople finally break over the filioque, the Latin claim that the Spirit proceeds from the Son as well as the Father. Few think it a disaster at the time, but the breach has widened into deep mistrust.

diary.title: End of the Macedonian dynasty
diary.details: The Macedonian dynasty, under which Byzantine power reached its height, ends with the empresses Zoe and Theodora, born in the purple. Zoe, who ruled through four husbands, collected magical amulets and automata, some of which may still survive; after her death the mob put her sister on the throne in place of her last husband.

diary.title: Miphoria fades; the Crown of Thorns comes to Constantinople
diary.details: Miphoria, the first covenant of House Mercere, on the coast near Smyrna, had ridden giant magical sea turtles; the Tribunal told its Redcaps to draw less mundane notice, and without the turtles the covenant withered. By this year most of its Redcaps have moved to other covenants. In the same year the Crown of Thorns is brought from the Holy Land to Hagia Sophia.

diary.title: English axemen in the Varangian Guard
diary.details: After the Norman Conquest of England, Anglo-Saxon exiles take the place of the Norsemen in the emperor's Varangian Guard.

diary.title: Cosmas ostracised; Diadelphia disbanded
diary.details: Cosmas of Diadelphia is ostracised, and to everyone's surprise his rival brother Baztas leaves the Tribunal with him. With no magi left, Diadelphia is disbanded by default.

diary.title: Gigas closes to all but Tremere; Estropi flees
diary.details: Gigas adopts a rule of admitting only magi of House Tremere, which deepens the Tribunal's distrust. In the same year the Bjornaer of Estropi abandon Mount Erciyes before the advancing Seljuk Turks.

diary.title: Manzikert
diary.details: At Manzikert the Seljuk horse archers wear down Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes, and Andronikos Doukas, commanding the reserve, deliberately withdraws and leaves him to be captured. Alp Arslan frees Romanos on generous terms within a week, but the Doukas blind him and repudiate the treaty, and the furious Seljuks overrun the Anatolian plateau, the empire's granary. The Byzantine magi living there flee and never return. The icon of St. Loukia cries out a warning before the battle, and in this year Tikh of Jerbiton, teaching at the orphanage, notices the icon's strange properties: it portrays Loukia of Berytus, a Montanist executed for blasphemy, and a Magic aura grows round it.

diary.title: Xylinites founded
diary.details: Needing room for a laboratory, Tikh of Jerbiton clears and partly drains a great vaulted cistern beneath the orphanage of St. Christopoulos and founds Xylinites there, with the icon of St. Loukia as its heart. For the next 130 years its magi teach at the orphanage, find Gifted foundlings, and build influence in the palace through the eunuchs the school sends there.

diary.title: Alexandria founded
diary.details: Methodius, the best-loved Redcap of his day, who claims descent from Alexander and found the king's flying device in Seljuk lands, chooses an old fortress on Mount Pagus above Smyrna for a second Mercere covenant. He binds an eidolon lingering among the ghosts of Alexander's army as its patron, leaves the walls in ruin to avoid notice, and finishes building this year, naming the covenant Alexandria.

diary.title: Kyddopetre disbanded
diary.details: With Cilicia lost to the Sultanate of Rum after Manzikert, the Flambeau of Kyddopetre, though breaking no law by living outside the empire, feel too cut off from their Greek sodales and disband.

diary.title: Alexios Komnenos takes the throne; the Normans land
diary.details: After the rebellions of Michael VII and Nikephoros Botaneiates, the general Alexios Komnenos seizes the throne in a daring coup. The same year Robert Guiscard of Sicily (the book calls him king) takes Durazzo with Norman knights and Saracen horse, beats the Byzantine army and marches into Greece; when he is called home, his son Bohemond overruns Macedonia and much of Thessaly.

diary.title: Venice at Rodos
diary.details: The Republic of Venice sets up the naval base on Rodos that it still keeps.

diary.title: Anna Komnene born
diary.details: Anna, the eldest of the nine children of Alexios Komnenos, is born in the purple. In old age she will write the Alexiad, her life of her father.

diary.title: Plague ends the Norman war
diary.details: A terrible plague breaks out in Bohemond's camp and ends the Norman invasion.

diary.title: The Pechenegs crushed at Levounion
diary.details: A great host of Pecheneg nomads invades. Allied with the Cumans, the Byzantines all but wipe them out at Levounion; the survivors sue for peace, and Pecheneg and Cuman horsemen have served in imperial armies ever since.

diary.title: Grammaton disbanded
diary.details: After more than a century, and some notable discoveries, it is plain that Grammaton's research into binding magic will never reach its goal. The covenant disbands and its magi join others.

diary.title: A Latin patriarch of Antioch
diary.details: When crusaders take Antioch a Latin patriarch is set up there, driving the Orthodox patriarch into exile; his successor Dorotheus now lives at Nicaea. (The book dates this 1095; Antioch actually fell in 1098.)

diary.title: The First Crusade
diary.details: Answering the emperor's plea for help, Pope Urban preaches a crusade. Alexios wanted mercenaries, not armies that might keep his lost lands, and has the crusaders shadowed by Pecheneg and Cuman horse as they plunder their way across the empire. He refuses to ship them to Asia until their lords swear to return former imperial lands; only Raymond of Toulouse keeps his word, and each side comes away feeling betrayed. (The book dates the crusade 1091 to 1108.)

diary.title: A second Holy Lance
diary.details: During the First Crusade a second, longer lance is found, which also seems to be a true relic.

diary.title: Ephesus recovered
diary.details: After nearly forty years of Seljuk rule, Ephesus returns to the empire and is renamed Hagios Theologos, but it dwindles to a few hundred souls by a silted harbour.

diary.title: The Court of Fools founded
diary.details: Mystics and soothsayers of House Ex Miscellanea form the Court of Fools, a wandering covenant that travels the Greek mainland.

diary.title: Wilusa founded and lost
diary.details:
After many such proposals, the Tribunal finally lets Droserius of House Merinita and four companions found Wilusa at Ilion, where he says the spirit of the river Scamander, dwelling in a regio, has promised to be their patron. By the next Tribunal the covenant and all its magi have vanished, and no search finds any trace. The Tribunal has refused every later plan for a covenant there.

Secrets
Droserius and his companions are trapped in one of Ilion's Faerie regiones, made to fight the fall of Troy over and over.

diary.title: Petronas becomes logothete
diary.details: Petronas of House Mercere begins nearly a hundred years as the Tribunal's logothete. (The book says only that he served for almost a century before 1207.)

diary.title: Genoa and Pisa win trading rights
diary.details: With Alexios fighting the Turks in Asia, the fleets of Genoa and Pisa gather off the Ionian coast and force trading privileges like those Venice already holds. Native Greek trade and the imperial fleet decline from this time.

diary.title: Thermakopolis founded
diary.details: Jerbiton magi found Thermakopolis in Constantinople, sworn to preserve and protect the city: the pride, and later the shame, of their House.

diary.title: Ioannes II Komnenos
diary.details: Ioannes II, a pious and swarthy man called both the Beautiful and the Moor, succeeds his father despite palace plots. When he revokes the Venetians' privileges, their fleet seizes several great islands, and he has to restore them to win the islands back.

diary.title: Lamites founded
diary.details: Magi devoted to prophecy found Lamites in Anatolia and claim the Phrygian Sibyl as their patron.

diary.title: Lamites destroyed
diary.details: Everyone at Lamites dies, most believe at the hands of Lamia, angered by their presumption; it may instead have been the faerie Lamia, resenting rivals.

diary.title: Manuel I Komnenos
diary.details: Manuel I, tall, athletic, a great huntsman, warrior and notorious seducer, takes the throne.

diary.title: The Second Crusade; Roger II takes Thebes
diary.details: The Second Crusade passes through the empire with more looting and ends in disaster, and relations with the crusaders sink further. About this time Roger II of Sicily ravages the Morea, takes Thebes and Athens, and carries the Theban silk industry, workers and all, off to Sicily; Thebes later recovers. (The book dates the crusade 1143 to 1149 and puts Roger's raid in the middle of the century.)

diary.title: Thumachia founded
diary.details: Mostly Jerbiton magi found Thumachia to guard the Tribunal's western border after the ravages of the Second Crusade, treading carefully between meddling in mundane affairs and protecting their sodales.

diary.title: Euboea sacked
diary.details: William I of Sicily, called the Bad, lands ten thousand men from 164 ships and sacks every coastal town of Euboea, which never recovers its old prosperity.

diary.title: Moero's Garden founded
diary.details: Ionnia of House Jerbiton, a minor noble who loves the women poets, finds the house of the poet Moero in one of Constantinople's empty quarters, summons her ghost as patron and invites aristocratic Jerbiton sodales to join her. The covenant is pledged to recovering early Byzantine art and letters, and its members must live, like senators, from land others work.

diary.title: Memnos plans Favonius
diary.details: On his travels through mainland Greece, Memnos of Verditius meets Dryops, the spirit of an oak forest, who is bored and longs to see the world. Memnos has the forest felled and carried to his workshop on Andros, the spirit with it, and spends decades planning a ship of its wood that the spirit will inhabit and fill with a Magic regio. Having grown terrified of the sea, he gives the finished Philomela to his apprentice to captain; when the Procne joins her, the covenant takes the name Favonius. In these years too Ausculator takes his mater's place at the head of Hedyosmos. (The book says some fifty years ago.)

diary.title: War with Venice
diary.details: When the Genoese colony at Galata is burned, Manuel blames Venice and imprisons ten thousand Venetians in Constantinople. The Venetian fleet sails against the empire, but plague strikes it at Chios and it limps home carrying death to Venice; peace follows and the prisoners go free.

diary.title: Renier of Montferrat marries Maria Komnene
diary.details: Boniface of Montferrat's brother Renier marries Maria Komnene, giving the family the claim to Thessaloniki that Boniface will later press. Manuel I dies this year, leaving an infant heir; about now Andronikos Komnenos builds the palace of Nymphaion south of Smyrna.

diary.title: Andronikos enters Constantinople; the Latins massacred
diary.details:
Andronikos Komnenos rides into Constantinople at the head of an army and has his rivals murdered, Renier of Montferrat among them. The mob turns on the Venetians and then on every Westerner, killing tens of thousands, even the sick in their beds. Venice and Montferrat do not forget.

Secrets
Andronikos, exiled for plotting against Manuel, had sold his soul to a demon in a woman's shape for the throne.

diary.title: Andronikos the Tyrant crowned
diary.details: Andronikos I becomes emperor and rules by torture and executions.

diary.title: The sack of Thessaloniki
diary.details:
William II of Sicily takes Durazzo without a fight and marches along the Via Egnatia. In August Thessaloniki falls: its defenders inexplicably run out of missiles, the walls give way as if by magic, St. Demetrios does not rise to defend it, and five thousand die amid unheard-of sacrilege, leaving a strong Infernal aura. Thumachia is sacked in the same war; its survivors join Thermakopolis. In answer to the outrage two holy magae, the sisters Anna and Theocharista Psellus, found the convent of Koukoubiou and with it Oikos tou Eleous, the House of Mercy; the novice Gemma has been with them ever since.

Secrets
Behind the sack the sisters find a widespread diabolist circle among the Paulicians of Thessaloniki, which they still fight.

diary.title: Andronikos falls; Isaac II Angelos
diary.details: Andronikos orders hundreds more executions; the mob rises from Hagia Sophia, his soldiers refuse to fire on it, and he is caught, blinded in one eye, and tortured to death in the streets, while the palaces and many relics are plundered. His ghost still rides on moonless nights. Isaac II Angelos is raised to the throne, and the rising spreads to Thessaloniki, where the Sicilians are routed and cut down. The same year House Tremere backs the lords leading a Bulgarian revolt with advice and materials, though not troops; in reply a few Greek magi form the League of Advisors and go to court in Constantinople, offering counsel unpaid and keeping just short of the forbidden role of court wizard.

diary.title: The logothete made permanent
diary.details: The Tribunal passes a motion making the logothete, until now elected from the Redcaps every seven years, a permanent post, to spare the bureaucracy a changing administration. A new logothete is chosen only on death, Twilight, resignation or a failed vote of confidence among the Redcaps.

diary.title: Barbarossa's crusade; the battle standard lost
diary.details: Frederick Barbarossa's crusade marches overland through the empire; Isaac's own envoys urge him to take Constantinople, he occupies Philippopolis and Didymoteichon, and Isaac must ferry his army across the Bosporus. Isaac then leads the army of Constantinople against the rebel Bulgarians and is routed; the imperial battle standard, a holy relic of the emperors, is last seen in that army.

diary.title: Richard takes Rodos
diary.details: During the Third Crusade Richard the Lionheart takes Rodos and recruits its sailors.

diary.title: Alexios III Angelos
diary.details: In April Isaac II is overthrown and blinded by his brother, who becomes Alexios III and pays for tribute to the German emperor Henry VI with the hated Alamanikon tax. Central authority crumbles; Leo Sgouros makes himself master of the Morea, and local rulers spring up across the mainland.

diary.title: The crusaders sack Zara
diary.details:
The Fourth Crusade, meant for Egypt, cannot pay Venice for the fleet it ordered after far fewer knights arrive than planned. To reduce the debt the crusaders take and plunder Zara, a Christian city, for Venice, and the pope excommunicates them. At Zara Prince Alexios, son of the deposed Isaac, offers money and troops if they will restore his father.

Secrets
Infernal agents worked in every army of the crusade. Their excommunication left the knights without Divine protection, and several nobles made pacts with demons; the whole design was the work of Akgah, a prince of Hell.

diary.title: The first siege of Constantinople
diary.details: Porphyrio, the giant whale that Belisarius once fought, surfaces in April, a week before the Venetian fleet fills the Sea of Marmara. In June the crusaders storm the tower at Galata and break the great chain across the Golden Horn. After a month's siege Alexios III flees by night, and the prince is crowned Alexios IV beside his blind father, Isaac II.

diary.title: The Great Fire
diary.details: In August crusaders attack a mosque outside the walls; driven back by the locals, they set houses alight, and the wind carries the fire into the city. It burns for three days and leaves 440 acres in ashes, which are still a waste in 1220. The emperors, unable to pay what they promised, lose the people's goodwill.

diary.title: The fall of Constantinople
diary.details:
In April the second assault carries the walls: the cleric Aleaumes of Clari hurls himself through a breach, the defenders panic, and Murzuphlos slips away by night. Constantine Laskaris is acclaimed in Hagia Sophia but flees at dawn as the army deserts, and the city suffers three days of murder, rape and sacrilege. The magi of Thermakopolis, trusting their Mentem magic to keep the peace, fail, and their spells frighten their own side off the walls; four of them die, and Michael dies last, after binding his apprentice Petros, Wilrich of Flambeau and three Jerbiton survivors to defend the city for ever. Only Mathieus escapes, to Normandy. The Court of Fools, visiting the city, burns with it. Three Jerbiton of Xylinites fall fighting, the rest flee into exile and Artoud of Criamon stays on alone (the book dates this once to 1205). Moero's Garden flees with the Greek nobles to its chapter house in Nicaea, leaving most of its treasures behind. The icon of St. Loukia screams a warning for the third time this spring.

Secrets
In the Hippodrome the demon Akgah, a vast two-headed winged leopard, fights the Hagka and wins; crusaders who see it think it the lion of Venice. In these days someone also took the palladium and its relics from under the Column of Constantine, and the city's ancient Divine wards fell. The survivors who swore Michael's oath hid in the catacombs, helped by a humanoid figure of living rock.

diary.title: The Latin Empire
diary.details: By the partition agreed in March, the emperor takes a quarter of the empire and Venice and the crusader lords three-eighths each. Electors choose Baldwin of Flanders as Emperor Baldwin I over Boniface of Montferrat. Venice claims Candia, Rodos, Karpathos, the Cyclades, Durazzo and, of the northern isles, only Lemnos, Ingasia's island, which takes the Lemnian Earth and leaves the covenant poorer; some magi suspect Verditius of a deal with the doge. Boniface marches on Thessaloniki, where the Greeks welcome him, and only Doge Dandolo's diplomacy stops a war with Baldwin. Greek leaders flee to Arta and to Nicaea, where Theodore Laskaris sets up a court in exile; Alexios and David Komnenos seize Trebizond.

diary.title: The League of Advisors disbanded
diary.details: Accusations fly: House Tremere is blamed, and so is House Jerbiton. The League of Advisors, which lost many members with Thermakopolis, cannot survive the charge of meddling with mundanes and breaks up. The Tribunal fails to convict its surviving members.

diary.title: Murzuphlos seizes the throne
diary.details: In January the mob gathers at Hagia Sophia and Alexios Doukas, called Murzuphlos, takes power in a palace coup; Isaac and Alexios IV die (some say Isaac of age and shock). Crowned Alexios V, he strengthens the walls and rejects the crusaders' claims. In a skirmish at Philia he loses his crown and the Hagka banner to raiding French knights.

diary.title: Adrianople
diary.details:
The attempt to impose feudal rule on Thrace sets off a Greek revolt backed by Tsar Kaloyan of Bulgaria. On 14 April the Bulgarians ambush the Latins at Adrianople; Louis of Blois is killed by Cumans and Baldwin is captured and never seen again. Doge Enrico Dandolo dies the same year, and the captured Murzuphlos is thrown to his death from the Column of Theodosius.

Secrets
A Redcap who whispered that House Tremere knew more of Baldwin's fate died soon after in a fall from his horse, and the archai of the day let the matter drop. One tale says his skull became a drinking cup.

diary.title: Henry I crowned; Achaea and Athens founded
diary.details: When news of Baldwin's death arrives, his brother is crowned Emperor Henry I on 20 August, ruling a narrow strip round Constantinople. In the Morea William de Champlitte and Geoffrey de Villehardouin beat an army ten times their number from Epiros at the Olive Grove of Koundouros and found the Principality of Achaea; the defeated Michael Komnenos Doukas retreats to Arta and founds Epiros. (The book also dates Achaea's founding to 1204.) Otto de la Roche founds the Duchy of Athens, and the monastery of Daphni is sacked and given to the Cistercians. At Nicaea Theodore Laskaris names Michael Autoreianos Orthodox patriarch, and the Venetians begin walling their quarter of Constantinople.

diary.title: The Tribunal of 1207
diary.details: The first Tribunal since the fall meets on Delos. Michael's Tabula is formally founded by the survivors who swore Michael's oath, named for the stone tablet on which it was carved. Petronas abdicates as logothete after almost a century and Leontius of Alexandria, an unhappy choice, replaces him. Maria Laskarina of Polyaigos, filia of its founder, is elected polemarch. Krum of Bjornaer, late of Moero's Garden, hears Lucian of Aegaea's tales of Poseidon and joins Aegaea. Frankish magi found Novocastrum on the western borders of the Kingdom of Thessaloniki. (The book gives no season for the meeting.)

diary.title: St. Demetrios slays Kaloyan; Boniface killed
diary.details: Boniface of Montferrat dies in a Bulgarian ambush and his head is sent to the tsar, leaving his two-year-old son Demetrios heir to Thessaloniki under Queen Margaret, who soon marries Nicholas of St. Omer, a lord of Thebes. Kaloyan (the book also calls him Ioannitsa) besieges the city; the sisters of Oikos tou Eleous call on St. Demetrios, and early in October a shining armoured rider comes out and kills the tsar with a spear. The Bulgarians say his Cuman commander did it. Henry's battles reopen the road between the two Latin states, and his wife Agnes of Montferrat dies. Marco Sanudo attacks Naxos. Seirene twins from Lesbos join Oikos tou Eleous and secretly back Queen Margaret.

diary.title: Theodore Laskaris crowned; Leo Sgouros leaps
diary.details: Theodore I Laskaris (the book calls him Theodore II) is crowned emperor at Nicaea, vowing to retake Constantinople. Trapped in Acrocorinth, Leo Sgouros rides his horse off the battlements to his death, and Greek resistance in the Morea falters. Otto de la Roche takes the title of duke.

diary.title: Demetrios crowned; Oberto seized
diary.details: Demetrios is crowned king of Thessaloniki at four. Count Oberto of Biandrate, who has forced Margaret from the regency to put William VI of Montferrat on the throne, shuts the gates against Henry, but Henry, once admitted, takes Margaret's side and has Oberto chained in the castle of Serres. In the Morea William de Champlitte dies on his way to France, and Geoffrey de Villehardouin, regent, contrives with Venice to delay the heir and keeps the principality.

diary.title: Epiros turns on Thessaloniki
diary.details:
Michael Komnenos Doukas, allied with Venice, attacks Thessaloniki and his son-in-law the boy king; Henry intervenes to save Demetrios from Venice, the Bulgarians and Epiros. Michael's half-brother Theodore Komnenos Doukas defects from Nicaea to Epiros. Porphyrion of Tytalus leaves Hedyosmos for Rome.

Secrets
In Rome Porphyrion is rumoured to have found the Jar of Pandora before moving on to Normandy, where he may bid to become primus of Tytalus.

diary.title: Antioch-on-the-Maeander
diary.details: Theodore Laskaris marches out of Philadelphia and defeats Sultan Kaykhusraw I of Rum; the Maeander becomes Nicaea's southern border. Greek chroniclers say the sultan had struck the emperor down when a mysterious French knight appeared from nowhere and killed him, and the Tribunal whispers that the knight was a magus. The Latin patriarch Thomas Morosini dies, and the whole Morea is now in Latin hands.

diary.title: Novocastrum destroyed; Candia and Naxos
diary.details: Epiros overruns the western borders of Thessaloniki, and the Frankish magi of Novocastrum die resisting it; few mourn them. Venice ousts the Genoese pirate Enrico Pescatore and establishes the Kingdom of Candia. Marco Sanudo has taken nearly all the Cyclades and parcels them into some fifty lordships of the Duchy of Naxos. Nicaea takes back most of David Komnenos's conquests.

diary.title: Epiros turns on Venice
diary.details: Michael of Epiros starts taking the towns of the Adriatic and Ionian shores from Venice, his ally of three years before.

diary.title: Corfu and Amastris taken; peace with the Latins
diary.details: Michael of Epiros wrests Corfu from Venice. Theodore Laskaris takes Amastris on the Black Sea, still his eastern border; the Sultanate of Rum drives north between Nicaea and Trebizond and kills David Komnenos. Nicaea makes peace with the Latin Empire, which holds for six years.

diary.title: The Tribunal of 1214
diary.details: The Tribunal meets on Delos. Aiakia of Hedyosmos is elected archon and Maria Laskarina re-elected polemarch. Leontius, the logothete, narrowly escapes ostracism over his faulty register of tokens and shards. (The book gives no season for the meeting.)

diary.title: Michael of Epiros murdered
diary.details: Michael Komnenos Doukas is stabbed by a servant driven past bearing by his cruelty, and his half-brother Theodore succeeds him, taking Ohrid and Pelagonia from the Bulgarians. Gervase becomes Latin patriarch of Constantinople after four years' vacancy.

diary.title: Death of Emperor Henry
diary.details:
Henry marries Maria of Bulgaria, Kaloyan's daughter, and dies suddenly the same year, poisoned, people say, by her or by Count Oberto; Maria vanishes. The barons elect Peter of Courtenay, Henry's brother-in-law, who accepts William of Montferrat's claim to Thessaloniki, and Margaret flees into exile, leaving her son in the city. Ravano dalle Carceri, lord of Negroponte, dies, and Venetian bailiffs split his three baronies into six. A peace treaty settles the Troad.

Secrets
Hermetic gossip ties the vanished Maria of Bulgaria to the Daughters of Erichtho.

diary.title: Peter of Courtenay captured; Yolanda regent
diary.details: Peter is crowned by the pope and lands at Durazzo with 5,500 men, but Theodore of Epiros seizes him on the Via Egnatia; he dies a prisoner, almost certainly murdered, though no grave is known. His wife Yolanda of Flanders reaches Constantinople by sea and rules as regent, making peace with Bulgaria and Nicaea.

diary.title: Geoffrey II of Achaea; Ivan Asen II
diary.details: Geoffrey de Villehardouin dies and his son Geoffrey II, husband of Yolanda's daughter Agnes, succeeds him; generous to Greeks and Latins, he taxes Latin church lands and spares the Orthodox clergy. In Bulgaria Ivan Asen II takes the throne from Tsar Boril (the book still names Boril as tsar).

diary.title: Death of Yolanda
diary.details: Yolanda marries her daughter Marie of Courtenay to Theodore Laskaris and dies suddenly. Her elder son Philip of Namur refuses the throne; his brother Robert of Courtenay accepts it but has not yet arrived, and the Latin Empire is leaderless. The Latin patriarch Gervase dies too, and the Serbian Church becomes autocephalous. In August Venice and Nicaea agree a trade treaty, ending the Nicene navy's war on Venetian shipping.

diary.title: Nicaea at war again
diary.details: The peace with the Latins breaks and Theodore Laskaris masses his army to take Holkos on the Hellespont while the Latin knights are away fighting the Bulgarians. He also gathers churchmen at Nicaea to seek an end to the schism with Rome. Several magi of the Court of Fools, lost in 1204, reappear.
