tribunals.secrets:
Proximios, the likely next logothete, secretly serves the Infernal and founded the League of the Vigilant to turn the polity's own suspicions against the innocent; see An Enemy Within.

Gemma and Bobila of Ingasia are selling more enchanted items to mundanes than the Peripheral Code allows, mostly to Nicaea.

The Tribunal next meets on Delos in 1221. Leontius means to resign as logothete there, and the Redcaps plan to propose Proximios; Pancratius, Syagricus's apprentice, hopes for his Gauntlet; and the League Against Idolatry presses to end the Ceremony of Propitiation. House Tremere has asked the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to try the two surviving members of the League of Advisors again, and the Verditius Contest of 1234 will test whether Ingasia is now the House's domus magna. If the saga follows history, Robert of Courtenay reaches Constantinople in 1221, Theodore Laskaris takes Holkos, and the Latins, beset from the north, sue for peace that year.

Proximios of Alexandria, founder of the League of the Vigilant, is an Infernalist who means to bring the Order down, starting in Thebes.

Behind the seeds: one of the children at the interviews is a faerie changeling who means to lead the others away to safety. The flies are a nasu bound in a relic of the Persian Wars, and the rival who found it commands them. The despot's adviser is close to the Infernal, writes the island's only books, among them a corrupt Bible, and hoards its vis while his demon watches. The senior magus asking after the mysterious knight may be the knight himself, testing how easily he could be found out.

neighbours.name: Didyma
neighbours.summary:
A cluster of crumbling temples ten miles south of Miletos and a mile from the Anatolian coast, in a craggy hollow split from the limestone of a flat, dry plain barely 100 paces above the sea. The hollow, some five paces deep, is ringed by a retaining wall, and the marble columns rise out of it to throw long black shadows across the plain.

Most of the temples date from Trajan's rebuilding in 100, though they have fallen and risen many times. The covenfolk, most of them of the Branchidae family, make up a sizeable village here.
neighbours.secrets: The cult is not as old as it claims. It has been remade after each conquest and persecution, last after the Christians left in the eighth century, so its rites are a second-hand memory of ancient stories shaped by the faerie Apollo Didyma, himself a mirror of human tales; its priestly dress is closer to Rome than to old Greece. Only one who knows faeries and stories deeply, or the far past by supernatural means, could see it.

neighbours.name: The Temple of Apollo
neighbours.summary: The enormous temple, on a base 50 paces by 100, a stone forest of over 100 columns each 20 paces tall, seen for miles across the plain and mostly open to the sky. Its enclosed centre holds Alexander's and Nikola's laboratories with the library and scriptorium between them, among them the record of many thousands of prophecies, most of them long past or trivial. Its statues and frescoes show gods and, oddly for a Greek temple, many wild beasts, mythic and mundane, perhaps for those that follow the Sacred Way.

neighbours.name: The Temple of Athena
neighbours.summary: Well kept and shrouded in thick black drapes that crack in the wind and hide all within, which usually overcomes Ariane's Restriction. Like the smaller temples it stands on a stepped platform two paces high of some 3,500 square feet, with 10-pace columns about a roofed hall flanked by two large cellae. It holds Ariane's laboratory and the coffers.

neighbours.name: The Temple of Zeus
neighbours.summary: Sound in structure though much chipped, with fantastic bones littering the ground outside and exotic pelts curing between the columns. It holds Herakles's and William's laboratories, and the Frankish mercenaries camp in its central hall.

neighbours.name: The Temples of Dionysus and Hermes
neighbours.summary: Damaged, with fallen columns and headless or missing statues, and sometimes used as stores. The Temple of Dionysus held the laboratories of Lydia and Cora, which are offered to visitors who need one.

neighbours.name: The Baths
neighbours.summary: Roman work: a domed central hall, the covenfolk's meeting, storage and work place, with two wings. The eastern baths are filled in and house covenfolk; the western are in use, tiled in fine mosaics of gods and myths, fed from the Sacred Spring, and heated by the Bath Rock instead of the old boilers. Bathing there gives the covenfolk a +1 Living Modifier to aging rolls.

neighbours.name: The Round Altars
neighbours.summary: Two round altars carved with gods and titans before the Temple of Apollo, their purpose forgotten. Magi duel at certamen on the rim of the large one, 7 paces across and a pace high. The small one, 3 paces across, has no use.

neighbours.name: Hera's Temple and the Church
neighbours.summary: Two collapsed buildings: Hera's temple, fallen early in the seventh century, and Theodosius's fifth-century church, heart of a small colony of monks, brought down by an earthquake in the late 800s. The monks moved to Miletos. The old monk Basil and a few young monks live in a corner still standing.

neighbours.name: The Covenant Wall
neighbours.summary: A stone retaining wall about five paces tall around the hollow, the Boundary of the Aegis of the Hearth; cavalry cannot pass it. Climbing it is a Dexterity + Athletics roll against 9, with armour's encumbrance, and a fall does +10. On the east, five steps a pace tall, two deep and 50 wide lead up to the plain: easy on foot, Dexterity + Ride against 6 for a rider. Zeus' Arm lifts bulky goods in and out.

neighbours.name: The Sacred Spring
neighbours.summary:
In the open heart of the Temple of Apollo, behind a crumbling wall, it feeds a square pool of 500 square feet, a pace deep, and the baths. It is a vis source and the water of prophecy.

A prophecy. The Branchidae chooses a subject, an individual, place, bloodline (DE p. 93) or nation, with an Arcane Connection to the individual or to a member of the bloodline, and moves a pawn of vis of any Art into a draught of the water, a day in a laboratory or sooner by ReVi. An oracle, who needs the Visions Flaw but not the Gift, drinks, trances about an hour and tells the vision. Interpreting it takes about a day and gives the prophecy text, usually a cryptic phrase, copied like a level 5 Lab Text, with an expiry, most often a year or a decade.

Anyone who reads or hears the text gains one Prophecy Point, a one-off +3 like a Confidence Point on a roll about the subject, or +6 if it concerns faeries, before the expiry. A second reading gives no second point, but each different prophecy of a subject gives one. At once a grog may have one valid prophecy, a companion or magus three, Mythic Blood six, and a place, bloodline or nation usually one; beyond that the visions repeat. A false prophecy gives no point, and the Branchidae rarely lie about them, faithful transmission being their religion.
neighbours.secrets: The Branchidae put the +6 down to Apollo Didyma being a great faerie. The truth is that prophecies are stories, and faeries work to fulfil them.

neighbours.name: The Didyma Plain
neighbours.summary: Six small fishing villages on the coast and dozens of farming hamlets on the plain, each under 100 people, living by grain, vegetables and goats, with fish on the shore. Nearly all are Christians who hear Sunday mass in Miletos or Panormos, and many walk to Didyma once or twice a year for a traditional prophecy. They think well of the covenant, and think the magi and oracles very odd.

neighbours.name: The Sacred Way
neighbours.summary:
A road of stone blocks a pace square, five to seven paces wide, running ten miles from Miletos to the hollow of Didyma, turning aside for Panormos, about five hours' walk. The old shrines, sphinxes, statues of patriarchs and tombs of citizens are mostly gone, and Christian shrines stand each half mile, each with a Divine aura of 2.

It is also a great way from the faerie realm into the mundane world, and nearly any faerie may step onto it, sphinxes most of all. Herakles came by it as a child, and several Merinita have sought the way back along it, perhaps Orion among them, who vanished in 1053.

neighbours.name: Miletos
neighbours.summary:
An ancient port on a rocky peninsula, sometimes called Palatia for the old stone temples and halls that fill it, the home of Thales and the first town of Mythic Europe laid out on a grid. Walled, with the Sacred and Lion gates towards the land, it has two harbours, the Lion Harbour behind a gated sea-wall and the Theatre Harbour, and fresh water still comes down a Roman aqueduct. Several thousand people live there, far fewer than of old, so stone and empty ground lie south of the walls.

Greek refugees from Constantinople brought a boom. Greek, Venetian, Arab and Jewish quarters all use the port as a hub for goods from Constantinople, North Africa, the East and Europe, and under the profit runs a hatred of the Venetians that sometimes breaks out in the streets. All value the covenant's warded warehouses, and old half-pagan customs survive among the citizens, among them walking the Sacred Way for a prophecy before a wedding, a birth or a bargain.

neighbours.name: Panormos
neighbours.summary:
A port of just under a thousand people on the turquoise sea, a mile north-west of Didyma, whose temples stand in plain view. Many townsfolk are unGifted Branchidae; the covenant's Christians come here to mass, and townsfolk walk the other way for prophecies. The weathered skulls of a dozen sea-monsters hang from the arch on the main road east, which joins the Sacred Way just outside town.

Arab traders here are said to buy and sell on what pirates plunder from the Miletos shipping lanes.

neighbours.name: The Delphinion
neighbours.summary: A plain, well-kept, defunct stone temple behind the warehouses, where the Sacred Way begins: a lacuna of the Faerie in the city, and home to Callista's household. Chloris likes to raise her litters here.

neighbours.name: The Lion Harbour Warehouses
neighbours.summary: Three adjoining warehouses of solid, airy stone under wooden roofs, 5,000 square feet each, and a dock for large ships, not under any Aegis. Each is warded against vermin, rot and pestilence. Usually eight of the turb stand guard, with five Defender Swords, and a dozen porters and teamsters hired by Callista, who have seldom seen a magus. One is leased at present to a Venetian cartel. Here too are the Oracle's Dredge, two small old cedarwood boats and six Porter's Helpers.

neighbours.name: The Arab Market of Miletos
neighbours.summary: The busy, scented spice market, where some goods hold vis.

neighbours.name: The Strategos' Fortress
neighbours.summary: Ten towers about a great courtyard on a hill in the middle of Miletos, over the Theatre Harbour, on the site of the Roman theatre turned to military use more than 500 years ago. Few remember the theatre, Apollo Didyma among them.

neighbours.name: Aftonsitiron
neighbours.summary: A small village a mile north of Miletos, of rich soil and heavy barley crops, some of it holding vis.

neighbours.name: Anakletos, Strategos of Miletos
neighbours.summary:
The Nicaean governor of a large hinterland that takes in the covenant, a clever man of middle age, once a young officer of a rich Constantinople family, raised fast when the army fell apart. On paper he has ten taxiarchiai of 1,000 and two moria of 3,000; in truth about 100 foot and 100 horse, with about 100 Latin mercenaries at the gates and as marines against pirates. With levies he might raise 3,000 in a season, leaving the country bare.

Fearing invasion, and with quarrels between Latins and Greeks on his hands, he leaves the oracles alone. He knew Ariane in Constantinople, and knows the magi for members of a league of half-pagan sorcerers.
neighbours.secrets: He has had a fearsome prophecy of a Muslim invasion.

neighbours.name: The Metropolis of Miletos
neighbours.summary: An old Greek see: its bishop Kaisarios Eusebio sat at Nicaea in 325, Hyakinthos was raised to archbishop in 538, and Michael won metropolitan rank in the early eleventh century. A few Latin clergy serve the Venetian quarter. Niketas II has held it since 1172, from the episcopal palace, and before him Nikephoros (965-969), Epiphanios (969-1013), Michael (1013-1170), Niketas (1170) and Nikephoros II (1170), with the see empty in 1171 for want of a quorum.

neighbours.name: The Kommerkiarioi of Miletos
neighbours.summary: The tax officials who assess and tax goods at the port at a tenth, half to Nicaea and half to the local forces and expenses, and seal them so they are not taxed twice in imperial cities. A split lot needs an official present; forging a seal is death, or sometimes a heavy fine. Their head, Leander, tall, bald and piercing-eyed, is known to be corrupt, and many merchants pay him, though nothing is proven at Nicaea. Cleon has the covenant and its warehouses.
neighbours.secrets: Torvus is blackmailing Leander with stolen papers.

description.biography:
A huge, bearded, obese old man in a white hooded toga, who seldom leaves the Temple of Apollo. Twilight scars: those within earshot feel a deep throbbing hum, and a faint coloured nimbus some two paces across shows his mood. Casting sigil: the sphere, in every effect's shape or trappings. Voting sigil: a foot-wide bronze disk stamped with the Eye of the Branchidae. Patriarch and Librarian of the covenant. Longevity Ritual -8, Bronze Cord -2. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init +1, Attack +2, Defense +4, Damage -2. Soak +3 (Stamina and Bronze Cord).

General spells at the levels printed: Sight of the True Form 20, Wizard's Communion 10, Wizard's Vigil 40 (as a Communion of 30), Demon's Eternal Oblivion 10, Circular Ward Against Demons 25, Aegis of the Hearth 25. End of the Titans and Faerie Bane are the Magic and Faerie equivalents of Demon's Eternal Oblivion. Printed casting totals include +3 for Method Caster, without talisman attunements.

characters.summary: Fourth Patriarch of Didyma and head of the Branchidae family, at its head since Jason was given up for lost in 1132. His schemes have made the covenant secure with its neighbours. He rarely leaves the temples, and his laboratory stands within Apollo's.
characters.secrets: His Death Prophecy: to be slain by his apprentice. He has two left living, Nikola and Aoede. Though the title was barely his, he kept the older Tessa and Damen from Didyma, by the wards cast with Lana. He magically fixed Niketas's election in 1172 and made him a Longevity Ritual.

description.biography:
Tall and white-haired with a long face, in a brown hooded stola. Twilight scars: eyes fixed and blank as those painted on a sarcophagus, though she sees well, and brown blood mildly acid as lemon juice, which hurts nobody. Casting sigil: a faint echo exactly one diameter behind her casting, of her voice or of the effect, with fainter echoes open to InVi study of sigils. Voting sigil: the Strategos' sword. Longevity Ritual -5. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init +1, Attack +2, Defense +4, Damage +1; Strategos' sword Init +3, Attack +10, Defense +9, Damage +7. Soak +1.

General spells at the levels printed: The Invisible Eye Revealed 20, Wizard's Communion 20, Wizard's Vigil 40, Maintaining the Demanding Spell 15. She knows Aegis of the Hearth at levels 25 and 40: she casts the covenant's at 40, usually with the others helping by Wizard's Communion for Penetration, and at 25 when they cannot. The Spell Persists keeps up a spell of level 30 or less for Sun.

Covenant Strategos; an arche of the Kretan phyle on the Council of Magistrates, sitting on the Treasury Council as a tutor who finds Gifted children. Her Study Requirement needs large specimen collections, at present animal bones, and at least a season to exchange them. She lives in her laboratory with her husband and servant Alexios.

characters.summary: Strategos of the covenant, Alexander's filia and his heir as Matriarch, a stateswoman who writes to Tribunal officers and Redcaps without end and loves to talk Tribunal business. Her daughters Lydia and Cora drowned in 1205, and she blames Herakles; she married Alexios soon after.
characters.secrets: Her Death Prophecy: to die on a full moon. Alexios has come to think she married him only to escape her grief, though he denies with a brittle smile that it is anything but a love match. She has waited all her life for Alexander to die and knows nothing of the wards unless he tells her.

description.biography:
A giant strong-man in a lion-skin cloak, with a round shield and his club, who gives out that he is Zeus's son and his namesake come again. Twilight scar: a booming voice, Loud reaching 60 paces and Firm 30; he cannot speak Quiet, though No Voice works as usual. Casting sigil: heat, the air warming a degree or more by the effect's strength. Voting sigil: an old Greek silver coin, the Sacred Spring on one side and Zeus's head on the other. Longevity Ritual -4. Encumbrance 0 (1).

Combat: fist Init +1, Attack +9, Defense +8, Damage +5; club and shield Init +2, Attack +12, Defense +12, Damage +8. Soak +7.

General spells at the levels printed: Wizard's Communion 20, Wizard's Vigil 20, Demon's Eternal Oblivion 5, Disenchant 15, Gather the Essence of the Beast 15. Deficient Technique halves his Muto casting totals after the die and the aura.

Herakles's club, by his account carved by Zeus from an ancient oak, is no magic item but an Excellent one (City & Guild p. 69): Single Weapon, Init +1, Attack +4, Defense +3, Damage +3, Strength 0, Load 1. He sometimes goes about disguised, by Disguise of the New Visage and Preternatural Growth and Shrinking, most often as an ancient crone; his Gift is as plain as ever, but no one knows him. He holds Lana's effects, and William of Normandy is his guest.

characters.summary: A giant-blooded magus who appeared as a small boy on the Sacred Way in 1165 claiming Zeus as his father, and was apprenticed to Nicodemus. Miletos takes him for the demigod, and he believes it, and flings himself at any peril to prove it. In 1205 he brought a dozen sea-monsters' heads to Panormos.

characters.name: Ariane

params.detail: cannot cast when seen by unGifted humans

invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Through the Aegis.

description.biography:
Slender and attractive, in a thin white hooded stola, the covenant's Chancellor. Twilight scar: she seems able to live on air, with +3 to Deprivation rolls for food and -3 for air. Casting sigil: a yellow-green fog that puffs from her or her target. Voting sigil: a coin-sized gold locket holding a copy of the icon of St. Loukia, patron of Xylinites. Longevity Ritual -4, Bronze Cord -2. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init 0, Attack 0, Defense 0, Damage -1. Soak +4 (Stamina and Bronze Cord).

General spells at the levels printed: Wizard's Communion 20, Wizard's Vigil 20, Maintaining the Demanding Spell 15, Opening the Intangible Tunnel 15, Aegis of the Hearth 25. Her Palm spells, Sense of the Lodestone and Chill Touch of Exposure are learned to cast down an Intangible Tunnel. The Focus is in the printed totals of Step Sideways, The Leap of Homecoming and Seven League Travel Circle.

A wealthy Constantinople merchant's daughter, schooled among the eunuchs of Xylinites, then still Jerbiton. The fall killed her father and her parens Theoderic, and she fled to Miletos with one of her father's trading partners. Former classmates, now powerful in the exiled court at Nicaea, still write to her. Her Restriction fails if the unGifted close their eyes or look away, but a hidden watcher stops her; beasts and beings of other realms do not count. She is married to the turb leader Sebasten, who lives apart and often visits her bed. She wishes William would go home.

characters.summary: Chancellor of the covenant, a refugee from Constantinople's fall who came in 1205 and has since turned pagan. She keeps to a draped temple with her blind maidens, watches the covenant's interests through Intangible Tunnels and her cat, and is kind to those who trouble to know her, but fearful of Latin magi.
characters.secrets: She suspects William took part in the sack of Constantinople, and fears him for it. She leans towards the Children of Olympos.

description.biography:
A Latin knight of Ramius's school, of the Normandy Tribunal, with wild red hair. Twilight scars: one blue eye, one brown, and hair crackling with static, flashes of it showing in the dark. Casting sigil: a showy, harmless discharge of electricity. Voting sigil: a falcon's feather of silver. Longevity Ritual -2, Bronze Cord -2. Encumbrance 3 (4).

Combat: fist Init +2, Attack +4, Defense +5, Damage +1; long sword and shield Init +4, Attack +11, Defense +11, Damage +7; lance and shield, mounted, Init +4, Attack +13, Defense +12, Damage +6, with the +3 mounted bonus; pole-axe Init +3, Attack +11, Defense +7, Damage +12; short bow Init +1, Attack +8, Defense +6, Damage +7. Soak +13 (Stamina, armour and Bronze Cord).

He has long sword, round shield, pole-axe, lance, short bow and arrows, breastplate and mail with a helm, and carries only what he is using; the rest rides on his warhorse Lambert.

General spells at the levels printed: Wizard's Vigil 20, Demon's Eternal Oblivion 5, Gather the Essence of the Beast 15. The three Personal Wards are Touch, Sun.

He came east behind the crusaders of 1204, and since that siege has sworn never again to kill a human. A metoikos of the Tribunal, guest of Herakles since 1210, he may vote but hold no Tribunal office, though the covenant's charter counts him a full resident. He leads four Frankish mercenaries, with whom he and Herakles hunt faeries on the Sacred Way and Typhon's brood in the mountains. Unmarried; his soldiers quietly joke about how close he and Herakles are. Most of his private Lab Texts are back in Normandy.

characters.summary: A Norman knight-magus of the Gentle Gift, liked by mundanes in spite of his strange looks, who means to be the greatest slayer of monsters there has been. He hunts with Herakles.
characters.secrets: He claims he took no direct part in the siege of Constantinople.

characters.name: Philip

description.biography:
Tall, lanky and imposing, with tight black curls and a full beard flecked with early grey, and surprisingly stealthy for his size. In mail and helm with longsword, round shield, short bow and quiver. Encumbrance 2 (4). Printed Leadership 4+2 and Stealth 4+1.

Combat: fist Init +2, Attack +5, Defense +5, Damage +1; longsword and shield Init +4, Attack +14, Defense +13, Damage +7; short bow Init +1, Attack +11, Defense +8, Damage +7. Soak +11.

One of the two turb captains and an arche. His grandfather Zotikos was a faerie goblin in Nicodemus's service, and he is an unGifted Branchidae. He is grave and bound up in the turb, and the covenant's women keep trying to draw him off; his reserve only spurs them on.

characters.summary: A turb captain and arche, well liked.

characters.name: Callista

description.biography:
A tall woman whose long curled black hair is slowly going grey, with her agenda and warehouse log books. Her Ability Block comes of Warping. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init 0, Attack 0, Defense +1, Damage 0. Soak 0.

An arche, she lives in the Delphinion with her husband Cleon, two teenage children and six servants, and deals for the magi with the city's officials and merchants. Her open paganism worries parts of the city but raises her standing as the prophets' voice. She carries the Warning Flame and uses the Spice Wand.

characters.summary: The covenant's representative in Miletos, and an arche.

characters.name: Ella the Oracle

description.biography:
A pampered woman in middle age in a priestess's hooded stola, her scalp shaved to show off a shapely head. Her fear of snakes comes of Warping. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init +1, Defense +6. Soak +3.

Honoured by the covenfolk and given no other work, she bristles at any whisper of free-loading and talks up her duties, and she watches Julia warily. Her Malediction: oracle work has addicted her to vis, and she suffers Deprivation (check each month) unless she takes it; the Fatigue is Long-Term, and only a pawn of vis restores it.

characters.summary: The oracle of Didyma, who drinks the draught and speaks the vision.

characters.name: Niketas II of Miletos

description.biography:
An old cripple lost in coarse clerical robes, with crosier and pallium. He can crawl but not walk, so he sits on his throne in the episcopal palace or is carried by two strong young monks. Faith Points 3, +1 from his relic. Longevity Ritual -4. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: dodge Init -2, Defense -2. Soak +1 (Stamina and Commanding Aura).

Commanding Aura: like Aura of Rightful Authority at Voice Range, free and with no Penetration, plus Magic Resistance 10 and +2 Soak. Saint Nikephoros' Journey: 3 Faith Points, Init +2, Corpus, like The Leap of Homecoming, a power of the relic, a fragment of bone set in his archbishop's ring, of Faith Score 1, which brings his Magic Resistance to 20.

Once a monk, pious and ambitious, Metropolitan of Miletos since 1172. He respects the magi's skill with the supernatural, and he and Alexander are old friends who write often.

reputations.name: Elderly politician and metropolitan of Miletos (local and ecclesiastical)

characters.summary: Metropolitan of Miletos and the covenant's ally, a tie few know of, even at the covenant.
characters.secrets: He owes Alexander his election and his long life, and in return discourages hard questions about the paganism at Didyma. He convalesced a season in the baths after an illness in 1194.

characters.name: Magarethe

description.biography:
Old, bent by her years yet agile, in a plain robe. Incomprehensible and Offensive to Animals come of Warping, the fruit of a lifetime among magi. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init -1, Attack +1, Defense -1, Damage -2. Soak -1.

Her eyes were burnt out at Constantinople thirty-five years ago so she might serve Ariane, whom she followed here. Respected by the covenfolk, she is archon: the longest serving arche and their voice and vote on the Council of Magi.

characters.summary: Ariane's oldest servant, archon of the Council of Archai.

characters.name: Marcel the Mercenary

description.biography:
A hardy Frankish warrior in full chain mail and helm, with long sword, round shield, lance, short bow and warhorse. Motion Sickness and Reckless come of Warping. Encumbrance 2 (3).

Combat: fist Init +2, Attack +8, Defense +8, Damage +1; long sword and shield Init +4, Attack +13, Defense +12, Damage +7; lance and shield, mounted, Init +4, Attack +15, Defense +13, Damage +6, with the +3 mounted bonus; short bow Init +1, Attack +9, Defense +6, Damage +7. Soak +11.

Years in Hermetic service against demons, giants and serpents have left little to surprise him, and he is very touchy about any hint of cowardice. Thomas, Alain and Guy are much like him. He lives at the covenant with his wife Lyra, a goat farmer's lovely young daughter from an hour's walk away, though they share little speech.

characters.summary: The Frankish mercenary who stands for his band of four.

characters.name: Aoede

description.biography:
A nervous, shy nine-year-old, often hiding behind Alexander's bulk, with the -3 age penalty already in her Characteristics. Casting sigil: an A minor chord rising from the target, as loud as the spell is strong, a whisper for the first magnitude. In a simple tunic. No Twilight Scars. Encumbrance 0.

Combat: fist Init +1, Attack +2, Defense +4, Damage -2. Soak -3.

Her parents, Lysias of the turb and the servant Rhea, are both of the extended Branchidae family. Close to Alexander, under his shared Parma Magica, she is not usually frightened by the Gifted. Ariane fascinates her, and she loves riding on Herakles's back, though she has lately begun to pretend she is too old for it. When not studying she may invent spells in Alexander's laboratory.

characters.summary: Alexander's apprentice and great-granddaughter, born in 1211, the darling of the Branchidae, though the unGifted resent that a little. She should take her Gauntlet at Didyma in 1231.
characters.secrets: Her Death Prophecy: to die in the dark.

characters.name: Basil the Monk

description.biography: A teacher, worth 12 Build Points. Learned and elderly, the oldest of the covenant who is no magus, an arche and a scribe.

characters.summary: A monk of Miletos, secretly a pagan for many years, who lives in the monastic ruins by a dispensation Niketas arranged and still writes to his brethren.

characters.name: Abbas

description.biography: A teacher, worth 8 Build Points: a strongman and master mason who runs the repairs, with three young apprentices (Craft: Stonemason 4, temples; 12 Build Points together), each indentured for ten years and free then to stay or find work in Miletos.

characters.summary: The covenant's master stonemason.

characters.name: Cleon

description.biography: A specialist, worth 6 Build Points: a kommerkiarios of Miletos, honest and careful with the seals, if incurious about goods that already bear a colleague's. He goes out once a year to assess the covenant's tax, a tenth of the oracle fees.

characters.summary: Callista's husband, the tax official who smooths the covenant's way with the city.

characters.name: Sebasten
characters.summary: Turb captain, arche and Ariane's husband, who visits her often but lives apart. The Grizzled Veteran (ArM5 p. 21) serves for him.

characters.name: Alexios
characters.summary: Nikola's husband and servant, 43, who lives in her laboratory and is neither Lydia's nor Cora's father.

characters.summary: Marcel's young wife, a goat farmer's daughter.

characters.name: Lysias
characters.summary: Of the turb, and Aoede's father.

characters.name: Rhea
characters.summary: A covenant servant, and Aoede's mother.

characters.name: Nestor of Polyaigos
characters.summary: Of the Branchidae line of Damen, whose filius he is, older than Nikola by several years.

characters.name: Io
characters.summary: Nestor's daughter, of the Branchidae line of Damen. He and she carry Arcane Connections to each other.

characters.name: Kaia
characters.summary: A Flambeau ally of Nestor's.

characters.name: Aristocles the Wanderer
characters.summary: Filius of Tessa, trained at Alexandria, senior to Nikola but younger than Nestor. His name and fate are unknown at Didyma: he wandered far and now lives at the oppidum of Tablinum in the Transylvanian Tribunal.
characters.secrets: He has renounced the Branchidae cult and means to end Apollo Didyma's worship by slaying him, with House Tremere's research behind him, whether or not it means the deed to be done.

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Apollo, watched over by Apollo Didyma, with a gallery from which Aoede can watch without disturbing the work. 70 Build Points. Virtues: Greater Guardian (Apollo Didyma, +3 Intellego), Gallery (+1 Teaching), Lesser Expansion (+1 Intellego).

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Apollo, large and luxurious, where she lives among her work with Alexios and her specimen collections, under a great statue of Branchos that rather dominates it. 80 Build Points. Virtues: Greater Feature (Branchos statue, +3 Intellego), Palatial (+1 Intellego, +2 Teaching), Living Quarters, Specimens (+1 Animal). Flaws: Greater Focus (Branchos statue, +4 Intellego).

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Athena, dark behind black drapes and lit by smoky candles, with the vis still she brought from Constantinople and much plain, good equipment. 40 Build Points. Virtues: Greater Feature (vis still, +3 vis extraction), Superior Equipment (+1 vis extraction). Flaws: Defective Lighting, Undecorated (-1 vis extraction).

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Zeus, watched over by his father, and kept going by offerings of mutton fat at solstices and equinoxes. Cramped for him; to anyone else it is an Awkward Shape, +1 General Quality and Upkeep without the Spells specialization. 30 Build Points. Virtues: Greater Guardian (Zeus, +3 Rego), Cramped (+1 Spells), Sacrifices (+2 Rego).

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Zeus, fitted out by Orion in 1020 with the large forge Hector and Achillios fought over; William wonders if it is more nuisance than use. 40 Build Points. Virtues: Greater Feature (forge, +3 Items), Specimens (magic creature skeletons, +1 Vim), Guard (mercenaries). Flaws: Greater Focus (forge, +4 Items).

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: In the Temple of Dionysus, a Basic laboratory stripped of most equipment, offered to visitors. 50 Build Points.

creatures.name: Mileta

powers.name: Aura of Rightful Authority
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 151). Greater Power, -2 Might Cost, +4 Init.

powers.name: Awaken the Slumbering Corpse
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 134). Greater Power, -3 Might Cost, +2 Init.

powers.name: Human Shape
powers.description: Takes the shape of a tall, skeletal, hairless woman, fangs and all, of Corpus and Animal Form at once. Personal Power, -1 Might Cost (RoP: Magic p. 39).

powers.name: Shadow Form
powers.description: In a shadow big enough to hide her she becomes one, +4 Stealth and proof against physical harm. Greater Power, -3 Might Cost, +1 Init.

powers.name: Viper's Gaze
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 120), against humans too (Animal and Corpus). Lesser Power, -2 Might Cost.

powers.name: Location (both ways)
powers.description: Invested in the familiar bond (ArM5 p. 105).

creatures.appearance: An enormous iridescent snake, 20 feet long and 6 inches through, or a thin bald woman in a black hooded toga.
creatures.notes:
Alexander's familiar, who hides deep in the Sacred Spring or works in his laboratory passing as an unGifted Branchidae; few covenfolk see through that, and fewer know the assistant is the spring snake. Her fang wound can carry venom, Ease Factor 9, Incapacitating Wound (ArM5 p. 180). Printed Infernal Lore 4+2.

Bond: Golden +1, Silver +2, Bronze +2, by InMe Lab Total 35.
creatures.secrets: Her Dark Secret: she was a demon, long before she met Alexander, changed into a creature of Magic she knows not how, perhaps by miracle or lost magic; she feels no loyalty to Hell, and she may only be deluded. No Hermetic magic can prove she is no demon, only that a Demon's Eternal Oblivion did not affect her.

creatures.name: Chloris the Curious

powers.name: Cat's Leap
powers.description: An Animal version of Gift of the Frog's Legs (ArM5 p. 134). Personal Power, -2 Might Cost.

powers.name: Eyes for Power
powers.description: She sees vis. Personal Power twice, -2 Might Cost, +4 Init.

powers.name: Leap of Homecoming
powers.description: An Animal version of the spell (ArM5 p. 135). Personal Power twice, -3 Might Cost.

powers.name: Mental Communication (both ways)
powers.description: Invested in the familiar bond (ArM5 p. 105).

powers.name: Prying Eyes
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 144). Lesser Power, -1 Might Cost, +3 Init.

powers.name: Whispers Through the Black Gate
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 130), -2 Might Cost.

creatures.equipment: A leather collar stamped with Ariane's sigil and studded with tiny stones, each a fixed Arcane Connection: three points on the Sacred Way (the covenant end, the Panormos turning, two miles south of Miletos), the Delphinion, the Lion Gate, and an alley by Xylinites. There is room for six more.
creatures.appearance: A small, harmless-looking tortoiseshell cat.
creatures.notes:
Ariane's familiar, a patient, wayward watcher from dark corners who tells her mistress of visitors when she pleases and may go off for seasons. The Curse of Venus keeps her chased by tomcats, pregnant or nursing; many of Miletos's cats are hers, some perhaps magical, and she likes the Delphinion for her litters.

Bond: Golden +1, Silver +1, Bronze +2, by InAn Lab Total 26.

creatures.name: Torvus

params.power: Sight of the True Form, twice

powers.name: Location (both ways)
powers.description: Invested in the familiar bond (ArM5 p. 105).

powers.name: Mental Communication (both ways)
powers.description: Invested in the familiar bond (ArM5 p. 105).

powers.name: Sailor's Foretaste of the Morrow
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 127). Lesser Power, -1 Might Cost.

powers.name: Shriek of the Impending Shafts
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 136). Personal Power, -2 Might Cost.

powers.name: Sight of the True Form
powers.description: The spell at level 15, but constant (ArM5 p. 130). Personal Power twice, -3 Might Cost, +1 Init.

powers.name: The Cloudless Sky Returned
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 128). Greater Power, -1 Might Cost.

creatures.appearance: A brown falcon with a three-foot wingspan.
creatures.notes:
William's familiar and his eye for miles around, a thief who hoards curious things on and under the temple roofs. A fast flyer, +3 on rolls of speed.

Bond: Golden +1, Silver 0, Bronze +2, by InAu Lab Total 20.
creatures.secrets: Papers in his hoard show the corruption of Miletos's tax officials, and without William's knowledge he is blackmailing their head, Leander.

creatures.name: Apollo Didyma
creatures.appearance: He showed himself here in ancient times, but not for centuries, and seems to dwell at several places in the Faerie realm, Olympos among them.
creatures.notes:
The aspect of Apollo at Didyma: the covenant's patron and the source of its prophecies, a powerful faerie, which is a rare thing in a covenant's patron. The book gives him no Might or statistics.

He seeks the worship of the pagan gods and the undoing of the titans' servants. He warns the Branchidae by prophecy, now and then sends an intermediary down the Sacred Way, may grant Branchidae Prophecy to others, and calls the Order little but 'the priests of Hermes'.

Branchos, the founder (died about 900 BC), built him the first shrine, and his daughter was the first oracle; some say he lived for centuries and joined Apollo's retinue on Olympos.

creatures.name: Sphinx
creatures.how_many: commonly seen on the Sacred Way

powers.name: Faerie Sight
powers.description: Tells glamour from the mundane, knows another faerie's glamour and sees Arcane Connections, and whose they are if that person is present. Perception + Awareness against the other's Might / 5 reads a faerie's motives (RoP: Faerie p. 50).

powers.name: Faerie Speech
powers.description: Speaks the language of her human audience (RoP: Faerie p. 50).

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Constant. She flies, carrying a rider or a victim up to Size +1. Personal Power, two intricacy points to Might Cost.

powers.name: Hound
powers.description: She knows the direction and distance of her quarry. Lesser Power, one intricacy point.

powers.name: Shriek of the Impending Shafts
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 136). Personal Power, two intricacy points.

creatures.appearance: A lion's body with a woman's torso and head growing from it, like a feline centaur, and the wings of an eagle.
creatures.notes: She hunts lone travellers, avoiding groups: she swoops, grapples, climbs 20 feet each round and drops them, +1 damage for each two feet fallen (ArM5 p. 181). Her Sovereign Ward: she cannot harm one who solves her riddle, and must offer one if asked. Herakles and William hunt sphinxes for vis, and one might be a Merinita's familiar. If she drinks the sacred water she can have Apollo Didyma's visions.

creatures.name: Agamenoth
creatures.weakness: Abhors water: it does him no harm, but he must flee it or spend a Confidence Point to stay by it for a diameter

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes physical form (RoP: The Infernal p. 31), a giant earth elemental or a coal seam.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: Appears in dreams (RoP: The Infernal p. 32).

powers.name: Lord of Moving Earth
powers.description: Duplicates any named non-ritual Creo, Muto or Rego Terram spell of ArM5, at a Might Cost of its magnitude.

powers.name: Move Through Earth
powers.description: Constant. Moves through earth or stone unhindered.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Whoever sins near him may gain Fury +1 (RoP: The Infernal p. 31). On any botch roll extra botch dice equal to the trait; a botch on them is a furious rage (ArM5 p. 54).

powers.name: Recalcitrance
powers.description: Against any Rego effect or ward, of any realm, his Might counts as 60. Printed with no Init.

powers.name: Stir the Sulfurous Earth
powers.description: An earthquake a mile across, stinking of sulphur, lasting a simple die of rounds. Each round those in it roll Dexterity + Athletics against 6 to stay standing. Stone buildings make one stress roll against the rounds of shaking, +3 if over two storeys, or fall, for +15 damage inside. It is felt 300 miles off. He must penetrate the area's Magic Resistance, so an Aegis normally protects a site.

creatures.appearance: A gigantic black mound of earth and rock, leaking sulphur from its cracks and forming limbs and heads as it needs, or a pitch black seam of coal several hundred paces wide and long.
creatures.notes: Prince of the Moving Earth.
creatures.secrets: He brought down the church and monastery at Didyma, and has since slept as coal under the plain, but the fall of Constantinople woke him, and when he is fully roused his earthquakes will strike Didyma and Miletos.

enchanted_devices.name: Vermin Wards
enchanted_devices.description: Three fist-sized stones carved with rats, at the Miletos warehouses. Printed Re(In)An 29. 36 Build Points.

effects.name: Vermin Ward
effects.description: Keeps animals of less than Size -1 out of a Structure.

enchanted_devices.name: Wards Against Rot
enchanted_devices.description: Three carved stone irises at the Miletos warehouses. Printed PeAq 34. 42 Build Points.

effects.name: Ward Against Rot
effects.description: Stops stored goods rotting.

enchanted_devices.name: Pestilence Wards
enchanted_devices.description: Three, at the Miletos warehouses. Printed ReVi 34, Pen +12. 42 Build Points.

effects.name: Pestilence Ward
effects.description: Bars minor demons of Might 10 or less from the Structure.

enchanted_devices.name: Warning Flame
enchanted_devices.description: A wand that lights a brazier at the end of the Sacred Way, just outside the Aegis, in an emergency in Miletos; covenfolk then find a magus, usually Ariane, who can reach Callista by Intangible Tunnel. Carried by Callista at Miletos. Printed CrIg 10. 4 Build Points.

effects.name: Warning Flame
effects.description: Lights the brazier.

enchanted_devices.name: Bath Rock
enchanted_devices.description: Heats the western baths. Printed CrIg 19. 8 Build Points.

effects.name: Bath Rock
effects.description: Heats the water of the baths.

enchanted_devices.name: The Oracle's Dredge
enchanted_devices.description: A pole about 20 feet long with a scoop on one end. Covenfolk paddle round the Lion Harbour with it each month, or the Meander's silt shows within a season and closes the harbour within a decade; city and merchants know of it. Printed PeTe 15. 6 Build Points.

effects.name: Destroy the Silt
effects.description: Destroys about 10 cubic paces of mud it touches.

enchanted_devices.name: Porter's Helpers
enchanted_devices.description: Six handles at the Miletos warehouses. Printed ReTe 15. 36 Build Points.

effects.name: Porter's Helper
effects.description: Clamped to a heavy object, lets the user move it as with +5 Strength.

enchanted_devices.name: Defender Swords
enchanted_devices.description: Ten, five usually with the warehouse garrison. Printed ReTe 20. 80 Build Points. No Concentration roll for watching melee blows, but one to do anything else, and against 15 to attack while concentrating.

effects.name: Defend
effects.description: Automatically parries any number of metal weapons the wielder knows are coming, so not a stab in the back.

enchanted_devices.name: Zeus' Arm
enchanted_devices.description: A wooden crane with a 50-square-foot platform that lifts up to 100 tons into and out of the hollow. Printed ReTe 30. 12 Build Points.

effects.name: Lift
effects.description: Lifts what rests on its platform.

enchanted_devices.name: The Spice Wand
enchanted_devices.description: Used on the Arab spice market. Printed InVi 12. 6 Build Points.

effects.name: Vibrate at Vis
effects.description: Trembles slightly if it touches vis.

enchanted_devices.name: Vis Divining Rods
enchanted_devices.description: A pair of silver rods held out like a dowser's. Printed InVi 20. 8 Build Points.

effects.name: Hear the Vis
effects.description: The user hears when within 30 paces of vis; Perception + Finesse against 6 finds it to within a foot.

enchanted_devices.name: Diamond of Hermes
enchanted_devices.description: Nikola made it for her work as a tutor, and lends it to Alexandria's Redcaps to check rumours of Gifted children. Printed InVi 25. 10 Build Points.

effects.name: Glow at the Gift
effects.description: Glows bright when touched by a Gifted person.

enchanted_devices.name: The Vis Net
enchanted_devices.description: Printed ReVi 20. 8 Build Points.

effects.name: Gather Vis
effects.description: Cast into water with vis in it, gathers it as slimy, pulsing fist-sized crystals of 1 pawn each.

enchanted_devices.name: Staff of the Branchidae
enchanted_devices.description: Alexander's talisman: a seven-foot wiry hornbeam staff, said to be a branch of a tree Branchos planted over two thousand years ago. 15 spaces used. Attunements: +6 Vim against hostile magic, +4 control at a distance, +4 destroy at a distance, +3 project a bolt or missile. The snake of its Sticks to Snakes is Size -4, Soak +2, fangs Init +3, Attack +11, Defense +10, Damage -7, poison Ease Factor 6, Light Wound (ArM5 p. 180); as the talisman in Grasping the Snake it has Alexander's Form Magic Resistance. 54 Build Points.

effects.name: Tongue of Beasts
effects.description: Lets the caster speak fluently with any animal.

effects.name: Sticks to Snakes
effects.description: Turns a stick into a writhing snake.

effects.name: Grasping the Snake
effects.description: Turns the talisman itself into the snake.

effects.name: Swarming Bolts of Earth
effects.description: Ten crystal spears rise from the ground to impale the targets, +10 damage each.

enchanted_devices.name: Soteria's Hand
enchanted_devices.description: Nikola's talisman: the lead-plated skeletal hand of the first Hermetic Branchidae, which she dug up many years ago. 6 spaces used. Attunements: +4 destroy the human body, +4 wards. 22 Build Points.

effects.name: The Wound that Weeps
effects.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 133), with no Penetration, for frightening mundanes.

effects.name: Exorcise the Cursed Room
effects.description: Demons in the Room lose 5 Might.

enchanted_devices.name: The Strategos' Sword
enchanted_devices.description: A long sword of office made by Orion almost 200 years ago. 12 spaces used. 46 Build Points.

effects.name: Ward Against Men
effects.description: Wards the target against people; Nikola must lower her Parma a moment to use it on herself.

effects.name: Arms Multiplied
effects.description: Makes 10 copies of the sword, plain and fit for mundane use, but little use against supernatural foes.

effects.name: Demon Bane
effects.description: Does 15 Might damage to a demon.

enchanted_devices.name: William's Crusade Armor
enchanted_devices.description: William's talisman: an iron eagle welded to a steel breastplate. Only the eagle is enchanted, but it has armour's shape bonuses (ArM5 p. 97). 8 spaces used. Attunements: +7 protect the wearer, +7 repel faeries. 26 Build Points.

effects.name: The Light Pours Out of Me
effects.description: Harmless, brilliant light streams from the armor.

effects.name: Iron Ward
effects.description: Wards against faeries of Might 15 or less.

effects.name: Endurance of the Berserkers
effects.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 134), at Diameter.

enchanted_devices.name: The Helm of Zotikos
enchanted_devices.description: A bronze helm Nicodemus made for his goblin servant, Philip's grandfather, and Philip's by inheritance. 4 spaces used. 16 Build Points.

effects.name: Death Speaker
effects.description: Looking into a corpse's eyes, the wearer speaks to its spirit, much like Whispers Through the Black Gate.

effects.name: Shriek of the Impending Shafts
effects.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 136).

enchanted_devices.name: Morpheus Arrows
enchanted_devices.description: Three arrows. 18 Build Points.

effects.name: Morpheus Arrow
effects.description: Whoever is hit, with his group, falls into a deep sleep.

enchanted_devices.name: Fire Arrows
enchanted_devices.description: Five arrows. 10 Build Points.

effects.name: Fire Arrow
effects.description: Bursts into flame on impact, +5 damage beside the arrow's own, and sets alight what it hits, +5 a round until put out.

enchanted_devices.name: Bridging Arrows
enchanted_devices.description: Two arrows. 12 Build Points.

effects.name: Bridging Arrow
effects.description: Shot, makes a pace-wide bridge of twisted wood from bow to arrowfall, up to 100 paces, for up to Size +4.

changes.name: Catella
changes.was:
The only Gifted member of Alexandria, who looks thirty-nine. She came straight from her Gauntlet, two years before Constantinople fell, while the covenant's name was still good, drawn by Alexander's artifacts; in some twenty years of study she has got little further with them.

Because of that interest she was made keeper of the artifacts and their loans, which both thrills and galls her: she loves having charge of them but hates that they are often out when she wants to study them. Alexandria has chosen to lend them freely, and she abides by it even when it upsets her own plans. She has no Mechanica yet, so cannot mend the glass submarine. She would also dearly like Hagia Sophia in Constantinople studied for insights from Heron's theories, and will fund any magus with a way to do it.
changes.value:
The only Gifted member of Alexandria, who looks thirty-nine. She trained in Constantinople and left around the time of the siege, while the covenant's name was still good, drawn by Alexander's artifacts; in some twenty years of study she has got little further with them.

Because of that interest she was made keeper of the artifacts and their loans, which both thrills and galls her: she loves having charge of them but hates that they are often out when she wants to study them. Alexandria has chosen to lend them freely, and she abides by it even when it upsets her own plans. She has no Mechanica yet, so cannot mend the glass submarine. She would also dearly like Hagia Sophia in Constantinople studied for insights from Heron's theories, and will fund any magus with a way to do it.

changes.name: Thrakesion
changes.was: Nicaea's southernmost theme, Thrakesion, running from Lydia to the Maeander and its fertile basin: the old Ionia and Caria, once thick with towns and ports along the Aegean. Centuries of war with the Turks have drawn its people into walled cities, Philadelphia the chief. The Maeander has been Nicaea's southern frontier since 1211, when Theodore Laskaris beat Kaykhusraw I of Rum at Antioch-on-the-Maeander.
changes.value:
Nicaea's southernmost theme, Thrakesion, running from Lydia to the Maeander and its fertile basin: the old Ionia and Caria, once thick with towns and ports along the Aegean. Centuries of war with the Turks have drawn its people into walled cities, Philadelphia the chief. The Maeander has been Nicaea's southern frontier since 1211, when Theodore Laskaris beat Kaykhusraw I of Rum at Antioch-on-the-Maeander.

Miletos, south of the Maeander's mouth, still lies inside Nicaea, in its extreme south-west.
